For a pair such as English and French, there are hundreds of millions of such pairs, drawn from parliamentary records, international organisations, subtitles and websites. For many languages of Pakistan, the supply is tiny. Much everyday Saraiki or Balochi is spoken rather than written, much of what is written never reaches the internet, and spelling can vary from writer to writer.

Researchers have tried several ways around the shortage. One is to train a single system on many languages at once, so that what it learns from a well-resourced language can partly carry over to a related one with fewer examples; a system that knows Urdu and Punjabi well may make better guesses about Saraiki. Another is to create data directly by paying or inviting speakers to translate a set of sentences. This is slow and expensive, and its quality depends heavily on careful checking, but it produces exactly the kind of material the systems need.

The question is not only technical. A language that is absent from digital tools becomes a little harder to use in school, government and commerce, and its younger speakers may come to feel that serious matters belong in other languages. Some linguists therefore argue that communities should lead such projects, choosing which texts are translated and how their language is written, rather than simply supplying raw material for outside companies. Whose data it is, they suggest, matters as much as how much of it there is.

rc-s041.x:
Ask a child in Gilgit why the sky is blue and you may be told that it reflects the sea. The explanation is charming but wrong; the sky over the mountains, hundreds of kilometres from any coast, is often bluer than the sky over Karachi. The real answer, worked out by physicists in the nineteenth century and associated above all with Lord Rayleigh, has to do with how sunlight interacts with the air itself.

Sunlight looks white but contains all the colours of the rainbow, each corresponding to a different wavelength. As it passes through the atmosphere, some of it strikes molecules of nitrogen and oxygen, which are far smaller than the wavelength of visible light. Such tiny particles scatter light in all directions, and they scatter short wavelengths much more strongly than long ones: blue light is scattered several times more than red. Wherever we look in the daytime sky, away from the sun itself, we see this scattered light arriving from every direction, and it is dominated by blue.

A careful reader may object that violet light has an even shorter wavelength than blue and should therefore dominate. Part of the answer is that sunlight contains less violet than blue to begin with, and part lies in our eyes, which are more sensitive to blue. The sky's colour is thus partly a fact about physics and partly a fact about human vision.

The same principle explains sunsets. When the sun is low, its light must travel through far more air to reach us. Along that long path most of the blue is scattered away to the sides, and what arrives directly is the remaining orange and red. Clouds, by contrast, are made of water droplets much larger than air molecules. Large particles scatter all colours roughly equally, which is why clouds look white or grey. The same is true of the fine dust and smoke that hang over cities in winter, turning a blue sky into a pale and milky one.

rc-s042.x:
Few roads have outlived as many empires as the one that runs across the north of the subcontinent from Bengal to the Khyber. Long before it had its modern name, a great route linked the Gangetic plain with the north-west, carrying soldiers, pilgrims and merchants; ancient texts and inscriptions point to its importance more than two thousand years ago. But the road as later generations knew it owes most to a ruler whose reign was remarkably short.

Sher Shah Suri held power in north India for only about five years in the 1540s, between two periods of Mughal rule. In that time he rebuilt and extended the old route and, more importantly, organised it. At regular intervals along it he had sarais built, walled rest houses where travellers could find shelter, water and food, often with separate quarters for Hindus and Muslims. Wells were dug and trees planted to shade the way. Horses were kept ready at the sarais so that messengers could ride from one to the next, carrying news and orders across the empire far faster than before.

The motive was not only generosity. A ruler who could move troops and information quickly could collect revenue, put down rebellion and keep distant governors honest. The sarais also became small market towns, and some later grew into permanent settlements. In this sense the road was an instrument of government as much as a convenience for travellers.

The Mughals who returned to power maintained much of Sher Shah's system, and in the nineteenth century the British paved and straightened long stretches, giving it the name by which it is known today, the Grand Trunk Road. Modern highways in Pakistan, India and Bangladesh still follow parts of its course. Travellers on them seldom think about the short-lived ruler who shaped it, yet the habit of measuring a journey by the distance between rest stops is, in a way, his legacy.

rc-s043.x:
Pakistan grows very little of the tea it drinks, and it drinks a great deal. Almost all of it is imported, much of it from Kenya, and is paid for in foreign currency. This simple fact links the price of a cup at a roadside dhaba to events far away: the size of the Kenyan harvest, the cost of shipping across the Arabian Sea and, above all, the value of the rupee.

When the rupee loses value against the dollar, an importer must pay more rupees for the same chest of tea. Economists call the share of that extra cost that reaches shop prices the pass-through. For tea, pass-through tends to be high, for a reason that has little to do with tea and much to do with habit. Demand for a product is called inelastic when people keep buying roughly the same amount even as its price rises. Tea in Pakistan is close to that case: households may grumble, but few give up their morning cup, so sellers can raise prices without losing many customers.

That does not mean consumers do nothing. Faced with higher prices, families tend to switch rather than stop. They move from branded packets to cheaper loose leaf, buy smaller packs more often, or brew the same leaves a little longer. Small sellers adjust too, sometimes keeping the price of a cup fixed while making it slightly smaller. These changes rarely show up as falling sales in national figures, but they are real, and they fall hardest on poorer households, for whom tea is a larger share of spending.

Policy makers face an awkward trade-off. Cutting import duties on tea can cushion consumers but reduces government revenue at the moment it may be most needed. Encouraging local cultivation, which has been tried on a small scale in the hills of the north, could reduce dependence on imports, but tea bushes take years to mature and need particular soils and rainfall. There is no quick way to make a nation's favourite drink immune to the exchange rate.

rc-s044.x:
A qawwali performance rarely begins at full strength. At first there is only the harmonium, feeling its way through a melody, and perhaps a few quiet beats on the tabla. Then the lead singer offers a line of verse, the chorus answers, and the clapping begins. Over the next half hour, sometimes much longer, the music climbs: the tempo quickens, phrases are repeated with growing force, and the singers seem to press the same few words harder and harder until they open into something new.

Qawwali grew up in the Sufi shrines of South Asia, and tradition credits its shaping to the poet and musician Amir Khusrau, who lived in Delhi around the turn of the fourteenth century. Its purpose was devotional. The poetry, in Persian, Urdu, Punjabi and other languages, speaks of longing for the divine, often in the language of earthly love, and the music was meant to carry listeners toward a state of spiritual absorption. The harmonium, now so central, is a comparatively recent arrival, brought to the subcontinent from Europe in the nineteenth century.

What strikes many first-time listeners is how much of a performance is not fixed in advance. A skilled lead singer watches the audience closely. If a line moves them, he may repeat it many times, varying the melody with each return. He may weave in a couplet from a different poem that comments on the main text, a technique known as girah, linking the two in a way the listeners are expected to recognise and enjoy. The same song may last ten minutes one evening and forty the next.

When Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan carried qawwali to concert halls around the world in the 1980s and 1990s, some purists worried that removing it from the shrine would empty it of meaning. Others answered that the form had always adapted to its listeners. Both sides agreed on one point: qawwali is less a fixed composition than a conversation between singer and audience.

rc-s045.x:
For years, pictures of plastic pollution came mostly from the open ocean: floating bags, turtles tangled in netting, great swirling patches of debris far from land. Yet most of that plastic did not begin its journey at sea. It was dropped, dumped or washed off the land, and a large share of it travelled to the coast by river.

Estimating how much plastic rivers carry has proved surprisingly hard. An influential estimate published in 2017 suggested that a handful of large rivers in Asia and Africa, the Indus among them, delivered most of the plastic reaching the oceans. Later work using more detailed models reached a different conclusion: the load seemed to be spread across a thousand or more rivers, many of them short streams flowing through crowded coastal cities. A small urban river that passes through dense neighbourhoods with weak waste collection, close to the sea, may release more plastic than a great river whose waste is trapped along hundreds of kilometres of banks and reservoirs.

The difference matters for action. If a few giant rivers were responsible, a few large clean-up projects might make a dent. If the problem is spread across many small streams, solutions must be local and numerous: regular collection of household waste, barriers at the mouths of urban drains, and the cleaning of channels before the monsoon flushes them out. In Karachi, for example, the rains that clear clogged nullahs can also send months of accumulated waste into the sea in a few days.

Plastic does not stay in large pieces. Sunlight and abrasion break it into fragments, and eventually into microplastics too small to collect, which are now found in river sediments, fish and even drinking water. Once at this stage, it is effectively impossible to remove. For that reason, many researchers argue that the cheapest place to deal with river plastic is not the ocean, nor even the river, but the street.

rc-s046.x:
Dr Mahnoor had been warned about her first night on call at the district hospital, but the warnings had been about the wrong things. She had expected blood and noise. Instead, for the first two hours, there was only the hum of the ceiling fans and a nurse named Shakeela knitting at the end of the corridor, a ball of red wool in her lap.

The first patient arrived at eleven: a farmer from a village forty minutes away, brought on the back of a motorbike by his son, his breath short and his hands cold. Mahnoor knew what to do. She had done it in textbooks and on practice dummies a hundred times. Yet when she reached for her stethoscope, she found she could not remember which pocket she had put it in, and for a long, terrible second she stood patting her coat while the son watched her face.

Shakeela had already put down her knitting. Without a word she handed Mahnoor the stethoscope, which had been lying on the desk, and began unbuttoning the farmer's shirt. They worked for an hour. Mahnoor gave instructions; Shakeela carried them out, occasionally saying, "Doctor, shall I also...?" and naming the very thing Mahnoor had been about to forget. By one o'clock the farmer was breathing more easily and his son had fallen asleep on a bench.

Later, when the ward was quiet again, Mahnoor tried to thank her. Shakeela waved the thanks away and picked up the red wool. "Thirty years," she said, counting stitches. "I have seen many first nights. The good doctors are the ones who listen on the second night too."

Mahnoor sat at the desk and wrote up her notes slowly, in her neatest hand. Outside, the fans turned and the corridor lights buzzed. She found, to her surprise, that she was no longer afraid of the morning, only of becoming the kind of doctor who would forget what this night had taught her.

questions.s:
Researchers at a Karachi marine institute report that the coral reef has ______ sharply over a decade: where divers once counted dozens of fish species, they now find only a handful.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: flourished
expanded
stabilised
declined
questions.e: A fall from dozens of species to a handful is a decline. "Flourished" and "expanded" describe the opposite change, and "stabilised" means the reef stopped changing, which the sharp drop rules out.

questions.s:
The novelist is known for her ______ style; she rarely writes a sentence longer than ten words and avoids decoration of any kind.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: concise
elaborate
ornate
rambling
questions.e: Short sentences with no decoration describe a concise style. "Elaborate", "ornate" and "rambling" all suggest length or ornament, the very things the text says she avoids.

questions.s:
Although the committee's report was meant to settle the dispute, its conclusions were so ______ that both sides claimed it supported their position.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: decisive
persuasive
ambiguous
detailed
questions.e: If both opposing sides can read the report as support, its conclusions must be open to more than one reading, that is, ambiguous. A "decisive" report would have settled the dispute, and "detailed" or "persuasive" conclusions do not explain why each side found its own view in them.

questions.s:
Early critics dismissed the architect's glass-and-steel designs as a passing fashion, but within twenty years the style had become so ______ that it appeared in almost every major city.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: obscure
pervasive
fragile
controversial
questions.e: Appearing in almost every major city means the style had spread everywhere, which is what "pervasive" means. "Obscure" says the reverse, and "controversial" describes opinion about the style rather than how widely it spread.

questions.s:
The historian cautions that the merchant's diary, written decades after the events it describes, should not be treated as a fully ______ record of the 1890s trade in Peshawar.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: lengthy
personal
recent
reliable
questions.e: Writing decades later raises doubts about memory, so the caution is about how far the diary can be trusted: it may not be fully reliable. A diary is personal by nature, so "personal" gives no reason for caution, and "recent" contradicts the gap the text describes.

questions.s:
Bilal's experiment failed to ______ the earlier result: when he repeated the procedure exactly, his plants grew no faster than the control group.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: publish
contradict
predict
replicate
questions.e: Repeating a procedure and not getting the same result is a failure to replicate it. "Contradict" is tempting, but Bilal's result did contradict the earlier one, so saying he "failed to contradict" it reverses the meaning.

questions.s:
The new traffic plan was intended to ______ congestion on Lahore's Canal Road, yet commuters report that their journeys now take longer than before.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: worsen
alleviate
measure
ignore
questions.e: "Yet" signals that the outcome (longer journeys) went against the intention, so the plan was meant to ease, or alleviate, congestion. "Worsen" would make the outcome match the intention, removing the contrast.

questions.s:
Far from being ______, the scientist's claim that some bacteria can survive in near-boiling water was confirmed by several independent laboratories within a year.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: verified
celebrated
modest
spurious
questions.e: "Far from being" sets up a contrast with being confirmed, so the blank needs a word meaning false or not genuine: "spurious". "Verified" means the same as confirmed and so destroys the contrast.

questions.s:
The mayor's speech was meant to reassure residents, but her refusal to answer questions about the water supply only ______ their suspicion that the problem was serious.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: dispelled
concealed
questioned
reinforced
questions.e: "But" and "only" show that the speech had the opposite of its intended effect, so the refusal strengthened, or reinforced, the residents' suspicion. "Dispelled" would mean the speech succeeded in reassuring them.

questions.s:
The museum's new gallery is fully ______ to visitors who use wheelchairs: every exhibit can be reached by ramp or lift.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: accessible
hostile
unknown
indifferent
questions.e: Ramps and lifts to every exhibit make the gallery accessible, meaning easy to reach and use. "Hostile" and "indifferent" describe attitudes that the ramps and lifts contradict.

questions.s:
Unlike her predecessor, who announced decisions without consulting anyone, the new principal took a ______ approach, inviting teachers and students to help shape school policy.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: authoritarian
collaborative
cautious
secretive
questions.e: Inviting others to shape policy is working together, a collaborative approach, and "unlike" confirms it differs from deciding alone. "Authoritarian" describes the predecessor, not the new principal.

questions.s:
The economist argues that the fall in onion prices was ______ rather than permanent, a brief effect of an unusually large harvest that would vanish the following season.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: structural
transient
deliberate
inevitable
questions.e: A brief effect contrasted with "permanent" is transient, meaning short-lived. "Structural" suggests a deep, lasting cause, which is close to the "permanent" the economist rejects.

questions.s:
Ayesha's account of the trip was so "vivid" that her listeners felt they had walked the streets of Gilgit themselves.

As used in the text, what does the word "vivid" most nearly mean?
o: loud and excited
long and rambling
clear and lifelike
brightly coloured
questions.e: Listeners felt they had been there, so the account created clear, lifelike pictures in their minds. "Brightly coloured" is a literal sense of vivid that fits paint or cloth, not a spoken account.

questions.s:
After weeks of heavy rain, the farmers were ______ to see the sun return, since their wheat could finally be harvested.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: alarmed
reluctant
puzzled
relieved
questions.e: The sun ended a worry and let the harvest go ahead, so the farmers were relieved. "Alarmed" and "reluctant" suggest the return of the sun was unwelcome, which the reason given contradicts.

questions.s:
The documentary does not take sides; it ______ the arguments of both supporters and opponents of the dam with equal care.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: presents
dismisses
exaggerates
conceals
questions.e: A film that takes no side sets out each side's arguments fairly, so it presents them. "Dismisses" or "conceals" would mean it treats the arguments unfairly, which clashes with "equal care".

questions.s:
The study's sample of only twelve students was too small to ______ the researchers' sweeping conclusions about all university students in Pakistan.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: justify
contradict
inspire
summarise
questions.e: The complaint is that twelve students are not enough evidence to support broad claims, so the sample is too small to justify them. "Contradict" is wrong because the problem is weak support, not opposing evidence.

questions.s:
The poet's later work is marked by a ______ tone; the playful humour of her early collections gives way to quiet reflections on loss and memory.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: whimsical
triumphant
sarcastic
sombre
questions.e: Quiet reflections on loss replacing playful humour point to a serious, sad, sombre tone. "Whimsical" describes the playful early work, the very quality the text says disappears.

questions.s:
To reduce waste, the café now ______ customers who bring their own cups by giving them a small discount.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: punishes
ignores
rewards
warns
questions.e: A discount is a benefit, so the café rewards these customers. "Punishes" and "warns" describe negative treatment, which a discount is not.

questions.s:
The engineer's design was remarkably ______: it used fewer parts than any rival model yet performed every task the brief required.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: extravagant
efficient
fragile
conventional
questions.e: Doing every required task with fewer parts than rivals is achieving more with less, which is efficiency. "Extravagant" means wasteful, the opposite of using fewer parts.

questions.s:
Though the two languages share many words, linguists consider their grammars ______; a sentence built by the rules of one is often meaningless in the other.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: identical
simple
flexible
incompatible
questions.e: "Though" contrasts the shared words with grammars that do not fit together, and a sentence that fails in the other language shows the rules are incompatible. "Identical" would mean the sentence works in both.

questions.s:
The minister's statement was carefully ______: it neither confirmed nor denied that talks had taken place, leaving reporters with nothing definite to print.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: candid
noncommittal
emphatic
provocative
questions.e: Neither confirming nor denying is avoiding a clear position, which is noncommittal. "Candid" and "emphatic" would give reporters something definite, the opposite of what happened.

questions.s:
The students had to "abandon" their plan to camp beside the lake when a storm was forecast.

As used in the text, what does the word "abandon" most nearly mean?
o: describe
delay
improve
give up
questions.e: A storm forced the students to drop the plan altogether, so abandon means give up. "Delay" is tempting, but it means putting the plan off, not giving it up.

questions.s:
Seeds found in a dry cave were still ______ after two thousand years; when planted, several of them sprouted.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: visible
fossilised
viable
valuable
questions.e: Seeds that sprout when planted are capable of growing, which is what viable means. "Fossilised" seeds have turned to stone and could not sprout.

questions.s:
The company's profits rose steadily, but critics noted that this success ______ its poor record on workers' safety, which had drawn little public attention.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: exposed
improved
obscured
explained
questions.e: The safety record drew little attention because the success hid it from view, so the success obscured it. "Exposed" means the opposite, and nothing suggests the success "improved" safety.

questions.s:
The guide asked the group to remain ______ inside the cave so that the bats roosting above them would not be disturbed.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: quiet
lively
scattered
curious
questions.e: Not disturbing roosting bats calls for silence, so the group must stay quiet. "Lively" behaviour is exactly what would disturb the bats.

questions.s:
Researchers had assumed the two bird populations were separate, but genetic tests revealed that they ______ regularly, sharing genes across the mountain range.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: compete
hibernate
interbreed
nest
questions.e: Sharing genes means birds from the two groups mate and produce offspring, so they interbreed. "Compete" shows contact between the groups but no exchange of genes.

questions.s:
Critics praised the translator for her ______: she captured not only the literal meaning of the Urdu verses but also their rhythm and their humour.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: brevity
fidelity
originality
ambiguity
questions.e: Keeping the meaning, rhythm and humour of the original is faithfulness to it, or fidelity. "Originality" is tempting as praise, but a translator who adds her own ideas departs from the source rather than capturing it.

questions.s:
The price of solar panels has fallen so far that installing them is now ______ for many middle-income households, not just wealthy ones.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: compulsory
unthinkable
affordable
fashionable
questions.e: A falling price brings panels within reach of households with less money, so they are affordable. "Unthinkable" says the reverse, and "compulsory" is about rules, not price.

questions.s:
The heavy fines are meant to ______ the practice of dumping factory waste into the river.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: promote
reward
curb
permit
questions.e: Fines punish an activity in order to reduce it, so they are meant to curb dumping. "Promote", "reward" and "permit" all encourage or allow the practice, the opposite of a fine's purpose.

questions.s:
The archive's catalogue is ______ at best: many boxes are labelled only with a year, and some carry no label at all.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: exhaustive
meticulous
redundant
rudimentary
questions.e: Labels with only a year, or none, show a basic, undeveloped catalogue, which is rudimentary. "Exhaustive" and "meticulous" describe thorough work, the opposite of these sparse labels.

questions.s:
The new chemistry textbook is praised for its ______ explanations, which beginners can follow without a teacher's help.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: lucid
confusing
outdated
technical
questions.e: Explanations that beginners can follow alone are clear, which is what lucid means. "Technical" explanations would be harder for beginners, not easier.

questions.s:
Apricot growers in Hunza ______ their fruit in the sun on flat rooftops, a method that preserves it through the long winter.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: freeze
sell
dry
plant
questions.e: Spreading fruit in the sun to preserve it is drying it. "Freeze" also preserves food, but sunshine on a rooftop cannot freeze anything.

questions.s:
The judge ruled that the letter was ______ to the case, since it had been written years before the contract in dispute existed.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: essential
damaging
original
irrelevant
questions.e: A letter written before the contract existed cannot bear on a dispute about it, so it is irrelevant. "Essential" and "damaging" both assume the letter matters to the case, which the reason given denies.

questions.s:
The architect wanted the library to feel ______, so she used tall windows and pale walls that make even small reading rooms seem large and open.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: cramped
spacious
ancient
formal
questions.e: Making small rooms seem large and open creates a spacious feeling. "Cramped" is the feeling the windows and pale walls are meant to prevent.

questions.s:
The scientist was ______ about her findings, stressing that a single trial could not establish that the new drug was effective.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: jubilant
dismissive
circumspect
indifferent
questions.e: Warning that one trial proves little is being careful not to claim too much, which is circumspect. "Dismissive" goes too far: she does not reject her findings, she only limits what they show.

questions.s:
The team's initial results were "promising", but further tests were needed before the method could be adopted in hospitals.

As used in the text, what does the word "promising" most nearly mean?
o: encouraging
guaranteed
pledged
complete
questions.e: Results that justify further tests show signs of future success, so promising means encouraging. "Pledged" draws on the verb "promise" (to give one's word), which results cannot do.

questions.s:
The town's population ______ after the new factory opened, as hundreds of families moved there for work.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: fell
aged
grew
left
questions.e: Hundreds of families arriving makes the population larger, so it grew. "Fell" describes the reverse of families moving in.

questions.s:
The festival's organisers hoped to ______ interest in traditional crafts among young people, many of whom had never seen a loom at work.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: suppress
revive
measure
exhaust
questions.e: Organisers showing old crafts to young people want to bring interest back to life, or revive it. "Measure" is neutral, and a festival is not held simply to measure interest.

questions.s:
Although the study was widely reported as proof that coffee improves memory, its authors were careful to note that their findings were merely ______.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: preliminary
conclusive
fabricated
irrelevant
questions.e: "Although" contrasts the reports of proof with the authors' caution, and "merely" points to early, not-yet-final results: preliminary. "Conclusive" agrees with the reports instead of contrasting with them, and no author would call their own results "fabricated".

questions.s:
The essay's argument is ______: each paragraph builds on the last, and the conclusion follows inevitably from the evidence presented.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: tenuous
repetitive
cogent
derivative
questions.e: An argument whose conclusion follows inevitably from its evidence is convincing and well reasoned, or cogent. "Tenuous" means weak, and "repetitive" fails because each paragraph adds to the last.

questions.s:
Because the instructions were written in such ______ language, many users could not work out how to install the software.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: simple
confusing
friendly
polite
questions.e: Users failed to understand the instructions, so the language must have been confusing. "Simple" language would have helped them succeed.

questions.s:
The two scientists ______ about the cause of the fish deaths: one blamed a chemical spill, the other a sudden rise in water temperature.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: agreed
reported
disagreed
relied
questions.e: Each scientist gives a different cause, so they disagreed. "Reported" is too neutral: it ignores the conflict between the two explanations that the colon introduces.

questions.s:
Many of the village's oldest songs were never written down; they were ______ orally from parents to children over centuries.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: invented
forbidden
transmitted
translated
questions.e: Passing songs by mouth from one generation to the next is transmitting them. "Invented" fails because the songs already existed and were being handed on.

questions.s:
Several board members later admitted that they had voted for the budget cut without reading the proposal, a ______ that critics said reflected wider carelessness.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: lapse
triumph
precaution
compromise
questions.e: Voting without reading is a failure of care, a lapse, and the critics' word "carelessness" confirms this. "Precaution" is the opposite: a careful step taken in advance.

questions.s:
Sana kept a ______ record of her spending, writing down every rupee she spent on food, books and transport.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: vague
detailed
careless
rough
questions.e: Noting every rupee makes the record detailed. "Vague" and "rough" describe a loose record, the opposite of one that lists every rupee.

questions.s:
The drought forced farmers to ______ water carefully, giving each field only what it needed to survive.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: waste
purify
sell
ration
questions.e: Giving each field only a limited, fixed amount is rationing. "Purify" is about cleaning water, not dividing a scarce supply.

questions.s:
The new evidence did not overturn the theory but ______ it, adding detail to a picture that scientists already broadly accepted.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: refuted
refined
ignored
replaced
questions.e: Adding detail to an accepted picture improves it in small ways, which is refining it. "Refuted" and "replaced" mean the same as overturn, which the text explicitly denies.

questions.s:
The writer's portrait of the city is anything but ______: she dwells on its traffic, its noise and its crumbling buildings as much as on its gardens.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: idealised
unflattering
realistic
critical
questions.e: Giving the bad features as much attention as the gardens means the portrait is not made to look perfect, so it is "anything but" idealised. "Unflattering" and "critical" fit the portrait itself, so "anything but" would make the sentence say the opposite of what the colon explains.

questions.s:
The heavy load began to "strain" the old rope, and the climbers worried that it might snap.

As used in the text, what does the word "strain" most nearly mean?
o: pull tight under pressure
pass liquid through
injure a muscle in
make anxious
questions.e: A rope that might snap is being stretched by force, so strain means pull tight under pressure. "Make anxious" fits the climbers' feelings, but it is the rope, not the climbers, that the load strains.

questions.s:
The company's new phone was widely ______ by reviewers, who complained that it was slower and more expensive than the model it replaced.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: criticised
celebrated
copied
recalled
questions.e: Reviewers who complained were finding fault, so the phone was criticised. "Celebrated" means praised, which clashes with the complaints.

questions.s:
Because the old map placed the village several kilometres from its true position, the surveyors considered it too ______ to use.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: detailed
valuable
recent
inaccurate
questions.e: A map that puts a village in the wrong place is inaccurate. "Detailed" and "valuable" are not reasons to reject a map, so "too" would make no sense with them.

questions.s:
The professor's lectures were notoriously ______, wandering from Mughal architecture to cricket to the price of tea before returning, eventually, to the topic of the day.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: focused
concise
digressive
rigorous
questions.e: Wandering away from the main topic before returning to it is digressing, so the lectures were digressive. "Focused" and "concise" describe the opposite habit of staying on the point.

questions.s:
The scientist ______ her hypothesis by running a careful experiment with a control group.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: tested
hid
forgot
guessed
questions.e: An experiment with a control group is a way of checking a hypothesis, so she tested it. "Guessed" fails because a hypothesis is already a proposed answer, and an experiment checks it rather than guesses it.

questions.s:
The ceasefire remained ______ for weeks; minor clashes along the border threatened to break it at any moment.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: permanent
popular
secret
fragile
questions.e: An agreement that could break at any moment is fragile. "Permanent" contradicts the threat that it might end at any time.

questions.s:
Rather than relying on a single supplier, the Lahore start-up chose to ______ its sources of cotton, buying from farms in three different provinces.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: restrict
conceal
diversify
inspect
questions.e: Buying from many farms instead of one widens the range of sources, which is diversifying. "Restrict" means narrowing them, the reverse of moving from one supplier to several.

questions.s:
The historian's account is ______ by her reliance on a single source, a letter whose author had every reason to exaggerate.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: undermined
strengthened
inspired
confirmed
questions.e: Depending on one biased letter weakens the account, so it is undermined. "Strengthened" and "confirmed" would need trustworthy, varied evidence, which the text says is missing.

questions.s:
After practising every evening for months, Hamza could play the difficult piece with ______.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: fear
anger
ease
doubt
questions.e: Months of practice make a hard piece feel easy, so he plays it with ease. "Fear" and "doubt" describe the nerves that practice is meant to remove.

questions.s:
The novel's ending is ______; readers cannot tell whether the narrator returns home or stays in the city forever.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: predictable
tragic
rushed
open-ended
questions.e: An ending that leaves the outcome undecided is open-ended. "Predictable" fails because readers cannot even tell what happens, let alone foresee it.

questions.s:
The council's survey found that residents were ______ about the proposed bus route: about half supported it, and half opposed it.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: divided
unanimous
enthusiastic
uninformed
questions.e: A half-and-half split means opinion was divided. "Unanimous" means everyone agreed, the opposite of an even split.

questions.s:
The bakery's bread is so ______ that customers queue outside before it opens each morning.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: stale
bland
heavy
popular
questions.e: Queues before opening time show that many people want the bread, so it is popular. "Stale" and "bland" are faults that would keep customers away.

questions.s:
The runner ______ her injured ankle by resting it for two weeks before the next race.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: damaged
protected
ignored
broke
questions.e: Resting an injury keeps it from getting worse, so she protected her ankle. "Ignored" fails because resting the ankle for two weeks is paying close attention to it.

questions.s:
The report's authors acknowledge one important ______: they surveyed only urban schools, so their findings may not apply to villages.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: limitation
achievement
coincidence
advantage
questions.e: Findings that may not apply to villages point to a weakness in the study's scope, a limitation. "Advantage" is the opposite, since surveying only cities narrows what the study can show.

questions.s:
The minister tried to "address" the crowd's concerns, but the microphone failed after a few words.

As used in the text, what does the word "address" most nearly mean?
o: write on an envelope
deal with
find the location of
make a formal speech to
questions.e: One addresses concerns by responding to them, so here the word means deal with. "Make a formal speech to" fits addressing a crowd, but the object here is the crowd's concerns, not the crowd.

questions.s:
The first settlers' houses were ______, built quickly from mud and reeds to last only until the harvest.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: permanent
makeshift
lavish
elaborate
questions.e: Houses put up quickly from mud and reeds to serve for a short time are makeshift. "Permanent" contradicts "only until the harvest", and "lavish" clashes with the simple materials.

questions.s:
Dentists advise people to ______ sugary drinks, which can damage teeth over time.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: increase
prefer
share
limit
questions.e: Because sugary drinks harm teeth, the advice is to cut down on them, or limit them. "Increase" and "prefer" would make the damage worse.

questions.s:
The economist argues that low interest rates ______ borrowing, because loans become cheaper for businesses and families.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: prevent
punish
stimulate
conceal
questions.e: Cheaper loans encourage people to borrow more, so low rates stimulate borrowing. "Prevent" reverses the cause and effect the text describes.

questions.s:
Scientists were ______ to find frogs living in the dry desert, since the animals usually need moist surroundings.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: bored
surprised
eager
relieved
questions.e: Finding frogs where they would not be expected is surprising, as "since the animals usually need moist surroundings" makes clear. "Relieved" would imply the scientists had been worried about something.

questions.s:
Far from being a ______ figure, the poet was at the centre of Lahore's literary life, hosting gatherings that drew writers from across the subcontinent.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: celebrated
marginal
influential
sociable
questions.e: "Far from" sets up a contrast with being "at the centre", so the blank needs a word meaning on the edge: "marginal". "Celebrated", "influential" and "sociable" all agree with the description and so remove the contrast.

questions.s:
Because the museum relied on donations rather than ticket sales, its budget ______ from year to year depending on the generosity of patrons.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: froze
vanished
doubled
fluctuated
questions.e: A budget that depends on changing generosity rises and falls, or fluctuates. "Doubled" names one steady direction, which does not fit "depending on the generosity of patrons".

questions.s:
The plant needs plenty of light, so Zara moved it to a "bright" window.

As used in the text, what does the word "bright" most nearly mean?
o: clever
cheerful
shiny
full of light
questions.e: A window chosen because the plant needs light is one full of light. "Clever" and "cheerful" are senses of bright that describe people, not windows.

questions.s:
The team's early prototype was ______: it worked in the laboratory but broke down whenever it was tested outdoors.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: unreliable
affordable
durable
elegant
questions.e: A machine that works in one setting but fails in another cannot be depended on, so it is unreliable. "Durable" means long-lasting, which repeated breakdowns contradict.

questions.s:
The judge's ruling set an important ______: courts in later cases followed the same reasoning.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: penalty
precedent
deadline
exception
questions.e: A decision that later courts follow is a precedent. "Exception" fails because an exception is not followed; it is set aside from the usual rule.

questions.s:
Critics found the film's message ______: its constant speeches about honesty left viewers feeling lectured rather than moved.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: understated
subtle
ambiguous
heavy-handed
questions.e: Constant speeches that make viewers feel lectured show a message delivered too forcefully, which is heavy-handed. "Understated" and "subtle" mean the opposite, and the message is too obvious to be "ambiguous".

questions.s:
The library will ______ its opening hours during exam season, staying open until midnight instead of closing at eight.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: reduce
cancel
extend
publish
questions.e: Closing at midnight instead of eight makes the hours longer, so the library will extend them. "Reduce" means making them shorter.

questions.s:
The study found a ______ between hours of sleep and exam scores: students who slept more tended to score higher, though the reason was unclear.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: contradiction
confusion
coincidence
correlation
questions.e: Two measures that tend to rise together, with the cause unknown, show a correlation. "Coincidence" suggests a chance match, but a pattern that holds across many students is a tendency, not a single accident.

questions.s:
The rescued manuscripts were so ______ that conservators had to handle each page with tweezers.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: brittle
sturdy
colourful
valuable
questions.e: Handling pages with tweezers suggests that they could easily crack or crumble, so they are brittle. "Valuable" may be true, but the tweezers point to fragile paper, not to its worth.

questions.s:
The reformer was ______ in her campaign for girls' education, pressing her case with officials for thirty years despite repeated refusals.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: hesitant
capricious
tenacious
complacent
questions.e: Keeping up a campaign for thirty years despite refusals shows determination, or tenacity. "Capricious" means changing one's mind on a whim, the opposite of such persistence.

questions.s:
The new road will ______ the journey from the village to the market town, cutting it from three hours to one.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: lengthen
shorten
block
describe
questions.e: Cutting three hours to one makes the journey shorter. "Lengthen" reverses the change the text describes.

questions.s:
The scientist's notebooks ______ her daily progress, recording every measurement and every failed attempt.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: exaggerate
conceal
document
predict
questions.e: Recording every measurement is keeping a written account, so the notebooks document her progress. "Conceal" clashes with recording even her failures.

questions.s:
The narrator's account is deliberately ______: she leaves out key events and jumps between years, forcing readers to piece together what really happened.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: chronological
exhaustive
fragmentary
objective
questions.e: An account with gaps that readers must piece together is broken into parts, or fragmentary. "Chronological" fails because jumping between years breaks time order, and "exhaustive" because key events are left out.

questions.s:
To ______ the spread of flu in the school, students who felt ill were asked to stay at home.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: speed up
prevent
study
allow
questions.e: Keeping ill students away stops them from passing on the flu, so the aim is to prevent its spread. "Speed up" and "allow" describe the opposite effect.

questions.s:
The start-up's founders were ______ about their chances: they had little money and no customers, yet they believed their idea would succeed.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: pessimistic
optimistic
uncertain
indifferent
questions.e: Believing in success despite poor circumstances is optimism, as the "yet" shows. "Pessimistic" fits the circumstances, but not the founders' belief that they would succeed.

questions.s:
The new law's effects on small traders were ______; most saw no change in sales, and the few who did reported only tiny differences.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: profound
disastrous
lasting
negligible
questions.e: No change for most traders and tiny changes for the rest make the effects too small to matter, or negligible. "Profound" and "disastrous" describe large effects the evidence does not show.

questions.s:
The scientist's theory did not "hold up" when it was checked against new data from the field.

As used in the text, what does the phrase "hold up" most nearly mean?
o: cause a delay
remain convincing
rob someone
raise into the air
questions.e: A theory that fails a test against new data stops being convincing, so hold up means remain valid. "Cause a delay" is a common sense of the phrase (traffic can hold you up), but it does not fit a theory being checked.

questions.s:
Days of heavy rain caused the river to ______ its banks, flooding the fields on both sides.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: dry
overflow
narrow
repair
questions.e: Water flooding the fields has spilled over the banks, so the river overflowed them. "Dry" and "narrow" describe a shrinking river, which could not flood fields.

questions.s:
The artist's early paintings were ______ of famous European works, but she soon developed a style entirely her own.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: criticisms
originals
collections
imitations
questions.e: "But" contrasts the early paintings with a style "entirely her own", so the early work must have copied others: imitations. "Originals" removes that contrast.

questions.s:
The government's ______ to reduce plastic use includes a ban on thin shopping bags and a tax on bottled water.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: refusal
strategy
accident
failure
questions.e: A planned set of measures aimed at a goal is a strategy. "Refusal" contradicts the steps the government is taking, and "accident" clashes with a deliberate ban and tax.

questions.s:
The historian's claims are ______, drawn from tax records, letters and court documents that all point to the same conclusion.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: speculative
anecdotal
corroborated
contested
questions.e: Several independent sources pointing to the same conclusion confirm the claims, so they are corroborated. "Anecdotal" means resting on informal stories, the opposite of varied official records.

questions.s:
Before testing them, the student ______ the rock samples into three groups by size.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: mixed
sorted
lost
painted
questions.e: Arranging samples into groups by size is sorting them. "Mixed" means combining them, the opposite of separating them into groups.

questions.s:
The two companies agreed to ______, combining their resources to build a single factory that neither could afford alone.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: cooperate
compete
withdraw
negotiate
questions.e: Pooling resources for a shared goal is cooperating. "Negotiate" is tempting, but the phrase after the comma describes what they agreed to do, which is to work together, not to bargain.

questions.s:
The library asks readers to ______ books within two weeks so that others can borrow them.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: copy
return
keep
sell
questions.e: Others can borrow a book only once it is brought back, so readers must return it. "Keep" would stop anyone else borrowing it.

questions.s:
In the trial, the new vaccine proved highly ______, preventing illness in nearly all the volunteers who received it.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: effective
harmful
untested
expensive
questions.e: A vaccine that prevents illness in nearly everyone works well, so it is effective. "Untested" contradicts the trial in which it was tested.

questions.s:
Rather than ______ the old fort, the city restored it carefully, keeping its original stone walls.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: demolish
preserve
visit
repair
questions.e: "Rather than" needs an action opposed to careful restoration, and knocking the fort down is that opposite: demolish. "Preserve" and "repair" describe what the city actually did, so they cannot be the rejected alternative.

questions.s:
The author's tone toward the scheme is ______: she describes its stated goals respectfully but notes, with evident amusement, that none of them was ever achieved.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: wry
reverent
furious
neutral
questions.e: Quiet amusement at a gap between promises and results is dry, ironic humour, a wry tone. "Neutral" fails because her evident amusement shows an attitude, and "reverent" ignores the mockery.

questions.s:
The sudden noise "startled" the birds, and they rose from the trees all at once.

As used in the text, what does the word "startled" most nearly mean?
o: gently woke
attracted
trained
suddenly frightened
questions.e: Birds taking off all at once at a sudden noise have been given a sudden fright. "Gently woke" fails because a sudden noise that sends birds flying is not gentle.

questions.s:
The researcher ______ that the river's decline began before the dam was built, pointing to fish counts from the 1950s that were already falling.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: contends
doubts
forgets
regrets
questions.e: Citing falling fish counts from before the dam is giving evidence for a claim, so she contends, or argues, that the decline began earlier. "Doubts" fails because the evidence she points to supports the claim rather than questioning it.

questions.s:
The scheme was ______ after only a year because it cost far more than it saved.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: discontinued
expanded
renewed
launched
questions.e: A scheme that loses money is likely to be stopped, so it was discontinued. "Expanded" and "renewed" mean continuing it, which the reason given argues against.

questions.s:
The market was so ______ on the eve of Eid that shoppers could barely move between the stalls.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: empty
quiet
crowded
distant
questions.e: Shoppers who can barely move are surrounded by many people, so the market was crowded. "Empty" and "quiet" describe the opposite scene.

questions.s:
The team ______ a new method for testing water quality that is cheaper and faster than the old one.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: abandoned
rejected
devised
banned
questions.e: Coming up with a new and better method is devising it. "Abandoned" and "rejected" make no sense for a method praised as cheaper and faster.

questions.s:
The economist's forecast proved ______: inflation rose almost exactly as she had predicted two years earlier.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: prescient
misguided
premature
arbitrary
questions.e: Correctly foreseeing events two years ahead is being prescient. "Premature" fails because the forecast was not too early; it was proved right.

questions.s:
The scientist's explanation was so ______ that even experts in her own field struggled to follow it.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: straightforward
brief
convoluted
persuasive
questions.e: An explanation that even experts struggle with is overly complicated, or convoluted. "Straightforward" and "brief" would make it easier to follow, not harder.

questions.s:
The old building was ______ after the earthquake, so engineers ordered everyone to leave.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: unsafe
modern
beautiful
empty
questions.e: Engineers order people out of a building that might collapse, so it was unsafe. "Empty" fails because the order to leave shows people were still inside.

questions.s:
The novelist's sympathies clearly "lie" with the villagers, whose struggles she describes with great warmth.

As used in the text, what does the word "lie" most nearly mean?
o: tell untruths
rest
lie down
remain hidden
questions.e: Sympathies that "lie with" someone rest or belong with them. "Tell untruths" is another meaning of lie, but it cannot apply to sympathies, and the warmth of her writing shows nothing is "hidden".

questions.s:
Because the people's early history was recorded only in songs, scholars must ______ the order of events from clues in the lyrics.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: observe
invent
ignore
infer
questions.e: Working out a sequence from clues is inferring it. "Invent" is tempting, but scholars using clues are reasoning from evidence, not making events up.

questions.s:
The reform was not a sudden break with the past but the ______ of changes that had been under way for decades.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: reversal
origin
abandonment
culmination
questions.e: The reform completed a long process, so it was the culmination, or high point, of those changes. "Origin" fails because changes already under way for decades cannot begin with the reform.

questions.s:
The teacher praised Usman's essay for its ______ argument, which was easy to follow from start to finish.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: clear
muddled
missing
hidden
questions.e: An argument easy to follow from start to finish is clear. "Muddled" is the opposite quality, one a teacher would not praise.

questions.s:
Archaeologists were able to ______ the age of the pottery by analysing charcoal found beside it.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: alter
conceal
increase
estimate
questions.e: Testing nearby charcoal gives a good approximate date, so they estimate the pottery's age. "Alter" and "increase" fail because analysis cannot change how old something is.

questions.s:
Although the scheme was popular with voters, economists warned that it was not ______; the government could not afford to keep paying for it beyond a few years.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: sustainable
ambitious
generous
legal
questions.e: A scheme that cannot be paid for beyond a few years cannot be kept going, so it is not sustainable. "Generous" fails because the warning is about how long the scheme can last, not how much it gives.

questions.s:
The coach's ______ praise motivated the young players more than any criticism could have.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: mocking
reluctant
absent
sincere
questions.e: Praise that genuinely motivates is heartfelt, or sincere. "Mocking" praise is not real praise, and "absent" praise could not motivate anyone.

questions.s:
The committee's report was ______: it ran to six hundred pages and examined every aspect of the city's water supply.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: cursory
partial
exhaustive
superficial
questions.e: Six hundred pages covering every aspect make the report complete and thorough, which is exhaustive. "Cursory" and "superficial" mean hasty and shallow, the opposite.

questions.s:
The farmer had to ______ the broken fence before the goats escaped.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: paint
sell
repair
measure
questions.e: Fixing the broken fence keeps the goats in, so the farmer had to repair it. "Paint" and "measure" would leave the gap through which the goats could escape.

questions.s:
The scientist's discovery was ______: she found the new species while searching for something else entirely.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: accidental
planned
expected
deliberate
questions.e: Finding something while looking for something else is accidental. "Planned", "expected" and "deliberate" all describe the opposite situation.

questions.s:
The museum's director hopes that the new exhibition will "draw" large crowds during the holidays.

As used in the text, what does the word "draw" most nearly mean?
o: attract
sketch
take out
end level
questions.e: An exhibition that brings in crowds attracts them. "Sketch" is the everyday sense of draw, but an exhibition cannot sketch a crowd.

questions.s:
The village's ______ location, high in the mountains and far from any road, kept it isolated for centuries.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: central
remote
crowded
coastal
questions.e: Being far from any road high in the mountains makes a place remote. "Central" means the opposite, and "coastal" clashes with the mountains.

questions.s:
The professor ______ any suggestion that her result was accidental, insisting that it had been carefully predicted.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: welcomed
rebuffed
entertained
echoed
questions.e: Insisting the result was predicted means firmly rejecting the opposite view, so she rebuffed it. "Entertained" means considered seriously, which her insistence rules out.

questions.s:
The students ______ their results with the class, presenting graphs and photographs of their experiment.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: hid
lost
shared
deleted
questions.e: Presenting graphs and photographs to the class is sharing the results. "Hid" is the opposite of presenting them.

questions.s:
The scientists' estimate of the flood damage was deliberately ______: they used worst-case figures, so the true damage was probably smaller.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: optimistic
precise
random
pessimistic
questions.e: Basing an estimate on worst-case figures expects the worst, which is pessimistic. "Precise" fails because the true figure was probably smaller, so the estimate was not exact.

questions.s:
The language has ______ over centuries, absorbing words from Persian, Arabic and English.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: vanished
stagnated
evolved
shrunk
questions.e: Gradually taking in words from other languages is developing over time, or evolving. "Stagnated" means staying unchanged, which absorbing new words contradicts.

questions.s:
Her reputation as a careful scholar made the error in her final book all the more ______.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: forgivable
predictable
trivial
conspicuous
questions.e: A mistake by someone famous for care stands out sharply, so it is conspicuous. "Predictable" fails because a careful scholar is the last person expected to make such an error.

questions.s:
The clinic is ______ on Sundays, so patients must visit on another day.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: busy
closed
crowded
free
questions.e: Patients must go another day because the clinic is not open, so it is closed. "Busy" and "crowded" suggest it is open, merely full.

questions.s:
The children were ______ by the magician's tricks and begged him to perform them again.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: bored
frightened
delighted
annoyed
questions.e: Asking to see the tricks again shows the children enjoyed them, so they were delighted. "Bored" and "annoyed" children would not beg for more.

questions.s:
The inspectors' report ______ the causes of the factory fire, listing faulty wiring, blocked exits and missing alarms.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: ignores
prevents
celebrates
identifies
questions.e: Listing the causes is naming them, so the report identifies them. "Prevents" fails because a report written after a fire cannot stop it from happening.

questions.s:
The ______ of the experiment was clear: the more fertiliser the plants received, the taller they grew.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: cost
purpose
equipment
outcome
questions.e: The relationship described after the colon is what the experiment found, its outcome. "Purpose" is tempting, but a purpose is what an experiment sets out to do, not the pattern it reveals.

questions.s:
Nadia "picked up" a few words of Pashto while she was living in Peshawar.

As used in the text, what does the phrase "picked up" most nearly mean?
o: learned without formal study
lifted from the floor
collected by car
improved
questions.e: Gaining words just by living somewhere is learning them informally. "Lifted from the floor" is the literal meaning of the phrase, which cannot apply to words of a language.

questions.s:
The historian ______ the popular view that the canal was built in a single decade, showing that work actually stretched over forty years.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: endorses
echoes
debunks
overlooks
questions.e: Showing that a common belief is false is debunking it. "Endorses" and "echoes" mean agreeing with the view, which her evidence contradicts.

questions.s:
Because the evidence was ______, the jury could not reach a verdict.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: overwhelming
inconclusive
decisive
clear
questions.e: A jury fails to decide when the evidence does not settle the question, that is, when it is inconclusive. "Overwhelming" and "decisive" evidence would make a verdict easy.

questions.s:
Please ______ your phones during the exam so that they do not disturb other candidates.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: charge
display
switch off
lend
questions.e: A phone stops making noise only when it is switched off. "Display" would make the phones more noticeable, not less disturbing.

questions.s:
The new bridge has ______ trade between the two towns, which were once separated by a two-day journey.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: halted
delayed
boosted
hidden
questions.e: Replacing a two-day journey with a bridge makes trade easier, so it has boosted trade. "Halted" and "delayed" describe the effect of losing a bridge, not gaining one.

questions.s:
The scientist's ______ about the startling results was justified when other laboratories failed to reproduce them.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: scepticism
enthusiasm
confidence
delight
questions.e: Her attitude was proved right when the results could not be repeated, so she must have doubted them: scepticism. "Confidence" would have been proved wrong by the failed repeats.

questions.s:
The novelist's prose is ______, packed with long sentences, rare words and elaborate metaphors.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: spare
plain
ornate
colloquial
questions.e: Long sentences, rare words and elaborate metaphors make writing highly decorated, or ornate. "Spare" and "plain" mean simple, and "colloquial" means everyday speech, the opposite of rare words.

questions.s:
The hikers were ______ after the long climb and rested before continuing.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: energetic
exhausted
lost
early
questions.e: A long climb followed by a rest suggests the hikers were very tired, or exhausted. "Energetic" hikers would not need to rest.

questions.s:
The author ______ that social media harms teenagers but admits that her evidence is limited.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: proves
denies
forgets
suggests
questions.e: Admitting limited evidence fits a tentative claim, so she suggests rather than proves it. "Proves" clashes with the admission that her evidence is weak.

questions.s:
The rising cost of fuel has put "pressure" on small transport companies.

As used in the text, what does the word "pressure" most nearly mean?
o: a physical push
financial strain
the weight of air
polite persuasion
questions.e: Higher fuel costs squeeze a company's money, so pressure here means financial strain. "A physical push" is the literal sense, which does not fit costs acting on a business.

questions.s:
Because of the storm, the festival was ______ and moved to the following weekend.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: postponed
cancelled
extended
celebrated
questions.e: Moving an event to a later date is postponing it. "Cancelled" is the tempting choice, but a cancelled festival would not be held the following weekend.

questions.s:
The pharmacist gave ______ instructions: take one tablet every morning with water.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: confusing
simple
secret
rude
questions.e: One tablet each morning with water is an easy rule, so the instructions were simple. "Confusing" contradicts how clear the instruction is.

questions.s:
The critic's praise was ______: she admired the film's photography but found its story dull and its acting stiff.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: qualified
unreserved
effusive
insincere
questions.e: Praise limited by serious criticism is qualified, meaning restricted. "Unreserved" and "effusive" mean unlimited and gushing, which the complaints rule out.

questions.s:
The museum ______ visitors to touch some of the exhibits, an unusual policy that children especially enjoy.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: forbids
warns
forces
allows
questions.e: Children enjoy the policy because touching is permitted, so the museum allows it. "Forbids" is the usual policy, which would not be called unusual.

questions.s:
Before construction began, the engineers ______ the new design to make sure it could withstand strong winds.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: evaluated
painted
sold
ignored
questions.e: Checking whether a design can survive wind is judging its strength, or evaluating it. "Ignored" contradicts the effort to make sure it was safe.

questions.s:
The shop ______ its prices during the sale, so many items cost half as much as usual.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: raised
hid
reduced
fixed
questions.e: Items costing half as much means prices went down, so the shop reduced them. "Raised" means the opposite.

questions.s:
Researchers were ______ to explain why the birds left the lake early; none of their theories fitted all the facts.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: eager
unable
quick
paid
questions.e: If no theory fitted the facts, the researchers could not explain the event, so they were unable to. "Quick" contradicts the failure of every theory.

questions.s:
The politician's apology was widely seen as ______, since she repeated the same insult the very next day.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: heartfelt
overdue
eloquent
disingenuous
questions.e: Repeating the insult shows the apology was not meant, so it was disingenuous, or insincere. "Heartfelt" is the opposite, and "eloquent" describes style, not whether she meant it.

questions.s:
The beetle is ______ to a single valley in northern Pakistan; it is found nowhere else in the world.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: foreign
endemic
harmful
migratory
questions.e: A species found only in one place is endemic to it. "Migratory" animals move between regions, the opposite of being confined to one valley.

questions.s:
The students worked ______ to finish the project before the deadline.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: slowly
rarely
hard
carelessly
questions.e: Racing to meet a deadline calls for steady effort, so they worked hard. "Slowly" and "rarely" would make missing the deadline more likely.

questions.s:
The company plans to "launch" its new app in Karachi before releasing it nationwide.

As used in the text, what does the word "launch" most nearly mean?
o: introduce to the public
throw with force
send into space
set afloat
questions.e: Releasing an app first in one city is introducing it to users there. "Send into space" is the sense used for rockets, which does not fit an app.

questions.s:
Her argument was ______ by a single example that did not fit, so she revised it.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: proven
weakened
delayed
written
questions.e: An example that does not fit damages an argument, which is why she revised it, so it was weakened. "Proven" is the opposite: a contrary example cannot prove an argument.

questions.s:
Rather than ______ the dispute, the mediator's remarks inflamed it, and both sides walked out.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: escalating
prolonging
defusing
provoking
questions.e: "Rather than" contrasts with inflaming, so the blank needs the opposite, calming the dispute: defusing. "Escalating" and "provoking" mean the same as inflaming and remove the contrast.

questions.s:
The baby was ______ by the soft music and soon fell asleep.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: excited
scared
woken
calmed
questions.e: Soft music that leads to sleep soothes the baby, so it was calmed. "Excited" and "woken" describe the opposite effect.

questions.s:
The researchers kept the results ______ until the study was published, sharing them with no one outside the team.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: public
confidential
accurate
simple
questions.e: Sharing results with no one outside the team keeps them secret, or confidential. "Public" is the opposite of keeping them within the team.

questions.s:
The economy grew only ______ last year, rising by less than one per cent.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: rapidly
modestly
sharply
dramatically
questions.e: Growth of less than one per cent is small, and "only" stresses this, so it grew modestly. "Rapidly", "sharply" and "dramatically" all describe large growth.

questions.s:
The novel's hero is deeply ______: brave in battle yet cruel to his servants, generous to strangers yet cold to his family.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: consistent
cowardly
admirable
contradictory
questions.e: Each pair of traits clashes, so the hero is full of contradictions. "Consistent" is the reverse, and "cowardly" ignores his bravery in battle.

questions.s:
Imran will "run" the school's science club this year.

As used in the text, what does the word "run" most nearly mean?
o: manage
move quickly
flow
stand for election
questions.e: Running a club is being in charge of it, so run means manage. "Move quickly" is the most common meaning of run, but that sense needs no object, and here Imran runs the club itself.

questions.s:
The ______ of clean water in the village forced many families to walk miles each day to fetch it.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: abundance
quality
scarcity
purity
questions.e: Walking miles for water means there is too little nearby, a scarcity. "Abundance" means plenty, which would remove the need to walk.

questions.s:
To keep costs down, the architect ______ local materials such as brick and timber.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: avoided
imported
favoured
banned
questions.e: Using cheap local materials to cut costs means she preferred them, so she favoured them. "Imported" contradicts "local", and "avoided" would not keep costs down.

questions.s:
The firefighters arrived ______ and put out the blaze before it reached the shops.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: late
slowly
rarely
quickly
questions.e: Stopping the fire before it spread required a fast arrival, so they came quickly. "Late" and "slowly" would have let the fire reach the shops.

questions.s:
The author's claims about the ancient trade route are largely ______, based on guesswork rather than documents or excavations.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
o: conjectural
documented
verifiable
empirical
questions.e: Claims based on guesswork are conjectural. "Documented", "verifiable" and "empirical" all mean backed by evidence, which the text says is lacking.

questions.s:
