Although the medicine lowered blood pressure in most ______ researchers warned that its long-term effects were still unknown.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: patients; the
patients: the
patients, the
patients. The
questions.e: 'Although ... most patients' is a dependent clause, so a comma joins it to the main clause that follows. A semicolon or period would leave it as a fragment, and a colon must follow an independent clause.

questions.s:
The ______ cricket team from Lahore won the regional final by six wickets.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: womens'
women's'
womens
women's
questions.e: 'Women' is a plural that does not end in s, so its possessive is 'women's'. 'Womens' is not a word, and an extra apostrophe after the s is never standard.

questions.s:
The Mirzas have lived on this street for four generations, and the ______ house is now the oldest one on the block.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: Mirzas's
Mirzas'
Mirza's
Mirzas
questions.e: 'The Mirzas' is the plural of the family name, so the plural possessive adds only an apostrophe: the Mirzas' house. 'Mirza's' would be one person named Mirza, which does not fit 'the', 'Mirzas' has no possessive mark, and 'Mirzas's' is not standard for a plural.

questions.s:
The Batura Glacier has retreated noticeably since ______ of loss has alarmed farmers who depend on its meltwater.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: 1990 this rate
1990; this rate,
1990; this rate
1990, this rate
questions.e: Two independent clauses are joined, so a semicolon is correct. A comma alone makes a comma splice, no punctuation makes a run-on, and a comma after 'rate' cuts the subject 'this rate of loss' off from its verb.

questions.s:
Applicants must submit the ______ transcript, two letters of recommendation, and a short essay.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: following: a
following a
following. A
following; a
questions.e: 'Applicants must submit the following' is a complete clause, so a colon can introduce the list. A semicolon cannot introduce a list, the period leaves the list as a fragment, and no punctuation runs 'following' into the list.

questions.s:
Heavy rain flooded the lower ______ hundreds of families to move to higher ground.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: valley: forcing
valley; forcing
valley. Forcing
valley, forcing
questions.e: 'Forcing hundreds of families ...' is a participial phrase, not a clause, so a comma attaches it to the sentence. A semicolon or period would leave the phrase as a fragment, and a colon is not used to attach a modifier like this.

questions.s:
The idea that a city's trees can lower summer street temperatures by several ______ now widely accepted by urban planners.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: degrees; is
degrees—is
degrees is
degrees, is
questions.e: The whole phrase 'The idea that ... by several degrees' is the subject, and 'is' is its verb, so nothing should separate them. The 'that' clause is part of the subject, not an interruption, so a comma, semicolon or dash before 'is' is wrong.

questions.s:
Whether the new metro line will actually reduce traffic in ______ to be seen.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: Lahore; remains
Lahore remains
Lahore: remains
Lahore, remains
questions.e: The clause 'Whether ... in Lahore' acts as the subject of the verb 'remains', and no punctuation belongs between a subject and its verb. The comma, semicolon and colon all split them.

questions.s:
The festival's success came down to one ______ hundreds of unpaid volunteers.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: thing—its
thing, it was its
thing; its
thing. Its
questions.e: A dash after a complete clause can introduce an explanation, here the 'one thing'. A semicolon needs an independent clause after it, the period leaves 'Its ... volunteers' as a fragment, and 'thing, it was its' is a comma splice.

questions.s:
Not every metal is attracted to a magnet. ______ example, are not noticeably pulled by even a strong one.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: Copper, and aluminium, for
Copper and aluminium; for
Copper and aluminium for
Copper and aluminium, for
questions.e: 'For example' interrupts the clause and is set off by a pair of commas; the closing comma already follows 'example', so a comma must also come before 'for'. Commas around 'and aluminium' split the compound subject, and a semicolon would leave 'Copper and aluminium' as a fragment.

questions.s:
Even after a hundred ______ still the tallest building in the old part of the city.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: years it's,
years, its
years, it's
years, its'
questions.e: The sense is 'it is still the tallest building', so the contraction 'it's' is needed, after the comma that ends the introductory phrase. 'Its' is the possessive, 'its'' is not a word, and the final option drops the introductory comma and puts a comma between the verb and 'still'.

questions.s:
The volunteers say ______ ready to start planting the mangrove seedlings next week.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: they're
their
theyre
there
questions.e: The sense is 'they are ready', so the contraction 'they're' with its apostrophe is needed. 'Their' is possessive, 'there' refers to a place, and 'theyre' lacks the apostrophe.

questions.s:
The results of the sleep study were ______ who slept at least eight hours scored higher on every memory test.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: clear, and, students
clear: students
clear students
clear, students
questions.e: A colon after the complete clause 'The results ... were clear' introduces the explanation of what the results showed. A comma alone makes a comma splice, no punctuation makes a run-on, and a comma after 'and' wrongly separates the conjunction from its clause.

questions.s:
The book ______ from the library last week turned out to be a first edition.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: that, I borrowed
that I borrowed,
, that I borrowed
that I borrowed
questions.e: 'That I borrowed from the library last week' is a restrictive clause identifying the book, so it takes no commas. Each comma option either splits the clause from its noun or separates the subject 'The book' from its verb 'turned'.

questions.s:
Gilgit, where the Gilgit and Hunza rivers ______ a common starting point for trips to the high mountain valleys.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: meet—is
meet, is
meet is
meet; is
questions.e: The non-restrictive clause 'where the Gilgit and Hunza rivers meet' opens with a comma after 'Gilgit', so a matching comma must close it before the verb 'is'. No punctuation, a semicolon or a dash all fail to close the comma pair correctly.

questions.s:
The team ______ the samples had been labelled with the wrong dates.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: found; that
found, that
found: that
found that
questions.e: 'That the samples had been labelled with the wrong dates' is the object of 'found', and no punctuation separates a verb from its object. A comma, colon or semicolon before 'that' all break the clause.

questions.s:
Researchers tested the new dust-repelling coating on three different ______ glass and ceramic tile.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: surfaces: steel,
surfaces, such as: steel,
surfaces; steel,
surfaces steel,
questions.e: A colon after the complete clause 'Researchers tested ... on three different surfaces' introduces the list. A semicolon cannot introduce a list, a colon should not follow 'such as', and no punctuation runs the noun into the list.

questions.s:
The handwoven carpets of Balochistan are prized for their deep ______ few buyers realise how many months a single piece takes to weave.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: colours yet,
colours; yet,
colours, yet
colours, yet,
questions.e: When 'yet' joins two independent clauses, the comma goes before it. A comma after 'yet' wrongly separates the conjunction from the clause it introduces.

questions.s:
The lecture series, which began as a small reading group in a Peshawar ______ grown into an annual event that fills the university's largest hall.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: bookshop has
bookshop, has
bookshop; has
bookshop, it has
questions.e: The non-restrictive clause 'which began ... Peshawar bookshop' opens with a comma, so it must close with a comma before the verb 'has'. No punctuation leaves the pair broken, a semicolon splits subject from verb, and adding 'it' gives the sentence a second subject for the same verb.

questions.s:
The power went out just before the ______ the students finished the exam by candlelight.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: final paper; nevertheless,
final paper, nevertheless,
final paper nevertheless
final paper nevertheless,
questions.e: 'Nevertheless' links two independent clauses here, so it needs a semicolon before it and a comma after it. Only a comma, or nothing, before 'nevertheless' makes a comma splice or a run-on.

questions.s:
My grandmother's recipe for ______ a slow-cooked stew of wheat and meat, has been passed down for four generations.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: haleem;
haleem—
haleem,
haleem
questions.e: The appositive 'a slow-cooked stew of wheat and meat' closes with a comma, so it must open with a comma after 'haleem'. No punctuation leaves the pair incomplete, a semicolon cannot open an appositive, and a dash cannot be paired with a closing comma.

questions.s:
The two rival ______ from Faisalabad and one from Sialkot, met in the final after a week of rain delays.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: teams—one
teams; one
teams: one
teams, one
questions.e: The interrupting phrase 'one from Faisalabad and one from Sialkot' closes with a comma before 'met', so it must open with a comma too. A dash cannot pair with a closing comma, and a semicolon or colon would leave 'The two rival teams' without a verb.

questions.s:
______ largest city, Karachi, is home to more than fifteen million people.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: Pakistan's
Pakistans's
Pakistans'
Pakistans
questions.e: The largest city belongs to Pakistan, a singular noun, so the possessive adds an apostrophe and s: Pakistan's. The other forms treat the country's name as a plural or leave out the apostrophe.

questions.s:
The guide pointed out the fort's thick stone ______ had protected the town from invaders for centuries.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: walls. Which
walls; which
walls, which
walls which,
questions.e: 'Which had protected the town ...' is a non-restrictive clause adding information about the walls, so a comma introduces it. A comma after 'which' splits the pronoun from its verb, and a semicolon or period leaves the 'which' clause as a fragment.

questions.s:
The emergency kit contained a compass, a ______ a whistle and a first-aid pouch.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: torch:
torch,
torch
torch;
questions.e: Items in a simple series are separated by commas. A semicolon is used between list items only when they already contain commas, a colon does not separate items, and no punctuation runs 'a torch' into 'a whistle'.

questions.s:
Unlike most frogs, which lay their eggs in ______ Darwin's frogs carry developing tadpoles inside their vocal sacs.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: water; male
water. Male
water male
water, male
questions.e: The non-restrictive clause 'which lay their eggs in water' opened with a comma, so a comma must close it and also ends the introductory phrase 'Unlike most frogs ...'. A semicolon or period would leave that phrase as a fragment, and no punctuation runs it into the main clause.

questions.s:
The Lahore Fort—rebuilt several times by Mughal ______ now a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: emperors—is
emperors, is
emperors; is
emperors is
questions.e: The interrupting phrase opens with a dash, so it must close with a dash before the verb 'is'. A comma cannot close a dash, a semicolon splits subject from verb, and no punctuation leaves the phrase unclosed.

questions.s:
The student ______ leading the robotics club this year has already won two national prizes.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: who's,
whos
who's
whose
questions.e: The sense is 'who is leading the robotics club', so the contraction 'who's' is needed. 'Whose' is possessive and would need a noun after it, 'whos' lacks the apostrophe, and a comma after 'who's' splits the verb 'is leading'.

questions.s:
The panel included Hina Akbar, a ______ Sheikh, a sculptor; and Lubna Rao, a filmmaker.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: novelist Omar
novelist; Omar
novelist, Omar
novelist: Omar
questions.e: Each item in this list already contains a comma (name, role), so semicolons separate the items, as after 'sculptor'. A comma would make the names and roles impossible to sort, a colon does not separate list items, and no punctuation runs two items together.

questions.s:
The first trial of the vaccine produced weak results; the ______ however, showed a strong immune response.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: second, trial,
second trial;
second trial,
second trial
questions.e: 'However' interrupts the second clause and already has a comma after it, so a matching comma must come before it: 'the second trial, however, showed'. Leaving out that comma breaks the pair, a comma inside 'second trial' splits the noun phrase, and a semicolon would leave 'the second trial' as a fragment.

questions.s:
Saturn has more known moons than any other ______ are still being discovered.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: planet, new ones,
planet, new ones
planet new ones
planet. New ones
questions.e: The text contains two complete sentences, so a period separates them. A comma alone makes a comma splice, no punctuation makes a run-on, and a comma after 'ones' also splits the subject from its verb.

questions.s:
The Indus river dolphin, one of the world's few freshwater dolphin ______ almost completely blind.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: species, is
species; is
species—is
species is
questions.e: The appositive 'one of the world's few freshwater dolphin species' opens with a comma, so a comma must close it before the verb 'is'. No punctuation leaves the pair unclosed, a semicolon splits subject from verb, and a dash cannot close a comma-opened phrase.

questions.s:
Most of the town's residents work in the textile ______ growing number commute to Sialkot for jobs in sports-goods factories.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: industry; while a
industry. While a
industry while, a
industry, while a
questions.e: 'While a growing number commute ...' is a dependent clause, so it is joined to the main clause with a comma. A semicolon or period would leave it as a fragment, and a comma after 'while' separates the conjunction from its own clause.

questions.s:
The bridge's design won several awards, but ______ final cost was nearly twice the original estimate.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: its'
its
it was
it's
questions.e: The cost belongs to the bridge, so the possessive pronoun 'its', without an apostrophe, is correct. 'It's' means 'it is', 'its'' is not a word, and 'it was final cost' makes no sense.

questions.s:
Some desert plants store large amounts of water in their ______ cactus, for example, can swell noticeably after a heavy rain.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: stems, the saguaro
stems the saguaro
stems; the saguaro
stems the saguaro;
questions.e: Both parts are independent clauses, so a semicolon joins them; 'for example' is already set off by its own pair of commas. A comma alone makes a comma splice, no punctuation makes a run-on, and a semicolon after 'saguaro' splits the noun 'saguaro cactus'.

questions.s:
The poet Amna Riaz has published four collections. Her ______ won the national poetry award in 2019.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: collection Night Rain
collection, Night Rain
collection, Night Rain,
collection Night Rain,
questions.e: Because Riaz has four collections, the title is needed to say which one won, so it is a restrictive appositive and takes no commas. Paired commas would wrongly treat the title as extra information, and a single comma separates the subject from its verb 'won'.

questions.s:
After months of ______ two neighbouring villages agreed to share the spring's water.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: negotiation. The
negotiation; the
negotiation, the
negotiation: the
questions.e: 'After months of negotiation' is an introductory phrase, so a comma separates it from the main clause. A semicolon or period would leave the phrase as a fragment, and a colon must follow a complete clause.

questions.s:
The chess clubs across the city all face the same ______ shortage of trained coaches.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: problem; a
problem: a
problem, it is a
problem. A
questions.e: A colon after the complete clause 'The chess clubs ... face the same problem' introduces what the problem is. A semicolon needs an independent clause after it, the period leaves 'A shortage of trained coaches' as a fragment, and 'problem, it is a' is a comma splice.

questions.s:
______ essay on saving water at home won first prize in the district competition.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: Bilal's
Bilals
Bilals'
Bilal'
questions.e: The essay belongs to one person, Bilal, so the singular possessive 'Bilal's' is used. 'Bilals'' would be the possessive of a plural, 'Bilals' has no apostrophe, and 'Bilal'' drops the s.

questions.s:
The commission's final report, published last ______ dozens of changes to the way exam papers are marked.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: March recommends
March; recommends
March: recommends
March, recommends
questions.e: 'Published last March' is a non-restrictive phrase that opens with a comma, so a comma must close it before the verb 'recommends'. Without the comma the pair is broken, and a semicolon or colon separates the subject from its verb.

questions.s:
The new observatory was built on a remote ridge in northern ______ already recorded images of several faint comets.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: Chile, it has,
Chile; it has
Chile it has
Chile, it has
questions.e: Two independent clauses are joined, so a semicolon is correct. A comma alone makes a comma splice, no punctuation makes a run-on, and a comma after 'has' splits the verb 'has recorded'.

questions.s:
Mehwish's argument—that rural schools need better roads more than they need new ______ convinced the panel.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: buildings—soon
buildings soon
buildings; soon
buildings, soon
questions.e: The 'that' clause explaining the argument opens with a dash, so it must close with a dash. A comma cannot close a dash, a semicolon splits the subject 'Mehwish's argument' from its verb, and no punctuation leaves the interruption unclosed.

questions.s:
The exhibition features paintings by several ______ Sadequain and Gulgee.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: artists, including:
artists including:
artists, including
artists; including
questions.e: A comma before 'including' introduces the examples, and no punctuation should follow 'including', because a colon cannot come between a word like 'including' and its object. A semicolon cannot introduce a phrase that is not an independent clause.

questions.s:
The ______ of both factories agreed to install new fire exits by the end of the year.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: owners'
owners's
owner's
owners
questions.e: Here 'owners' is a simple plural subject; nothing belongs to the owners in this phrase, so no apostrophe is needed. The apostrophe forms are possessives and would need a noun after them.

questions.s:
Both ______ profits rose sharply in the year after the merger.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: companys'
companies'
company's
companies
questions.e: 'Both' shows there are two companies, and the profits belong to them, so the plural possessive 'companies'' is needed. 'Company's' is singular, 'companies' has no possessive mark, and 'companys'' misspells the plural.

questions.s:
In Skardu, where winter nights often fall well below freezing, most homes are still heated with ______ increasing number of families now use small solar panels as well.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: wood, but an
wood but; an
wood, but, an
wood but, an
questions.e: Two independent clauses are joined by 'but', so a comma comes before the conjunction and nothing after it. A comma or semicolon after 'but' cuts the conjunction off from the clause it introduces.

questions.s:
The museum's director, as well as two of her senior ______ to attend the opening in Islamabad.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: assistants—plans
assistants; plans
assistants plans
assistants, plans
questions.e: The phrase 'as well as two of her senior assistants' interrupts the subject and opens with a comma, so it must close with a comma before the verb 'plans'. No punctuation leaves the pair open, a semicolon splits subject from verb, and a dash cannot close a comma-opened phrase.

questions.s:
The award was presented to Nadia ______ has spent a decade mapping the ancient ruins near Taxila.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: Rehman; who
Rehman who
Rehman, who
Rehman. Who
questions.e: A clause describing a person already named is non-restrictive, so it is set off with a comma: 'Nadia Rehman, who ...'. Without the comma the clause wrongly reads as restrictive, and a semicolon or period leaves the 'who' clause as a fragment.

questions.s:
The city library closes at eight on ______ opens at ten on Sundays.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: weekdays it
weekdays it;
weekdays, it
weekdays; it
questions.e: Two independent clauses are joined, so a semicolon is correct. A comma alone makes a comma splice, no punctuation makes a run-on, and a semicolon after 'it' separates the subject from its verb.

questions.s:
Since the new bridge reopened in ______ through the old bazaar has fallen by almost half.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: June; traffic
June, traffic
June. Traffic
June: traffic
questions.e: 'Since the new bridge reopened in June' is a dependent clause, so a comma joins it to the main clause. A semicolon or period would leave it as a fragment, and a colon must follow an independent clause.

questions.s:
After studying satellite images from four decades, the researchers concluded that the ______ caused the grassland's decline.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: drought not overgrazing,
drought; not overgrazing,
drought, not overgrazing,
drought, not overgrazing
questions.e: 'Not overgrazing' is an interrupting contrast that must be enclosed by a pair of commas. With only one comma the subject is cut off from its verb 'caused', and a semicolon cannot be used inside a single clause.

questions.s:
The committee will, after reviewing all eighty ______ announce the winners on its website.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: applications,
applications—
applications
applications;
questions.e: The phrase 'after reviewing all eighty applications' interrupts the verb 'will announce' and opens with a comma, so it must close with a comma. No punctuation leaves the pair open, a semicolon would end the clause before its main verb, and a dash cannot close a comma-opened phrase.

questions.s:
Hunza's apricots, dried in the sun on flat ______ sold in markets as far away as Karachi.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: rooftops, are
rooftops: are
rooftops; are
rooftops are
questions.e: The phrase 'dried in the sun on flat rooftops' opens with a comma, so a comma must close it before the verb 'are'. No punctuation breaks the pair, and a semicolon or colon separates the subject from its verb.

questions.s:
The national science conference was held in Hyderabad, ______ March, and drew teachers from every province.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: Sindh; in
Sindh: in
Sindh, in
Sindh in
questions.e: When a province follows a city in the middle of a sentence, commas go both before and after it: 'Hyderabad, Sindh, in March'. Leaving out the second comma breaks the pair, and a semicolon or colon cannot sit inside this clause.

questions.s:
Bilal wanted to study ______ sister chose engineering instead.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: medicine his
medicine, his
medicine; his,
medicine; his
questions.e: Two independent clauses are joined, so a semicolon is correct. A comma alone makes a comma splice, no punctuation makes a run-on, and a comma after 'his' separates the word from the noun it belongs to.

questions.s:
A single ______ nest can contain more than a hundred carefully woven twigs.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: sparrows's
sparrow's
sparrows'
sparrows
questions.e: 'A single' shows there is one sparrow, so the singular possessive 'sparrow's' is needed. 'Sparrows'' is plural possessive, 'sparrows' is a plain plural, and 'sparrows's' is not standard.

questions.s:
Some spices, such as cumin and ______ best toasted in a dry pan before they are ground.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: coriander—are
coriander; are
coriander are
coriander, are
questions.e: The examples 'such as cumin and coriander' are non-restrictive and open with a comma, so a comma must close them before the verb 'are'. Leaving it out breaks the pair, a semicolon splits subject from verb, and a dash cannot close a comma-opened phrase.

questions.s:
The factory in Gujranwala switched to solar ______ result, its monthly electricity bill fell by a third.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: power as a
power; as a
power; as a,
power, as a
questions.e: 'As a result' links two independent clauses, so a semicolon goes before it (the comma after 'result' is already there). A comma alone makes a comma splice, no punctuation makes a run-on, and a comma inside 'as a result' breaks the phrase.

questions.s:
The Faisal Mosque in Islamabad, designed by the Turkish architect Vedat ______ completed in 1986.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: Dalokay; was
Dalokay was
Dalokay, was
Dalokay—was
questions.e: The phrase 'designed by the Turkish architect Vedat Dalokay' opens with a comma, so it must close with a comma before the verb 'was'. No punctuation leaves the pair open, a semicolon splits subject from verb, and a dash cannot close a comma-opened phrase.

questions.s:
The tea harvest begins in ______ work from dawn until the afternoon heat becomes too strong.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: April, pickers
April, pickers,
April pickers
April. Pickers
questions.e: There are two complete sentences here, so a period separates them. A comma alone makes a comma splice, no punctuation makes a run-on, and a comma after 'pickers' splits the subject from its verb.

questions.s:
Only one word can describe the view of Nanga Parbat from Fairy ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: Meadows, it is breathtaking.
Meadows: breathtaking.
Meadows; breathtaking.
Meadows breathtaking.
questions.e: A colon after a complete clause can introduce the single word that the clause promises. A semicolon needs an independent clause after it, 'Meadows, it is breathtaking' is a comma splice, and no punctuation runs the word into the place name.

questions.s:
The town, ______ population has doubled since 2000, now needs three new secondary schools.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: whose
whos'
who's'
who's
questions.e: 'Whose' is the possessive relative pronoun and can refer to places and things as well as people: the population belongs to the town. 'Who's' means 'who is' or 'who has', and the other two forms are not words.

questions.s:
Residents of the colony say ______ been more than ten years since the drainage canal was last cleaned.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: it's,
it's
its
its'
questions.e: The sense is 'it has been more than ten years', so the contraction 'it's' is needed. 'Its' is the possessive, 'its'' is not a word, and a comma after 'it's' would split the verb 'has been'.

questions.s:
If the samples are not kept ______ bacteria in them will multiply quickly.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: cold; the
cold: the
cold. The
cold, the
questions.e: 'If the samples are not kept cold' is a dependent clause, so a comma joins it to the main clause. A semicolon or period would leave it as a fragment, and a colon must follow an independent clause.

questions.s:
A former fast ______ now coaches young players at a cricket club in Rawalpindi.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: bowler: Saleem
bowler Saleem
bowler, Saleem
bowler; Saleem
questions.e: 'A former fast bowler' is an introductory appositive describing Saleem, so a comma separates it from the subject. Without the comma the words run together, and a semicolon or colon would leave 'A former fast bowler' as a fragment.

questions.s:
The ______ choice award at the festival went to a short film about a Karachi fish market.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: people's
peoples
people'
peoples's
questions.e: 'People' is a plural that does not end in s, so its possessive is 'people's'. 'Peoples' has no apostrophe, 'people'' drops the s, and 'peoples's' is not a standard form.

questions.s:
Rising sea levels and the loss of mangrove ______ the coastline near Keti Bandar more exposed to storms than ever.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: forests; have left
forests: have left
forests, have left
forests have left
questions.e: The compound subject 'Rising sea levels and the loss of mangrove forests' is followed directly by its verb 'have left', with no punctuation between them. A comma, semicolon or colon all wrongly separate the subject from the verb.

questions.s:
Many of Lahore's old havelis have been turned into restaurants and ______ once housed large extended families.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: guesthouses, they
guesthouses; they
guesthouses they
guesthouses, they,
questions.e: 'Many of Lahore's old havelis ... guesthouses' and 'they once housed large extended families' are both independent clauses, so a semicolon joins them. A comma alone makes a comma splice, no punctuation makes a run-on, and a comma after 'they' splits the subject from its verb.

questions.s:
Students who complete all twelve modules of the online course before the end of ______ a certificate signed by the dean.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: June receive
June—receive
June; receive
June, receive
questions.e: The long subject 'Students who complete ... before the end of June' contains a restrictive 'who' clause, which takes no commas, so nothing separates the subject from its verb 'receive'. A comma, semicolon or dash would all split them.

questions.s:
Before the final, the coach gave the team one piece of ______ the ball, not the scoreboard.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: advice, watch
advice that: watch
advice: watch
advice watch
questions.e: A colon after the complete clause 'the coach gave the team one piece of advice' introduces the advice itself. 'Advice, watch' is a comma splice, no punctuation makes a run-on, and a colon should not follow the word 'that'.

questions.s:
Before submitting their work to the journal, the two scientists reviewed each ______ papers line by line.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: others
others'
other's
other's'
questions.e: The standard possessive of 'each other' is 'each other's', with the apostrophe before the s. 'Others'' and 'others' are not used with 'each', and an extra apostrophe after the s is never correct.

questions.s:
The results of the trial were encouraging. ______ study included only forty volunteers.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: However: the
However, the
However the
However; the
questions.e: When 'However' begins a sentence as a transition, a comma follows it. Without the comma the sentence misreads 'However the study' as 'in whatever way the study', and a semicolon or colon cannot follow a single introductory word.

questions.s:
The tour stops in Lahore, known for its ______ famous for its shrines; and Bahawalpur, home to several palaces.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: food Multan,
food, Multan,
food: Multan,
food; Multan,
questions.e: The list items contain commas of their own, so semicolons separate the items, as the rest of the sentence shows. A comma would make the items hard to tell apart, a colon does not separate list items, and no punctuation runs two items together.

questions.s:
The Urdu ______ to the cloth spread on the floor or a table before a meal is served.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: word dastarkhwan refers
word, dastarkhwan, refers
word dastarkhwan, refers
word, dastarkhwan refers
questions.e: Urdu has many words, so 'dastarkhwan' is essential to say which word is meant; as a restrictive appositive it takes no commas. Paired commas would wrongly mark it as extra information, and a single comma separates the subject from the verb 'refers'.

questions.s:
The day's schedule is as ______ at nine, lectures at ten, and lunch at one.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: follows; registration
follows: registration
follows. Registration
follows registration
questions.e: 'The day's schedule is as follows' is a complete clause, so a colon introduces the list. A semicolon cannot introduce a list, no punctuation runs the clause into the list, and the period leaves the list as a fragment.

questions.s:
My uncle—who has repaired clocks in Rawalpindi's old bazaar for forty ______ the trade is slowly dying out.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: years says
years; says
years, says
years—says
questions.e: The 'who' clause opens with a dash, so it must close with a dash before the verb 'says'. A comma cannot close a dash, no punctuation leaves the clause open, and a semicolon splits the subject from its verb.

questions.s:
The price of wheat flour rose by 20 percent last ______ wages for most workers stayed the same.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: year, meanwhile
year meanwhile,
year; meanwhile,
year, meanwhile,
questions.e: 'Meanwhile' links two independent clauses here, so a semicolon goes before it and a comma after it. With only a comma or no punctuation before 'meanwhile', the sentence becomes a comma splice or a run-on.

questions.s:
The new curriculum aims not only to improve test ______ to turn students into confident readers.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: scores but also
scores: but also
scores; but also
scores, but also,
questions.e: 'Not only ... but also' links two parallel phrases ('to improve test scores' and 'to turn students ...') inside one clause, so no punctuation is needed. A comma after 'also' splits the phrase from its object, and a semicolon or colon cannot divide a single clause like this.

questions.s:
Mohenjo-daro, which was rediscovered in the 1920s and is now a UNESCO World Heritage ______ of the best-preserved Bronze Age cities in South Asia.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: Site—is one
Site; is one
Site is one
Site, is one
questions.e: The non-restrictive clause 'which was rediscovered ... World Heritage Site' opens with a comma, so a comma must close it before the main verb 'is'. Without that comma the pair is broken, a semicolon splits subject from verb, and a dash cannot close a comma-opened clause.

questions.s:
The stall near the college gate sells samosas, ______ jalebis and fresh lassi.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: pakoras,
pakoras
pakoras;
pakoras:
questions.e: Items in a simple series are separated by commas. A semicolon separates list items only when they contain commas themselves, a colon does not separate items, and no punctuation runs two items together.

questions.s:
The river was too high to ______ villagers waited on the bank for the water to fall.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: cross the;
cross the
cross; the
cross, the
questions.e: Two independent clauses are joined, so a semicolon is correct. A comma alone creates a comma splice, no punctuation creates a run-on (and misreads 'cross the villagers'), and a semicolon after 'the' splits the article from its noun.

questions.s:
The road to Naran was blocked by a ______ the tourists spent the night in Balakot.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: landslide, so,
landslide, so
landslide so,
landslide; so,
questions.e: When 'so' joins two independent clauses, a comma goes before it and nothing after it. A comma after 'so' cuts the conjunction off from the clause it introduces.

questions.s:
To escape the summer heat, the research team moved its base to ______ the nights are cool even in July.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: Murree where
Murree; where
Murree. Where
Murree, where
questions.e: 'Where the nights are cool even in July' adds information about a place already named, so it is non-restrictive and set off with a comma. Without the comma it wrongly reads as restrictive, and a semicolon or period leaves the 'where' clause as a fragment.

questions.s:
Nobody in the lab could remember ______ turn it was to lock the freezer room.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: who's
whos
whose
whose'
questions.e: The turn belongs to someone, so the possessive 'whose' is needed. 'Who's' means 'who is' or 'who has', 'whos' is not a word, and 'whose'' adds a stray apostrophe.

questions.s:
In the end, the judges chose the simplest ______ was also the cheapest to build.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: design; it
design, it
design it
design; it,
questions.e: Both 'the judges chose the simplest design' and 'it was also the cheapest to build' are independent clauses, so a semicolon joins them. A comma alone makes a comma splice, no punctuation makes a run-on, and a comma after 'it' separates the subject from its verb.

questions.s:
Ayesha's only ______ lives in Toronto, where he works as a nurse.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: brother; Hamza,
brother, Hamza,
brother Hamza,
brother, Hamza
questions.e: Because Ayesha has only one brother, his name adds non-essential information and is set off by a pair of commas. A single comma on either side of the name separates the subject from its verb 'lives', and a semicolon cannot sit inside a single clause.

questions.s:
The guide checked his own ticket first and then looked at ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: everyone else's.
everyone else'.
everyone's else.
everyone elses'.
questions.e: In 'everyone else', the possessive 's goes on the last word of the phrase: everyone else's. Putting it on 'everyone' splits the phrase, and 'elses'' and 'else'' are not standard forms.

questions.s:
The rapid growth of online shopping in cities such as Lahore and ______ changed the way small shops stock their shelves.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: Karachi; has
Karachi, has
Karachi: has
Karachi has
questions.e: The long subject 'The rapid growth of online shopping in cities such as Lahore and Karachi' is followed directly by its verb 'has changed'. Any comma, semicolon or colon there separates the subject from its verb.

questions.s:
The museum opens at ten in the ______ are sold until an hour before closing.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: morning; tickets
morning, tickets
morning tickets;
morning tickets
questions.e: Two independent clauses are joined, so a semicolon is correct. A comma alone makes a comma splice, no punctuation makes a run-on, and a semicolon after 'tickets' cuts the subject off from its verb 'are sold'.

questions.s:
All the ______ bicycles were parked in a single row outside the school gate.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: girls
girl's
girls'
girls's
questions.e: 'All the' shows there are many girls, so the plural possessive adds only an apostrophe after the s: girls'. 'Girl's' is singular, 'girls' has no possessive mark, and 'girls's' adds an extra s.

questions.s:
Once the paint had ______ children hung their pictures on the classroom wall.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: dried; the
dried: the
dried. The
dried, the
questions.e: 'Once the paint had dried' is a dependent clause, so a comma joins it to the main clause. A semicolon or period would leave it as a fragment, and a colon must follow an independent clause.

questions.s:
The parrot flapped ______ wings and flew to the top of the cage.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: it's
its
it is
its'
questions.e: The wings belong to the parrot, so the possessive pronoun 'its', with no apostrophe, is correct. 'It's' and 'it is' mean the same thing and make no sense here, and 'its'' is not a word.

questions.s:
The college library holds thousands of Urdu ______ also has a growing collection of Punjabi poetry.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: books. It
books, it,
books it
books, it
questions.e: There are two complete sentences here, so a period separates them. A comma alone makes a comma splice, no punctuation makes a run-on, and a comma after 'it' splits the subject from its verb.

questions.s:
For the picnic, we packed only three ______ fruit and juice.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: things. Sandwiches,
things sandwiches,
things; sandwiches,
things: sandwiches,
questions.e: The clause 'we packed only three things' is complete, so a colon introduces the list. A semicolon cannot introduce a list, the period leaves the list as a fragment, and no punctuation runs the noun into the list.

questions.s:
The tall trees along the canal ______ cool shade throughout the summer.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: bank, provide
bank provide
bank: provide
bank; provide
questions.e: 'The tall trees along the canal bank' is the subject and 'provide' is its verb; no punctuation goes between them. A comma, semicolon or colon all separate the subject from its verb.

questions.s:
Hamid practised penalty kicks every ______ he still missed his first attempt in the match.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: day but,
day; but,
day, but
day, but,
questions.e: When 'but' joins two independent clauses, a comma goes before the conjunction and nothing after it. A comma or semicolon placed after 'but' cuts the conjunction off from its own clause.

questions.s:
After the assembly, the students collected ______ bags from the hall.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: their
theyre
they're
there
questions.e: The bags belong to the students, so the possessive 'their' is needed. 'They're' means 'they are', 'there' refers to a place, and 'theyre' is a misspelling of the contraction.

questions.s:
Nida Aslam, the debating ______ the meeting with a short speech about the coming season.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: club's treasurer; opened
club's treasurer, opened
club's treasurer—opened
club's treasurer opened
questions.e: The appositive 'the debating club's treasurer' opens with a comma, so a comma must close it before the verb 'opened'. No punctuation leaves the pair open, a semicolon splits subject from verb, and a dash cannot close a comma-opened phrase.

questions.s:
Every hotel in the town was fully ______ we found a small guesthouse on the edge of the lake.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: booked, however,
booked however,
booked however
booked; however,
questions.e: 'However' links two independent clauses here, so it takes a semicolon before it and a comma after it. A comma or no punctuation before 'however' makes a comma splice or a run-on.

questions.s:
The old clock—a wedding gift to my ______ keeps perfect time.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: grandfather still
grandfather, still
grandfather—still
grandfather; still
questions.e: The appositive opens with a dash, so it must close with a dash before the rest of the main clause. A comma cannot close a dash, a semicolon splits the subject from its verb, and no punctuation leaves the appositive open.

questions.s:
Medicines that are left in hot ______ lose their strength surprisingly quickly.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: cars, often
cars; often
cars: often
cars often
questions.e: The restrictive clause 'that are left in hot cars' is part of the subject and takes no commas, so nothing separates the subject from 'often lose'. A comma, semicolon or colon would split the subject from its verb.

questions.s:
Lake Saiful ______ lies at more than 3,200 metres, freezes over completely in winter.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: Muluk which
Muluk; which
Muluk, which
Muluk: which
questions.e: There is only one Lake Saiful Muluk, so the 'which' clause is non-restrictive and needs a pair of commas; the closing comma is already after 'metres'. Without the opening comma the pair is broken, and a semicolon or colon cannot introduce a 'which' clause.

questions.s:
The village is famous for one ______ painted wooden toys.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: product. Brightly
product: brightly
product; brightly
product, it is brightly
questions.e: A colon after the complete clause 'The village is famous for one product' introduces what that product is. A semicolon needs an independent clause after it, the period leaves 'Brightly painted wooden toys' as a fragment, and 'product, it is' is a comma splice.

questions.s:
The Karachi Express left the station at ______ in Lahore early the next morning.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: dusk, arriving
dusk; arriving
dusk: arriving
dusk. Arriving
questions.e: 'Arriving in Lahore early the next morning' is a participial phrase, not a clause, so a comma attaches it to the sentence. A semicolon or period would leave the phrase as a fragment, and a colon is not used to attach a modifier.

questions.s:
The main bridge into the town is being ______ drivers must use the narrow road through the fields.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: repaired therefore,
repaired, therefore,
repaired, therefore
repaired; therefore,
questions.e: 'Therefore' links two independent clauses here, so a semicolon goes before it and a comma after it. With only a comma or nothing before 'therefore', the sentence is a comma splice or a run-on.

questions.s:
The ______ union voted to accept the new contract, which covers every nurse in the city's public hospitals.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: nurse's
nurses'
nurses's
nurse'
questions.e: The union belongs to many nurses, so the plural possessive 'nurses'' is needed. 'Nurse's' refers to only one nurse, and 'nurses's' and 'nurse'' are not standard forms.

questions.s:
The finalists came from Mingora, ______ Sindh; and Quetta, Balochistan.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Hyderabad,
Khyber Pakhtunkhwa: Hyderabad,
Khyber Pakhtunkhwa; Hyderabad,
Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Hyderabad,
questions.e: Each list item already contains a comma (city, province), so semicolons separate the items, as later in the sentence. A comma makes the items hard to sort, a colon does not separate list items, and no punctuation runs two items together.

questions.s:
Several of the paintings, including two by ______ damaged when the gallery's basement flooded.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: Chughtai, were
Chughtai were
Chughtai—were
Chughtai; were
questions.e: The phrase 'including two by Chughtai' opens with a comma, so a comma must close it before the verb 'were'. Without the comma the pair is broken, a semicolon splits subject from verb, and a dash cannot close a comma-opened phrase.

questions.s:
During the science lesson, Ms. Raza asked the class why the sky looks ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: blue;
blue.
blue?
blue,
questions.e: This is an indirect question: it reports what was asked inside a statement, so the sentence ends with a period, not a question mark. A comma or semicolon cannot end a sentence.

questions.s:
Some birds travel thousands of kilometres every year. Many ducks from Central ______ example, spend the winter in the wetlands of Sindh.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: Asia; for
Asia for
Asia, for
Asia: for
questions.e: 'For example' interrupts the clause and is followed by a comma, so a comma must also come before it. Leaving it out breaks the pair, and a semicolon or colon would cut the subject 'Many ducks from Central Asia' off from its verb.

questions.s:
The head coach—together with three of her senior ______ to Dubai a week before the tournament.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: players—flew
players, flew
players flew
players; flew
questions.e: The phrase 'together with three of her senior players' opens with a dash, so it must close with a dash before the verb 'flew'. A comma cannot close a dash, no punctuation leaves the phrase open, and a semicolon splits subject from verb.

questions.s:
Pakistan's longest river, the ______ in western Tibet before flowing south through Gilgit-Baltistan.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: Indus; rises
Indus rises
Indus—rises
Indus, rises
questions.e: The appositive 'the Indus' opens with a comma after 'river', so a comma must close it before the verb 'rises'. No punctuation leaves the pair open, a semicolon splits subject from verb, and a dash cannot close a comma-opened appositive.

questions.s:
In 2014, the Pakistani ______ won the Nobel Peace Prize at the age of seventeen.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: activist, Malala Yousafzai,
activist, Malala Yousafzai
activist Malala Yousafzai,
activist Malala Yousafzai
questions.e: There are many Pakistani activists, so the name is essential to say which one is meant; as a restrictive appositive it takes no commas. Paired commas would wrongly mark the name as extra information, and a single comma separates parts of the subject or the subject from its verb 'won'.

questions.s:
The factory, which employs nearly 2,000 people, shut down for a whole ______ many shops in the town lost business.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: month, consequently,
month consequently,
month; consequently,
month, consequently
questions.e: 'Consequently' links two independent clauses, so a semicolon goes before it and a comma after it. The commas inside the first clause do not change this: a comma or no punctuation before 'consequently' still makes a comma splice or a run-on.

questions.s:
The only ______ the two valleys is closed for four months every winter.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: road that connects,
road that connects
road, which connects
road, that connects
questions.e: 'That connects the two valleys' is a restrictive clause identifying the road, so it takes no commas. A comma before 'that' is wrong, a comma after 'connects' splits the verb from its object, and ', which connects' would need a closing comma before 'is'.

questions.s:
The first draft of the story was far too long; when the editor cut it by ______ plot became much easier to follow.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: half, the
half; the
half: the
half. The
questions.e: After the semicolon, the second part begins with the dependent clause 'when the editor cut it by half', which must be joined to its main clause with a comma. A semicolon or period would leave the 'when' clause as a fragment, and a colon must follow an independent clause.

questions.s:
Anyone who wishes to join next month's field trip to ______ hand in the signed consent form by Friday.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: Swat—must
Swat; must
Swat, must
Swat must
questions.e: The restrictive clause 'who wishes to join next month's field trip to Swat' is part of the subject 'Anyone ...', so no punctuation separates the subject from its verb 'must hand'. A comma, semicolon or dash would all split them.

questions.s:
Economists say ______ still too early to judge whether the new tax has achieved its aims.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: it's,
its'
it's
its
questions.e: The sense is 'it is still too early', so the contraction 'it's' is needed. 'Its' is the possessive, 'its'' is not a word, and a comma after 'it's' would separate the verb from 'still too early'.

questions.s:
The leaves of the old banyan tree outside the college library ______ a deep, glossy green after the monsoon rains.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: has turned
turn
turns
is turning
questions.e: The subject is the plural noun "leaves", so the verb must be the plural "turn". The phrase "of the old banyan tree" only describes the leaves; matching the verb to "tree" produces the singular forms, which are wrong here.

questions.s:
Each of the twelve students in Ms. Qureshi's chemistry class ______ a separate notebook for recording experiments.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: have kept
are keeping
keep
keeps
questions.e: "Each" is the subject and is always singular, so it takes the singular verb "keeps". The plural noun "students" sits inside the phrase "of the twelve students" and does not control the verb, so "keep", "are keeping" and "have kept" all fail.

questions.s:
Neither the principal nor the teachers ______ willing to move the final examinations to June.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: was
has been
is
are
questions.e: With "neither … nor", the verb agrees with the nearer subject. The nearer subject is the plural "teachers", so the plural "are" is needed; "is" would agree only with the farther noun, "principal".

questions.s:
The trunk of handwritten letters, which the museum bought from a family in Multan last year, ______ now on display in the east wing.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: are
is
have been
were
questions.e: The subject is the singular noun "trunk"; both "of handwritten letters" and the clause beginning "which" are interruptions. A singular subject needs "is", not a plural verb chosen to match "letters".

questions.s:
There ______ several reasons why the bridge over the Ravi was closed for repairs last month.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: is
was
are
has been
questions.e: In a sentence beginning with "There", the real subject follows the verb; here it is the plural "several reasons", so the verb must be "are". The singular options treat "There" as the subject, which it is not.

questions.s:
Playing chess against stronger opponents ______ young players learn to think several moves ahead.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: helps
have helped
help
are helping
questions.e: A gerund phrase used as a subject ("Playing chess against stronger opponents") is singular, so it takes "helps". The plural noun "opponents" is the object of a preposition inside the phrase and does not decide the verb.

questions.s:
At the bottom of the valley, beneath a thick layer of silt and stones, ______ the remains of a settlement that archaeologists date to the Bronze Age.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: lies
lie
is lying
has lain
questions.e: The sentence is inverted: the subject, "the remains of a settlement", comes after the verb. "Remains" is plural, so the plural "lie" is correct; the singular options agree wrongly with "silt and stones" or "settlement".

questions.s:
The report on water quality in the city's three largest lakes ______ that nitrate levels rose sharply between 2018 and 2022.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: have shown
show
shows
are showing
questions.e: The subject is the singular "report"; "on water quality in the city's three largest lakes" is a modifying phrase. A singular subject takes "shows", while the other options are plural forms that wrongly match "lakes".

questions.s:
Mathematics ______ the subject Hamza enjoys most, although he also does well in history.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: were
have been
is
are
questions.e: "Mathematics" ends in -s but is a singular noun naming one field of study, so it takes "is". The plural options mistake it for a plural noun.

questions.s:
The novelist, together with her two translators, ______ expected to attend the literature festival in Karachi next week.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: have been
are
were
is
questions.e: Phrases such as "together with her two translators" do not join subjects the way "and" does; the subject remains the singular "novelist", so the verb is "is". "Are" would be correct only if the sentence said "The novelist and her two translators".

questions.s:
Among the most surprising results of the survey ______ that more than half of the respondents had never visited a public library.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: was
have been
are
were
questions.e: The sentence is inverted, and its subject is the clause "that more than half of the respondents had never visited a public library"; a noun clause is singular, so the verb is "was". The plural "results" is inside the opening prepositional phrase and does not control the verb.

questions.s:
A number of volunteers from the university ______ helping to clean the beach at Clifton every Sunday.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: is
has been
are
was
questions.e: "A number of" means "several" and takes a plural verb, so "are" agrees with "volunteers". Writers often confuse it with "the number of", which is singular.

questions.s:
The number of students applying to the engineering course ______ grown every year since 2015.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: have
has
are
were
questions.e: "The number" names a single quantity and is singular, so the verb is "has". "Have" wrongly agrees with "students", which sits inside the phrase "of students applying".

questions.s:
Bilal and his sister ______ the same bus to school every morning.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: take
takes
has taken
is taking
questions.e: Two subjects joined by "and" make a plural subject, so the verb is "take". The singular forms would agree only with "sister".

questions.s:
Every painting and sculpture in the gallery ______ a small card beside it that names the artist.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: have
has
are having
were having
questions.e: When "every" introduces subjects joined by "and", each item is considered separately and the verb is singular, so "has" is correct. The pronoun "it" later in the sentence also signals a singular subject; "have" treats the pair as plural.

questions.s:
The professor's careful analysis of the poems, along with the many footnotes she added to the new edition, ______ the book valuable to students.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: are making
make
have made
makes
questions.e: The subject is the singular "analysis"; the phrase "along with the many footnotes…" is an interruption, not part of the subject. A singular subject needs "makes", while "make" wrongly agrees with "poems" or "footnotes".

questions.s:
Only one of the five proposals submitted by the design teams ______ the city's requirements for cost and safety.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: meets
meet
are meeting
have met
questions.e: The subject is "one", which is singular, so the verb is "meets". The plurals "proposals" and "teams" sit inside modifying phrases and do not control the verb.

questions.s:
The instructions printed on the back of the box ______ easy to follow, even for first-time users.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: was
is
are
has been
questions.e: The subject is the plural "instructions", so the verb is "are". The singular choices match "back" or "box", which are objects of prepositions.

questions.s:
The sound of the waves crashing against the rocks below the cliffs ______ visitors to the lighthouse long before they reach the top.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: have greeted
greet
greets
are greeting
questions.e: Strip away the modifiers and the core is "The sound … greets visitors"; "sound" is singular, so the verb is "greets". The plural forms are drawn in by "waves", "rocks" and "cliffs", none of which is the subject.

questions.s:
Either the Lahore office or the Islamabad office ______ responsible for processing the new visa applications.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: is
have been
were
are
questions.e: With "either … or", the verb agrees with the nearer subject, here the singular "Islamabad office", so "is" is correct. "Are" would treat the two offices as a combined plural subject, which "or" does not create.

questions.s:
The birds that nest along the shore of the lake ______ south every autumn.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: fly
flies
has flown
is flying
questions.e: The subject is the plural "birds"; "that nest along the shore of the lake" describes them. A plural subject takes "fly", while "flies" wrongly agrees with "shore" or "lake".

questions.s:
The economist argued that rising rents in the city's older districts, rather than higher fuel prices, ______ the main reason families are moving to the suburbs.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: has been
are
is
was
questions.e: The subject of the clause is the plural "rising rents"; "rather than higher fuel prices" is an interrupting phrase that does not add to the subject. A plural subject needs "are", so the singular forms fail.

questions.s:
The stack of exam papers on Mr. Rizvi's desk ______ taller every few minutes as students hand in their scripts.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: are growing
grow
have grown
grows
questions.e: The subject is the singular "stack", so the verb is "grows". "Grow" and the other plural forms wrongly agree with "papers", the object of the preposition "of".

questions.s:
Everyone in the two villages ______ access to the new health clinic.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: has
are having
were having
have
questions.e: Indefinite pronouns ending in -one, such as "everyone", are singular, so the verb is "has". The plural "villages" is inside a prepositional phrase and does not change that.

questions.s:
Some of the water stored in the reservoir ______ lost to evaporation during the hottest months.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: were
is
have been
are
questions.e: "Some" takes its number from the noun it refers to; here that noun is "water", which is uncountable and therefore singular, so "is" is correct. The plural forms would suit a countable plural such as "Some of the pipes".

questions.s:
"Tales of the Indus", a collection of short stories by a young writer from Sukkur, ______ won two national awards.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: are
were
have
has
questions.e: The title of a single book is singular even when its words are plural, so the verb is "has". "Have" mistakes the plural-looking title (or the word "stories") for the subject.

questions.s:
The tortoise pulled ______ head into its shell as soon as the children came near.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: their
it's
its
its'
questions.e: The possessive form of "it" is "its", with no apostrophe, and it matches the singular "tortoise". "It's" means "it is", "its'" is not a word, and "their" is plural.

questions.s:
After two years of fieldwork in Chitral, the scientists finally published ______ findings in an international journal.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: their
they're
its
there
questions.e: The antecedent, "scientists", is plural, so the plural possessive "their" is needed. "There" names a place, "they're" means "they are", and "its" is singular.

questions.s:
The prize money was divided equally between Sana and ______, since we had written the winning essay together.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: I
mine
me
myself
questions.e: After a preposition such as "between", a pronoun must be in the object case, so "me" is correct. "I" is a subject pronoun, a common error in pairs like this, and "myself" is reflexive, which needs "I" earlier in the clause as its subject.

questions.s:
My brother and ______ spent the summer volunteering at a clinic in Gilgit.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: myself
I
me
mine
questions.e: The pronoun is part of the subject of "spent", so it must be the subject form "I". Removing "My brother and" shows the test: "I spent the summer", not "me spent" or "myself spent".

questions.s:
The engineer ______ inspected the bridge last spring found several cracks in its supports.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: whom
which
whose
who
questions.e: The pronoun is the subject of "inspected", so the subject form "who" is needed. "Whom" is an object form, "which" is not used for people, and "whose" shows possession.

questions.s:
Rivers flowing out of the Himalayas carry huge amounts of silt and deposit ______ on the plains when the water slows down.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: them
its
they
it
questions.e: The pronoun stands for "silt", an uncountable singular noun, and it is the object of "deposit", so "it" is correct. "Them" wrongly refers back to "rivers" or "amounts", and "they" and "its" are the wrong case.

questions.s:
Before starting the project, the two researchers taught ______ to read the old Persian script in which the records were kept.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: itself
them
themselves
theirselves
questions.e: When the object refers to the same people as the subject, a reflexive pronoun is needed; for the plural "researchers" that is "themselves". "Theirselves" is not standard English, "itself" is singular, and "them" would suggest other people.

questions.s:
______ students in the final year were given an extra week to complete our research projects.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: We
Us
Ourselves
Our
questions.e: The pronoun begins the subject of "were given", so the subject form "We" is correct; dropping "students" shows this ("We were given"). "Us" is an object form and "Ourselves" is reflexive.

questions.s:
The author, ______ latest novel is set in the old city of Peshawar, will speak at the book fair on Saturday.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: who
who's
whose
whom
questions.e: "Whose" is the possessive relative pronoun: the novel belongs to the author. "Who's" is a contraction of "who is", which makes no sense before "latest novel".

questions.s:
The old city walls are still standing, although ______ were badly damaged by an earthquake in the nineteenth century.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: its
they
it
this
questions.e: The pronoun refers to the plural "walls" and is the subject of "were", so "they" is correct. "It" and "this" are singular and do not agree with "walls" or with "were".

questions.s:
The violinist and the pianist rehearsed separately for weeks, but on the night of the concert ______ performance together was flawless.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: their
there
its
they're
questions.e: The possessive refers to two people, "the violinist and the pianist", so the plural possessive "their" is needed. "Its" is singular, "there" is an adverb of place and "they're" means "they are".

questions.s:
Since 2019, the small bakery on Mall Road ______ fresh naan for the hostel every morning.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: supplies
has supplied
will supply
supplied
questions.e: "Since 2019" describes an action that began in the past and continues to the present, which calls for the present perfect "has supplied". The simple present and simple past do not fit an expression of time beginning with "since".

questions.s:
By the time the fire engines reached the warehouse, the flames ______ to the second floor.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: will spread
have spread
spread
had spread
questions.e: "By the time" with a past event ("reached") requires the past perfect for the action completed before it, so "had spread" is correct. "Have spread" links the action to the present, and "will spread" is future.

questions.s:
Last year, the botanists ______ more than 300 seed samples from the forests of Swat.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: will collect
have collected
collect
collected
questions.e: "Last year" marks a finished past time, so the simple past "collected" is correct. The present perfect "have collected" cannot be used with a finished time expression like "last year".

questions.s:
Next March, Ayesha ______ at the children's hospital for exactly ten years.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: worked
will have worked
has worked
works
questions.e: The sentence describes a period that will be complete at a future point ("Next March"), so the future perfect "will have worked" is needed. "Has worked" measures time up to now, not up to a future date.

questions.s:
The children had ______ their bicycles all the way to the lake and back before lunch.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: ridden
rode
ride
riding
questions.e: After the helping verb "had", the past participle is required, and the past participle of "ride" is "ridden". "Rode" is the simple past form and cannot follow "had".

questions.s:
The well behind the old mosque had ______ dry by the end of the summer, so villagers carried water from the river.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: went
gone
go
going
questions.e: "Had" must be followed by a past participle; the participle of "go" is "gone". "Went" is the simple past, so "had went" is a common but non-standard form.

questions.s:
After the long climb to the fort, the tired hikers ______ down in the shade of a tree to rest.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: lay
laid
lied
layed
questions.e: The verb meaning "to recline" is "lie", and its past tense is "lay". "Laid" is the past of "lay" (to put something down), which needs an object; "lied" means told an untruth, and "layed" is not a word.

questions.s:
When the train finally pulled into Rawalpindi station, Nida grabbed her bag and ______ onto the crowded platform.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: will step
has stepped
stepped
steps
questions.e: The sentence narrates finished events in the simple past ("pulled", "grabbed"), so the verb paired with "grabbed" should also be past: "stepped". The other forms switch tense without reason.

questions.s:
If the bridge had been inspected earlier, the engineers ______ the cracks before they grew so large.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: would find
will find
had found
would have found
questions.e: This is a condition about the past that did not happen ("had been inspected"), so the result clause needs "would have" plus a past participle. "Would find" refers to the present or future, and "had found" is not a result form.

questions.s:
If the rain ______ until tomorrow afternoon, the cricket final will be moved to Saturday.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: will continue
would continue
continued
continues
questions.e: In a condition about the future, the "if" clause takes the simple present and the main clause takes "will", so "continues" is correct. Putting "will" in the "if" clause is a common error, and "continued" or "would continue" belong to unreal conditions, not to a sentence with "will be moved".

questions.s:
Pure water ______ at 100 °C at sea level, but on a high mountain it boils at a lower temperature.
