Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: was boiling
had boiled
boils
boiled
questions.e: A general scientific fact is expressed in the simple present, and the second clause ("it boils") confirms this, so "boils" is correct. The past forms present a permanent truth as a single past event.

questions.s:
When the archaeologists entered the tomb, they discovered that someone ______ it centuries earlier.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: had opened
will open
opens
has opened
questions.e: The opening of the tomb happened before the past moment of discovery, so the past perfect "had opened" is required. "Has opened" connects the action to the present, which clashes with "centuries earlier".

questions.s:
The concert had already ______ by the time we found our seats in the hall.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: beginning
begun
began
begin
questions.e: After "had", the past participle is needed, and the participle of "begin" is "begun". "Began" is the simple past form, so "had began" is incorrect.

questions.s:
The new traffic rules, which ______ into effect last week, require all buses to stop only at marked points.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: come
came
have come
will come
questions.e: "Last week" marks a finished past time, so the simple past "came" is required. The present perfect "have come" cannot be combined with a specific past time such as "last week".

questions.s:
Visitors to the archive must ______ their bags and coats at the entrance.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: to leave
left
leaving
leave
questions.e: A modal verb such as "must" is always followed by the base form of a verb, so "leave" is correct. "Must left", "must leaving" and "must to leave" are not standard.

questions.s:
The students are looking forward to ______ the new observatory in the hills next month.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: have visited
visit
visiting
visited
questions.e: In "look forward to", the word "to" is a preposition, so it is followed by a gerund: "visiting". Treating "to" as part of an infinitive leads to the error "look forward to visit".

questions.s:
Ahmed told me yesterday that he ______ the novel twice before he saw the film.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: will read
has read
reads
had read
questions.e: The reading took place before another past event ("he saw the film"), and the whole report is in the past ("told"), so the past perfect "had read" is correct. "Has read" and "reads" anchor the action in the present.

questions.s:
The laboratory ______ its first clinical trial three years ago with only four researchers.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: had begun
began
has begun
begins
questions.e: "Three years ago" names a finished time in the past, which requires the simple past "began". The present perfect "has begun" cannot be used with "ago", and the past perfect "had begun" needs a later past event to refer back from.

questions.s:
Historians believe that the fort ______ in the sixteenth century, although some of its walls are much older.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: had built
has been built
is built
was built
questions.e: The fort received the action of building, so a passive verb is needed, and the time ("in the sixteenth century") is finished, so the simple past passive "was built" is correct. "Had built" is active and would mean the fort built something.

questions.s:
Each spring, the almond trees in the valley ______, and visitors travel from far away to see them.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: blossom
had blossomed
blossomed
have blossomed
questions.e: "Each spring" describes a repeated, habitual event, and the parallel clause uses the present ("visitors travel"), so the simple present "blossom" fits. The past forms clash with "travel".

questions.s:
The study, which ______ over a period of six years, found that children who read aloud every day developed larger vocabularies.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: was conducted
is conducting
has conducted
conducted
questions.e: A study does not conduct anything; it is conducted by researchers, so the passive "was conducted" is needed. The active forms "conducted", "has conducted" and "is conducting" would wrongly make the study the doer and leave the verb without an object.

questions.s:
The letter, written in 1947 and ______ for decades in a family trunk, was donated to the city archive last month.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: hid
hiding
hidden
was hidden
questions.e: The blank is joined by "and" to the past participle "written", so it must also be a past participle: "hidden". "Was hidden" adds a second main verb inside the phrase, and "hid" and "hiding" break the parallel form and wrongly make the letter the doer.

questions.s:
Of the two routes to Naran, the road through the valley is ______, although the mountain road offers better views.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: safest
the safest
the safer
the most safe
questions.e: When exactly two things are compared, the comparative form ("safer") is used, so "the safer" is correct. "Safest" and "most safe" are superlatives, which are used for three or more things.

questions.s:
Before the final match, all eleven ______ shirts were washed and pressed by the team's kit manager.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: players's
players'
player's
players
questions.e: The shirts belong to eleven players, so the plural possessive is needed: add an apostrophe after the plural -s to get "players'". "Player's" is singular possessive, and "players" is a plain plural that shows no ownership.

questions.s:
After the storm, ______ only bridge to the main road was rebuilt with money from the district. The village had been cut off for a week.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: the villages
the village's
the villages'
the village
questions.e: The second sentence makes clear that there is one village, so the singular possessive "the village's" is correct. "The villages'" is plural possessive, and "the villages" and "the village" show no possession.

questions.s:
The playground was covered with the ______ toys after the school's annual fun fair.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: children's
children
childrens
childrens'
questions.e: "Children" is already plural, so its possessive is formed by adding 's: "children's". "Childrens" is not a word, so "childrens'" and "childrens" are both incorrect.

questions.s:
Zainab borrowed her only ______ car to drive her grandparents to the airport.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: brothers'
brothers
brother's
brothers's
questions.e: "Only" shows that she has one brother, so the singular possessive "brother's" is correct. "Brothers'" would mean the car belongs to several brothers, and "brothers" is a plain plural.

questions.s:
The conference in Hyderabad focused on ______ access to higher education in rural Sindh.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: women
womens
women's
womens'
questions.e: "Women" is an irregular plural, so its possessive adds 's: "women's". "Womens" does not exist in standard English, which rules out "womens'" and "womens".

questions.s:
The aurora, seen in the far north and far south, is one of the most striking natural ______ on Earth.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: phenomena's
phenomenons
phenomenon
phenomena
questions.e: "One of the most striking natural…" requires a plural noun, and the plural of "phenomenon" is "phenomena". "Phenomenon" is singular, "phenomenons" is non-standard, and "phenomena's" is a possessive with nothing to possess.

questions.s:
The judges used three ______ to score each essay: clarity, originality and accuracy.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: criteria's
criteria
criterion
criterions
questions.e: "Three" calls for a plural, and the plural of "criterion" is "criteria". "Criterion" is singular, "criterions" is non-standard, and "criteria's" is a possessive form.

questions.s:
In the hills above Murree, two ______ worth of rain fell in a single afternoon.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: weeks's
weeks
week's
weeks'
questions.e: In expressions of time and amount such as "two weeks' worth", the time word takes a possessive; since "two weeks" is plural, the apostrophe follows the s. "Week's" is singular and does not match "two".

questions.s:
For three generations, ______ dairy farm has supplied the town with fresh milk; Mr. and Mrs. Khan now run it with their four children.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: the Khan's
the Khans's
the Khans'
the Khans
questions.e: The farm belongs to the Khan family, referred to as "the Khans"; the plural possessive of a family name adds an apostrophe after the s: "the Khans'". "The Khan's" refers to a single person, and "the Khans" shows no possession.

questions.s:
Several new ______ have opened along the canal road this year, each selling bread and sweets.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: bakeries
bakery's
bakerys
bakeries'
questions.e: The sentence needs a plain plural subject for "have opened", and nouns ending in a consonant plus -y change the y to -ies: "bakeries". The apostrophe forms are possessives, and "bakerys" is misspelled.

questions.s:
Our measurements matched ______ almost exactly, even though the two groups used different equipment.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: there's
theirs
theirs'
their's
questions.e: The possessive pronoun that stands alone is "theirs", which never takes an apostrophe. "There's" means "there is", and "their's" and "theirs'" are not standard forms.

questions.s:
After speed cameras were installed, there were ______ accidents on the motorway than in any previous year.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: little
less
fewer
lesser
questions.e: "Accidents" is a countable plural noun, so it takes "fewer"; "less" is used with uncountable nouns such as "traffic" or "noise". "Lesser" and "little" do not form a comparison with "than" here.

questions.s:
By the end of the exam, the students had so little time left that they ______ answer the final question.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: could not hardly
hardly couldn't
couldn't hardly
could hardly
questions.e: "Hardly" is already negative in meaning, so it must not be combined with "not"; "could hardly" is correct. The other choices create double negatives.

questions.s:
Walking along the beach at sunset, ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: Imran noticed a starfish stranded on the wet sand.
the wet sand had a starfish stranded on it that Imran saw.
a starfish stranded on the wet sand caught Imran's eye.
a stranded starfish was noticed by Imran on the wet sand.
questions.e: An introductory modifier must be followed by the noun it describes. Imran is the one walking, so the main clause must begin with "Imran"; the other choices make the starfish or the sand do the walking.

questions.s:
Known for its carved wooden balconies and narrow lanes, ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: there are many students of architecture who visit Peshawar's old city.
students of architecture often visit the old city of Peshawar.
many students of architecture are attracted to the old city of Peshawar.
the old city of Peshawar attracts many students of architecture.
questions.e: The phrase "Known for its carved wooden balconies…" describes the old city, so "the old city of Peshawar" must come right after the comma. The other choices place "students" or "there" there, so the students seem to have the balconies.

questions.s:
After finishing her first marathon, ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: Sara's legs ached for two days.
it took Sara two days to walk normally again.
a deep ache stayed in Sara's legs for two days.
Sara could barely walk for two days.
questions.e: Sara finished the marathon, so "Sara" must be the subject immediately after the modifier. In "Sara's legs ached", the subject is "legs", and the legs did not finish the marathon; "it" and "a deep ache" fail the same way.

questions.s:
A gifted mathematician from Tehran, ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: it was in 2014 that Maryam Mirzakhani became the first woman to win the Fields Medal.
Maryam Mirzakhani became the first woman to win the Fields Medal in 2014.
the Fields Medal went to Maryam Mirzakhani in 2014, making her its first female winner.
Maryam Mirzakhani's work earned her the Fields Medal in 2014.
questions.e: The appositive "A gifted mathematician from Tehran" must sit next to the person it renames, so the main clause must open with "Maryam Mirzakhani". In the possessive choice the subject is "work", and the other choices begin with "the Fields Medal" or "it".

questions.s:
To qualify for the school relay team, ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: under thirteen seconds is the time needed to run the sprint.
running the sprint in under thirteen seconds is required.
a runner must run the sprint in under thirteen seconds.
the qualifying time for the sprint is under thirteen seconds.
questions.e: An introductory infinitive phrase must be followed by the person who performs the action; only a runner can qualify for the team. The other choices make an action, a time or a requirement qualify for the team.

questions.s:
As a child growing up in Quetta, ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: the writer spent long winter evenings reading by the fire.
long winter evenings were spent by the writer reading by the fire.
the writer's winter evenings were spent reading by the fire.
reading by the fire filled the writer's long winter evenings.
questions.e: "As a child growing up in Quetta" describes the writer, so "the writer" must be the subject. The possessive "the writer's" is a trap: the subject of that clause is "evenings", which did not grow up in Quetta.

questions.s:
Exhausted after the twelve-hour journey from Skardu, ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: sleep came to the climbers as soon as they reached the hotel.
the climbers fell asleep as soon as they reached the hotel.
the hotel beds were a welcome sight for the climbers.
the climbers' first act at the hotel was to fall asleep.
questions.e: The climbers were exhausted, so "the climbers" must follow the introductory phrase. The other choices make sleep, the beds or the climbers' "first act" exhausted.

questions.s:
Unlike most birds, ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: penguins' wings work as flippers rather than for flight.
the wings of penguins are used for swimming rather than flying.
penguins cannot fly but are excellent swimmers.
flying is impossible for penguins, which swim instead.
questions.e: "Unlike most birds" sets up a comparison with another kind of bird, so the subject must be "penguins". Comparing birds with "the wings of penguins", "flying" or "penguins' wings" is illogical.

questions.s:
Because it lies in the path of the monsoon, Murree receives far more rain each year than ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: Multan's rainfall is.
Multan's does.
that of Multan.
Multan does.
questions.e: The sentence compares two places that receive rain, so the comparison needs a place and a matching verb: "than Multan does". "That of Multan" and "Multan's does" have no noun for "that" or "Multan's" to stand for, and "Multan's rainfall is" compares a city with rainfall.

questions.s:
Like her mentor, ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: the poet Hira Baig writes verse that blends Urdu and Punjabi.
Hira Baig's poems blend Urdu and Punjabi.
blending Urdu and Punjabi is typical of Hira Baig's poetry.
the poetry of Hira Baig blends Urdu and Punjabi.
questions.e: "Like her mentor" compares a person with a person, so the subject must be the poet herself. The other choices compare the mentor with poetry, poems or an action, which is an illogical comparison.

questions.s:
Completed in 1673 on the orders of the emperor Aurangzeb, ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: the builders placed the Badshahi Mosque opposite the Lahore Fort.
the Badshahi Mosque stands opposite the Lahore Fort.
visitors to the Badshahi Mosque can see the Lahore Fort across the square.
there is a clear view of the Lahore Fort from the Badshahi Mosque.
questions.e: The introductory phrase describes the mosque, so "the Badshahi Mosque" must be the subject that follows it. The other choices make visitors, "there" or the builders the thing completed in 1673.

questions.s:
Having studied harvest records from forty farms for two seasons, ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: the team concluded that the new seed variety raised wheat yields.
it became clear to the team that the new seed variety raised wheat yields.
the conclusion of the team was that the new seed variety raised wheat yields.
the new seed variety was shown by the team to raise wheat yields.
questions.e: The team did the studying, so "the team" must be the subject right after the modifier. In the other choices the subject is "the conclusion", "it" or "the new seed variety", none of which studied the records.

questions.s:
While searching through old newspapers in the city archive, ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: a letter from 1919 was discovered by a historian.
a forgotten letter from 1919 caught a historian's attention.
the discovery of a forgotten 1919 letter was made by a historian.
a historian came across a forgotten letter from 1919.
questions.e: The person searching must be the subject after "While searching…", so "a historian" must come first. The other choices make the letter or "the discovery" do the searching.

questions.s:
Founded in 1984 by a group of retired teachers, ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: more than 2,000 students now attend the school.
today there are more than 2,000 students at the school.
the school's students now number more than 2,000.
the school now has more than 2,000 students.
questions.e: The school was founded, so "the school" must be the subject immediately after the phrase. The possessive "the school's students" makes "students" the subject, and students were not founded in 1984.

questions.s:
Using a simple telescope that he had built himself, ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: Galileo observed four of Jupiter's moons in 1610.
the first observation of Jupiter's moons was made by Galileo in 1610.
Jupiter's four largest moons were first seen by Galileo in 1610.
four of Jupiter's moons were observed by Galileo in 1610.
questions.e: Galileo used the telescope, so "Galileo" must be the subject after the opening phrase. The other choices make moons or an observation use the telescope.

questions.s:
Originally written in Persian, ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: a scholar translated the poem into Urdu in the nineteenth century.
the poem was translated into Urdu in the nineteenth century.
an Urdu translation of the poem appeared in the nineteenth century.
Urdu readers first read the poem in the nineteenth century.
questions.e: The poem was written in Persian, so "the poem" must follow the modifier. The other choices make a scholar, a translation or readers "originally written in Persian".

questions.s:
Unlike the mountains of the north, ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: the plains of Punjab are flat and fertile.
Punjab has plains that are flat and fertile.
there are flat and fertile plains in Punjab.
Punjab's farmers work on flat, fertile plains.
questions.e: The comparison must be between like things: mountains and plains. The other choices compare the mountains with Punjab, with "there", or with farmers.

questions.s:
On weekends, Hassan enjoys reading, swimming and ______ meals for his family.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: to cook
cook
cooking
he cooks
questions.e: Items in a list should share the same grammatical form. "Reading" and "swimming" are gerunds, so the third item must be "cooking"; "to cook" and "he cooks" break the pattern.

questions.s:
The new library on campus is spacious, well lit and ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: quiet.
quietly.
has a quiet atmosphere.
it is quiet.
questions.e: The list follows "is" and contains adjectives ("spacious", "well lit"), so the last item must also be an adjective: "quiet". "Quietly" is an adverb, and the other two choices add a new verb.

questions.s:
The goals of the recycling project are to reduce waste, to save energy and ______ small local businesses.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: supporting
supports
the support of
to support
questions.e: The list repeats "to" before each item ("to reduce", "to save"), so the third item must be "to support". A gerund, a noun phrase or a present-tense verb breaks the parallel structure.

questions.s:
The coach told the players that they should arrive early, warm up properly and ______ during team talks.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: listening carefully
to listen carefully
listen carefully
they listened carefully
questions.e: All three actions follow "should", so each must be a base verb: "arrive", "warm up" and "listen". Adding "to", "-ing" or a new subject breaks the series.

questions.s:
Becoming fluent in a new language depends less on studying grammar rules than ______ with native speakers every day.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: to talk
when you talk
talking
on talking
questions.e: The comparison "less on … than …" needs the same structure on both sides, so "on studying" must be matched by "on talking". Without "on", the sentence compares a prepositional phrase with a bare gerund.

questions.s:
The food festival in Lahore was praised not only for its music but also ______ the variety of its food stalls.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: because of
for
by
due to
questions.e: With "not only … but also", the words after each part must match. The first part is "for its music", so the second must also begin with "for"; the other prepositions break the pairing.

questions.s:
The trainer advised Saima to drink more water, to sleep at least seven hours a night and ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: she should avoid sugary snacks.
to avoid sugary snacks.
avoiding sugary snacks.
that sugary snacks be avoided.
questions.e: The list after "advised Saima" uses infinitives ("to drink", "to sleep"), so the last item must be "to avoid". A gerund or a clause does not match the other two items.

questions.s:
The researchers found that students who read for pleasure scored higher in vocabulary tests, wrote more fluently and ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: their confidence in class discussions was higher.
having more confidence in class discussions.
were more confident in class discussions.
more confidence in class discussions.
questions.e: The three items share the subject "students who read for pleasure" and must all be past-tense verb phrases: "scored", "wrote" and "were". The other choices offer a participle, a noun phrase or a new clause with its own subject.

questions.s:
The museum's guided tour includes a walk through the gardens, a visit to the old printing press and ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: to hear the head curator.
a talk by the head curator.
listening to the head curator.
the head curator gives a talk.
questions.e: Each item in the list is a noun phrase beginning with "a" ("a walk", "a visit"), so the last one should be "a talk by the head curator". The other choices switch to a gerund, a clause or an infinitive.

questions.s:
For many students, studying early in the morning is more effective than ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: the study late at night.
to study late at night.
they study late at night.
studying late at night.
questions.e: A comparison with "than" should set like forms side by side; "studying early in the morning" is a gerund phrase, so it must be compared with "studying late at night". The infinitive and the clause are not parallel.

questions.s:
The engineer's report recommended widening the main road, adding a cycle lane and ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: to lower the speed limit.
the speed limit should be lowered.
lowering the speed limit.
lower speed limits.
questions.e: "Recommended" is followed by a series of gerund phrases ("widening", "adding"), so the third item must be "lowering the speed limit". An infinitive, a clause or a plain noun phrase breaks the parallel form.

questions.s:
The city's transport plan aims to make buses cheaper, faster and ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: more reliable.
it more reliable.
more reliability.
reliably.
questions.e: The words after "make buses" are comparative adjectives ("cheaper", "faster"), so the third must be "more reliable". "More reliability" is a noun, "reliably" is an adverb, and "it more reliable" adds an extra pronoun.

questions.s:
What impressed the judges most was not the size of the robot but ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: quick in its responses.
it responded quickly.
the speed of its responses.
responding quickly.
questions.e: With "not … but", both parts must have the same form. "The size of the robot" is a noun phrase, so it must be matched by "the speed of its responses"; a gerund, a clause or an adjective phrase does not pair with it.

questions.s:
The keys to the chemistry laboratory ______ kept in a locked box in the staff room.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: is
has been
was
are
questions.e: The subject is the plural "keys"; "to the chemistry laboratory" only describes them. A plural subject needs "are", while the singular options wrongly agree with "laboratory".

questions.s:
The scholar to ______ the manuscript was sent replied within a week with a full translation.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: which
whom
who
whose
questions.e: The pronoun is the object of the preposition "to", so the object form "whom" is required. "Who" is a subject form, "which" is not used for people, and "whose" shows possession.

questions.s:
After testing the rock in the hills, the engineers decided ______ the opening of the tunnel by six months.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: to delay
delaying
delayed
delay
questions.e: The verb "decide" is followed by an infinitive, so "decided to delay" is correct. "Decided delaying", "decided delay" and "decided delayed" are not standard.

questions.s:
If ______ planning to visit the Lahore Fort, arrive early to avoid the afternoon crowds.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: you're
you'r
youre
your
questions.e: The sentence needs a subject and a verb ("you are planning"), and the contraction of "you are" is "you're". "Your" is a possessive, and the other two are misspellings.

questions.s:
The quality of the photographs taken by the two drones ______ surprisingly high for such small cameras.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: are
is
have been
were
questions.e: The subject is the singular "quality"; "of the photographs taken by the two drones" is a modifying phrase. A singular subject takes "is", so the plural forms that match "photographs" or "drones" are wrong.

questions.s:
Had the ferry left port on time, the passengers ______ Gwadar before dark.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: would have reached
would reach
had reached
will reach
questions.e: "Had the ferry left…" is an inverted form of "If the ferry had left", a condition about the past that did not happen. The result therefore needs "would have" plus a past participle; "would reach" refers to the present or future.

questions.s:
In Hunza, many apricot farmers dry ______ fruit on flat rooftops during the summer.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: they're
there
their
its
questions.e: The antecedent is the plural "farmers", so the plural possessive "their" is correct. "There" is an adverb, "they're" means "they are", and "its" is singular.

questions.s:
Determined to finish before dark, ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: the volunteers planted the last row of saplings by six o'clock.
six o'clock saw the volunteers plant the last row of saplings.
the planting of the last row of saplings ended by six o'clock.
the last row of saplings was planted by the volunteers by six o'clock.
questions.e: Only people can be determined, so "the volunteers" must be the subject after the opening phrase. The other choices make the saplings, the planting or the time determined.

questions.s:
Hidden among the reeds at the edge of the lake ______ a small wooden boat and two oars.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: was
has been
is
were
questions.e: The sentence is inverted; its subject, "a small wooden boat and two oars", comes after the verb. Two nouns joined by "and" form a plural subject, so the verb is "were"; "was" agrees only with "boat".

questions.s:
Please ______ the boxes of books on the table by the door so that the volunteers can sort them.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: setting
set
sat
sit
questions.e: "Set" means "to place something" and takes an object, here "the boxes". "Sit" means "to be seated" and cannot take an object, "sat" is its past form, and "setting" cannot follow "Please" as a command.

questions.s:
Over the past decade, the salaries of nurses in the region have risen faster than ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: teachers have.
teachers.
those of teachers.
that of teachers.
questions.e: The sentence compares salaries with salaries, so a pronoun must stand for "salaries"; since the noun is plural, "those of teachers" is correct. "Teachers" and "teachers have" compare salaries with people, and "that" is singular.

questions.s:
The results of the national science competition will ______ on Friday morning.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: announcing
announced
been announced
be announced
questions.e: Results do not announce anything; they are announced, so a passive form is needed, and after "will" the passive is "be announced". "Will announced" and "will been announced" are not standard, and "will announcing" is not a verb form.

questions.s:
The new forest policy is designed both to protect old trees and ______ for people in nearby villages.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: it creates jobs
to create jobs
the creation of jobs
creating jobs
questions.e: With "both … and", the two parts must match: "to protect" is an infinitive, so the second part must be "to create jobs". A gerund, a noun phrase or a clause breaks the pairing.

questions.s:
Karachi is the largest city in the country: its population is greater than ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: that of any other city in Pakistan.
those of any other city in Pakistan.
any other city in Pakistan.
that of any city in Pakistan.
questions.e: A population must be compared with another population, so "that of" is needed, and "other" is required because Karachi is itself a city in Pakistan. "Any other city" compares a population with a city, and "those" is plural.

questions.s:
Saad was cooking dinner in the kitchen when the power suddenly ______.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: goes out
has gone out
went out
will go out
questions.e: A past continuous action ("was cooking") interrupted by a single event takes the simple past for that event, so "went out" is correct. The present and future forms do not fit a past narrative.

questions.s:
After the flood, a large ______ of sand and mud had to be cleared from the main road.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: few
number
amount
many
questions.e: "Sand and mud" are uncountable nouns, so they are measured with "amount". "Number" is used with countable plurals such as "rocks", and "many" and "few" are not nouns here.

questions.s:
Because the two sisters had studied together for months, the teacher was not surprised that ______ answers were almost identical.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: her
its
there
their
questions.e: The answers belong to both sisters, so the plural possessive "their" is needed. "Her" refers to one person only and "its" is used for things, while "there" is an adverb of place.

questions.s:
The blue cups on the top shelf of the cupboard ______ to my grandmother.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: belongs
belong
has belonged
is belonging
questions.e: The subject is the plural "cups", so the verb is "belong". The singular forms wrongly agree with "shelf" or "cupboard", which are objects of prepositions.

questions.s:
Neither the manager nor her assistants ______ aware that the meeting had been moved to Tuesday.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: has been
is
was
were
questions.e: With "neither … nor", the verb agrees with the nearer subject, the plural "assistants", so "were" is correct. "Was" would agree only with the farther subject, "manager".

questions.s:
Reading the comments under online news articles rarely ______ anyone's mood.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: improve
have improved
are improving
improves
questions.e: A gerund phrase used as a subject ("Reading the comments under online news articles") is singular, so the verb is "improves". The plural forms wrongly agree with "comments" or "articles", which sit inside the phrase.

questions.s:
Beside the entrance to the old library ______ two stone lions carved in the 1890s.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: stand
has stood
stands
is standing
questions.e: The sentence is inverted: the subject, "two stone lions", follows the verb. A plural subject needs "stand"; the singular forms agree wrongly with "entrance" or "library".

questions.s:
Several of the participants in the sleep study ______ been contacted again for a follow-up interview.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: have
has
is
was
questions.e: "Several" is always plural, so it takes "have". The singular forms ignore that "several" refers to more than one participant.

questions.s:
Before the match, the coach asked Fahad and ______ to lead the warm-up.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: myself
me
I
mine
questions.e: The pronoun is an object of "asked", so the object form "me" is needed; dropping "Fahad and" shows this ("asked me"). "I" is a subject form, and "myself" needs "I" as the subject of the clause.

questions.s:
At the end of the evening, the award was presented to ______ volunteers who had run the fundraiser.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: our
ourselves
us
we
questions.e: After the preposition "to", the object form is needed, so "us volunteers" is correct; removing "volunteers" gives "presented to us". "We" is a subject form, and "ourselves" needs "we" as the subject.

questions.s:
The new hospital wing has ______ own backup generator in case of power cuts.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: its'
its
their
it's
questions.e: The possessive form of "it" is "its", without an apostrophe, and it matches the singular "wing". "It's" means "it is" or "it has", and "its'" does not exist.

questions.s:
The scholars ______ translated the old diaries spent four years on the project.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: who
whose
which
whom
questions.e: The pronoun is the subject of "translated" and refers to people, so "who" is correct. "Which" is used for things, "whom" is an object form, and "whose" is possessive.

questions.s:
When the students handed in their forms, the clerk checked ______ carefully for errors.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: its
they
them
it
questions.e: The pronoun refers to the plural "forms" and is the object of "checked", so "them" is correct. "It" is singular and "they" is a subject form.

questions.s:
By the end of the summer camp, every child had ______ across the pool at least once.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: swam
swimmed
swum
swim
questions.e: After "had", the past participle is required, and the participle of "swim" is "swum". "Swam" is the simple past, and "swimmed" is not a standard form.

questions.s:
The scientist set the soil samples on the bench and let them ______ undisturbed for an hour.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: lain
lay
lie
laid
questions.e: "Let" is followed by the base form of a verb, and the verb meaning "to remain in a flat position" is "lie". "Lay" means "to put something down" and needs an object, while "laid" and "lain" are participles that cannot follow "let them".

questions.s:
For the past ten years, the clinic ______ free eye tests to schoolchildren in the district.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: offered
will offer
offers
has offered
questions.e: "For the past ten years" describes a period that runs up to now, so the present perfect "has offered" is required. The simple past would suggest the period has ended, and the simple present does not express duration.

questions.s:
If Bilal ______ more free time, he would learn to play the sitar.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: would have
had
has
will have
questions.e: This is an unreal present condition, shown by "would learn" in the main clause, so the "if" clause takes the simple past, "had". "Has" and "will have" belong to real conditions, and "would" does not go in the "if" clause.

questions.s:
Yesterday, the bus from Murree ______ twenty minutes late because of the heavy rain.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: arrived
arrives
has arrived
will arrive
questions.e: "Yesterday" marks a finished past time, so the simple past "arrived" is correct. The present perfect cannot be used with "yesterday".

questions.s:
The pottery, shaped by hand and ______ in a wood-fired kiln, is sold at the Sunday market.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: baking
baked
was baked
bakes
questions.e: The blank is joined by "and" to the past participle "shaped", so it must also be a past participle: "baked". "Was baked" adds a second main verb inside the interrupting phrase, and "bakes" and "baking" break the parallel form.

questions.s:
During the tour, the children were told not ______ the paintings in the gallery.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: touch
touching
touched
to touch
questions.e: "Told" is followed by an infinitive ("told someone to do something"), and the negative form is "not to touch". The other forms do not fit after "were told not".

questions.s:
Before the parade, the two ______ manes were braided with red ribbons.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: horses'
horses's
horse's
horses
questions.e: The manes belong to two horses, so the plural possessive "horses'" is needed. "Horse's" is singular, and "horses" shows no possession.

questions.s:
Dr. Malik is an old friend of ______, so I asked her to read my essay.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: mine
me
my
mine's
questions.e: After "a friend of", English uses the independent possessive pronoun: "a friend of mine". "My" must be followed by a noun, "me" shows no possession, and "mine's" is not a word.

questions.s:
______ been raining in Islamabad since early morning, so the match may be called off.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: Its has
Its
It's
Its'
questions.e: The sentence needs a subject and a helping verb ("It has been raining"), and "It's" is the contraction of "it has". "Its" is a possessive, "Its'" does not exist, and "Its has" uses the possessive where a subject is needed.

questions.s:
The museum's new gallery displays nine ______ of fish found only in the Indus river system.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: species'
specie
specieses
species
questions.e: "Species" has the same form in the singular and the plural, so "nine species" is correct. "Specie" is a different word meaning coins, "specieses" does not exist, and "species'" is possessive.

questions.s:
As the oldest of five siblings, ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: the younger brothers often got homework help from Kamran.
Kamran's evenings were often spent helping his younger brothers.
Kamran often helped his younger brothers with their homework.
helping his younger brothers with homework was often Kamran's job.
questions.e: "As the oldest of five siblings" describes Kamran, so "Kamran" must be the subject. In "Kamran's evenings" the subject is "evenings", and the other choices make an action or the younger brothers the oldest sibling.

questions.s:
Reaching the summit just after dawn, ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: the sun rose over the glacier as the climbers watched.
the view of the glacier at sunrise amazed the climbers.
the climbers watched the sun rise over the glacier.
the climbers' cameras captured the sunrise over the glacier.
questions.e: The climbers reached the summit, so "the climbers" must follow the opening phrase. The other choices make the sun, the view or the cameras reach the summit.

questions.s:
Rich in iron and protein, ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: many Pakistani families eat lentils every day.
Pakistani cooks use lentils in many dishes.
there are lentil dishes in many Pakistani homes.
lentils are a daily food in many Pakistani homes.
questions.e: The phrase "Rich in iron and protein" describes lentils, so "lentils" must be the subject after the comma. The other choices make families, cooks or "there" rich in iron and protein.

questions.s:
According to the reviewers, the battery of the new phone lasts much longer than ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: the older model does.
those of the older model.
the older model.
that of the older model.
questions.e: The battery must be compared with another battery, so "that of the older model" is needed; "that" is singular to match "battery". "The older model" and "the older model does" compare a battery with a phone, and "those" is plural.

questions.s:
The scholarship money can be spent either on tuition fees or ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: buying books.
on books.
to buy books.
books can be bought.
questions.e: With "either … or", the two parts must match. "On tuition fees" is a prepositional phrase, so the second part must also be one: "on books".

questions.s:
Bilal enjoys hiking in the summer and ______ in the winter.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: skiing
to ski
ski
skied
questions.e: Both activities are objects of "enjoys", which takes gerunds, so "hiking" must be matched by "skiing". "Enjoys … to ski" is not standard, and "ski" and "skied" are not parallel.

questions.s:
The workshop teaches students how to plan an experiment, how to record data and ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: how to present their results.
they present their results.
presenting their results.
the presentation of results.
questions.e: Each item in the series is a phrase beginning with "how to", so the third should be "how to present their results". A gerund, a noun phrase or a clause breaks the series.

questions.s:
The cost of repairing the two bridges damaged in the floods ______ been estimated at Rs 40 million.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: were
have
has
are
questions.e: The subject is the singular "cost"; everything from "of repairing" to "floods" modifies it. A singular subject takes "has", while "have" agrees wrongly with "bridges" or "floods".

questions.s:
This year the factory used ______ water than it did in 2020, thanks to a new recycling system.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
o: lesser
less
little
fewer
questions.e: "Water" is uncountable, so the comparative is "less"; "fewer" is used only with countable plurals such as "bottles" or "cups". "Lesser" means "smaller in importance", and "little" cannot be followed by "than".

questions.s:
The roots of mangrove trees trap mud and slow the force of incoming waves. ______ villages behind healthy mangrove belts on the Sindh coast often suffer less storm damage than villages where the trees have been cut down.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: Meanwhile,
As a result,
Similarly,
In contrast,
questions.e: The second sentence gives an effect of the protection described in the first, so a cause-and-effect transition is needed. "In contrast" wrongly signals that the villages' experience opposes what the roots do.

questions.s:
Bilal had planned to cycle to the university library on Saturday morning. ______ heavy rain flooded the road outside his house, so he studied at home instead.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: For example,
Therefore,
However,
Likewise,
questions.e: The rain defeated Bilal's plan, so the second sentence contrasts with the first. "Therefore" would wrongly suggest that his plan caused the flood.

questions.s:
Early telescopes used glass lenses to bend light toward a focus, but the lenses split white light into colours and blurred the image. ______ Isaac Newton designed a telescope that gathered light with a curved mirror instead of a lens.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: In addition to this problem,
To avoid this problem,
Like this problem,
Despite this problem,
questions.e: Newton's mirror design was a way around the colour blurring, so a transition stating purpose fits. "Despite this problem" makes no sense, because the mirror was a response to the problem, not something done in spite of it.

questions.s:
Ayesha's science project tested which household materials keep things warm best. ______ she wrapped identical jars of hot water in wool, newspaper, cotton and foil and recorded each jar's temperature every ten minutes.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: Nevertheless,
In contrast,
Even so,
To do so,
questions.e: The second sentence explains the method she used to carry out the test, so "To do so" fits. "Even so" and "Nevertheless" signal a concession, but nothing in the first sentence works against her method.

questions.s:
Most desert plants survive dry periods by storing water in thick stems or leaves. The creosote bush, ______ stores very little water; it survives by almost completely stopping its growth until rain returns.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: for example,
in addition,
by contrast,
as a result,
questions.e: The creosote bush does the opposite of what most desert plants do, so a contrast is needed. "For example" fails because the bush is not an example of plants that store water.

questions.s:
The Mughal emperor Shah Jahan commissioned the Taj Mahal in Agra as a tomb for his wife Mumtaz Mahal. ______ he ordered the building of Shahjahanabad, a new walled capital in Delhi.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: In addition,
Consequently,
For example,
Instead,
questions.e: The second sentence adds another of Shah Jahan's building projects, so an addition transition fits. "Instead" is wrong because he did not build the city in place of the tomb; he built both.

questions.s:
A 2020 survey of small shopkeepers in Faisalabad found that most still preferred cash to digital payments. ______ the share of shopkeepers who accepted mobile wallets had doubled since the previous survey, suggesting that habits were slowly changing.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: Even so,
In other words,
For this reason,
Similarly,
questions.e: The rise in mobile-wallet use qualifies the finding that cash was still preferred, so a concession is needed. "For this reason" fails because a preference for cash would not cause more shopkeepers to accept wallets.

questions.s:
Some historians describe the printing press as the cause of the European Reformation. Others are more cautious, arguing that printing spread reformist ideas faster but did not create those ideas. ______ the press was an accelerant, not a spark.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: Nevertheless,
By contrast,
For example,
In this view,
questions.e: The last sentence restates the cautious historians' position in a metaphor, so "In this view" correctly attributes it to them. "By contrast" fails because the sentence agrees with the view just described rather than opposing it.

questions.s:
Plastic bags are cheap to produce and convenient for shoppers. ______ they clog drains, harm animals and can remain in landfills for many decades.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: However,
Similarly,
Thus,
For instance,
questions.e: The second sentence lists drawbacks that contrast with the advantages in the first, so "However" fits. "Thus" would wrongly claim that cheapness and convenience cause the harm.

questions.s:
The recipe says to fry the onions until they turn golden. ______ the tomatoes and spices are added and cooked until the oil separates.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: In contrast,
Instead,
Next,
For example,
questions.e: The text describes steps in order, so a sequence word is needed. "Instead" would mean the tomatoes replace the onions, which the recipe does not say.

questions.s:
Volcanic soils are often extremely fertile because weathering ash releases minerals into them. ______ some of the most densely farmed land on the Indonesian island of Java lies on the slopes of active volcanoes.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: It is no surprise, then, that
In other words,
Despite this,
By comparison,
questions.e: Heavy farming on volcanic slopes is the expected result of fertile soil, so a transition expressing a logical consequence fits. "Despite this" fails because fertility is a reason to farm there, not an obstacle.

questions.s:
A new metro line in a large city was expected to reduce traffic on the main road it runs beside. ______ traffic on that road rose in the first year, as new shops and offices along the line drew more visitors to the area.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: Likewise,
In addition,
Instead,
For this reason,
questions.e: Traffic did the opposite of what was expected, so "Instead" fits. "For this reason" fails because the expectation of less traffic did not cause traffic to rise.

questions.s:
Critics sometimes dismiss detective novels as mere puzzles, enjoyable but shallow. Yet the best examples of the genre explore guilt, justice and the limits of what one person can know about another. ______ the puzzle is often the least interesting thing about them.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: Nonetheless,
Similarly,
For instance,
In fact,
questions.e: The last sentence pushes the previous claim further, so an intensifying transition fits. "Nonetheless" is tempting after "Yet", but it would set the last sentence against the point it actually strengthens.

questions.s:
Cheetahs are the fastest land animals over short distances. ______ they tire quickly and rarely chase prey for more than a few hundred metres.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: In addition,
However,
Therefore,
For example,
questions.e: Tiring quickly is a limitation that contrasts with great speed, so "However" fits. "In addition" fails because it would present the limitation as another strength.

questions.s:
Researchers at a Karachi university wanted to know whether background music affects how well students memorise vocabulary. ______ they divided 120 students into three groups: one studied in silence, one with instrumental music and one with songs that had lyrics.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: Likewise,
To find out,
In contrast,
Even so,
questions.e: Dividing students into groups is how the researchers answered their question, so a transition of purpose fits. "Even so" fails because nothing in the first sentence works against their method.

questions.s:
In a memory study, students who learned vocabulary in silence later recalled the most words. ______ students who learned while listening to songs with lyrics recalled the fewest.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: By contrast,
Consequently,
In other words,
For example,
questions.e: The two groups had opposite results, so a contrast fits. "In other words" fails because the second sentence gives a new result rather than restating the first.

questions.s:
Many phone apps let users try basic features for free. ______ a photo-editing app might allow free cropping but charge for advanced filters.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: Finally,
Therefore,
However,
For example,
questions.e: The photo-editing app illustrates the general statement, so "For example" fits. "However" fails because the app follows the pattern described rather than breaking it.

questions.s:
Most mountain glaciers around the world have shrunk in recent decades. ______ many glaciers in the Karakoram range have stayed stable or even grown slightly, a pattern scientists call the Karakoram anomaly.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: As a result,
In contrast,
Similarly,
For instance,
questions.e: The Karakoram glaciers behave differently from most glaciers, so a contrast fits. "Similarly" fails because stable or growing glaciers are the opposite of shrinking ones.

questions.s:
The committee's report praised the new curriculum for its focus on problem-solving. It did not, ______ ignore the curriculum's weaknesses: a full chapter addressed the shortage of teachers trained to deliver it.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: therefore,
similarly,
for example,
however,
questions.e: Not ignoring weaknesses qualifies the praise in the first sentence, so a contrast fits. "Therefore" fails because praising the curriculum is not a reason for discussing its weaknesses.

questions.s:
Economists once assumed that people always act to maximise their own financial gain. Experiments have since shown that many people will give up money to punish someone they think has behaved unfairly. ______ fairness, and not only self-interest, shapes economic decisions.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: In the same way,
Before this,
This suggests that
Even so,
questions.e: The last sentence draws a conclusion from the experiments, so "This suggests that" fits. "Even so" fails because the conclusion follows from the experiments rather than going against them.

questions.s:
Translating poetry is notoriously hard, because rhyme and rhythm rarely survive the move from one language to another. ______ some translators abandon rhyme altogether and try to keep only the poem's images and tone.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: Likewise,
For this reason,
In contrast,
Nevertheless,
questions.e: Giving up rhyme is a response to the difficulty just described, so a cause-and-effect transition fits. "Nevertheless" fails because abandoning rhyme does not go against the difficulty; it follows from it.

questions.s:
The ancient city of Mohenjo-daro had covered brick drains running beneath many of its streets. ______ its builders planned for sanitation on a scale that few cities would match for thousands of years.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: Nevertheless,
Meanwhile,
On the other hand,
Evidently,
questions.e: The drains are evidence from which the second sentence draws a conclusion, so "Evidently" fits. "On the other hand" fails because the conclusion agrees with the evidence rather than contrasting with it.

questions.s:
______ the new drip-irrigation system is expensive to install. But farmers who adopted it in the pilot project used 40 percent less water and recovered their costs within three seasons.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: Therefore,
Granted,
For instance,
Similarly,
questions.e: The writer admits a drawback before answering it with "But", so a concession word fits. "Therefore" fails because nothing earlier in the text explains the system's cost.

questions.s:
The novel's first half moves slowly, filled with long descriptions of the family's daily routines. ______ these chapters are essential: the tragedy of the second half works only because readers have come to know the household so well.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: Even so,
In other words,
For example,
As a result,
questions.e: Calling the slow chapters essential pushes back against the complaint in the first sentence, so a concession fits. "As a result" fails because slowness is not what makes the chapters essential.

questions.s:
The town council did not repair the old footbridge after the flood. ______ it built a new concrete bridge fifty metres downstream.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: For example,
Instead,
In addition,
Similarly,
questions.e: Building a new bridge replaced the repair that did not happen, so "Instead" fits. "In addition" fails because there was no earlier action for the new bridge to add to.

questions.s:
Sara first sketched the building's outline in pencil. ______ she added colour with watercolours and inked the final lines.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: Afterward,
However,
For instance,
Instead,
questions.e: The text describes steps in order, so a time sequence fits. "Instead" fails because she did not skip the sketch; she painted after it.

questions.s:
Sea otters eat sea urchins, which in turn graze on kelp. ______ along coasts where otters were hunted almost to extinction, urchin numbers exploded and kelp forests disappeared.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: Similarly,
In contrast,
Consequently,
Meanwhile,
questions.e: The loss of kelp follows from the food chain described in the first sentence, so a result transition fits. "Meanwhile" fails because it only signals events happening at the same time, not that one caused the other.

questions.s:
Many people believe that bats are blind. ______ every bat species can see, and some fruit bats have excellent eyesight.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: Therefore,
Similarly,
In fact,
For example,
questions.e: The second sentence corrects the popular belief, so "In fact" fits. "Therefore" fails because the belief that bats are blind cannot lead to the conclusion that they see.

questions.s:
The start-up shortened its delivery times, lowered its prices and added a customer helpline in Urdu and Punjabi. ______ it dealt with nearly every complaint raised in the previous year's customer survey.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: Even so,
For example,
Instead,
In short,
questions.e: The last sentence sums up the effect of the three changes listed, so "In short" fits. "For example" fails because the sentence is a summary, not an instance of one change.

questions.s:
Medieval European maps often placed Jerusalem at the centre of the world and filled distant regions with imaginary creatures. ______ such maps were not failed attempts at accurate geography; they expressed religious and cultural beliefs.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: However,
Likewise,
For example,
Therefore,
questions.e: The second sentence corrects the impression that such maps were simply inaccurate, so a contrast fits. "Therefore" fails because the strange features of the maps do not prove that they were never meant to be accurate.

questions.s:
The museum's new entry policy is "pay what you can." ______ visitors decide for themselves how much to pay, and no one is turned away for paying nothing.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: In contrast,
In other words,
Previously,
Nonetheless,
questions.e: The second sentence explains what the policy's slogan means, so a restatement transition fits. "Previously" fails because the sentence describes the new policy, not an earlier one.

questions.s:
The engineers in Islamabad spent March rewriting the app's software. ______ the hardware team in Shenzhen was testing the sensors that the app would control.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: For example,
Meanwhile,
In other words,
As a result,
questions.e: The two teams worked during the same period, so a transition showing simultaneous events fits. "As a result" fails because the software rewrite did not cause the sensor testing.

questions.s:
Pianists practise scales until the finger movements become automatic, freeing their attention for expression. ______ chess players memorise standard openings so that the first moves need little thought, leaving more energy for the complex middle game.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: For instance,
As a result,
Similarly,
In contrast,
questions.e: Chess players use the same strategy as pianists, so a similarity transition fits. "For instance" fails because chess players are not an example of pianists.

questions.s:
The historian argues that the canal transformed the region's economy. Before it opened, farmers could sell their wheat only in nearby markets; ______ they shipped it to ports hundreds of kilometres away.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: similarly,
therefore,
for example,
afterward,
questions.e: The text contrasts the time before the canal with the time after it, so a time transition fits. "Therefore" fails because selling only in nearby markets was not the reason farmers later shipped wheat far away.

questions.s:
Laboratory tests showed that the new battery lost only 2 percent of its capacity after 500 charging cycles. ______ the manufacturer delayed its launch: in hot climates, the battery's casing tended to swell.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: Likewise,
Accordingly,
In other words,
Nevertheless,
questions.e: Delaying the launch goes against what the good test results would lead one to expect, so a concession fits. "Accordingly" fails because strong results would not be a reason to delay.

questions.s:
A survey found that students' sleep worsened during exam season. ______ the average student slept 5.8 hours a night in the final week of exams, compared with 7.1 hours during the rest of term.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: Nevertheless,
Specifically,
Similarly,
Instead,
questions.e: The figures give precise detail about the general finding, so "Specifically" fits. "Nevertheless" fails because the numbers confirm the finding rather than going against it.

questions.s:
The author does not condemn her characters for the choices they make. ______ she shows how poverty and family pressure leave them with few real options.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: Similarly,
Consequently,
Rather,
Afterward,
questions.e: After a negative statement, the second sentence says what the author does instead, so "Rather" fits. "Consequently" is tempting, but not condemning the characters is not what causes her to show their limited options; both describe the same approach.

questions.s:
The documentary has been praised for its stunning footage of snow leopards in the Hindu Kush. ______ it says little about the herders whose livestock the leopards sometimes kill, an omission some viewers found troubling.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: Likewise,
Accordingly,
For instance,
Admittedly,
questions.e: The writer concedes a weakness in a film that has been praised, so a concession fits. "Accordingly" fails because the praise for the footage does not explain why the herders are left out.

questions.s:
Regular exercise strengthens the heart. ______ it improves mood and helps people sleep better.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: In addition,
For example,
Instead,
However,
questions.e: The second sentence adds more benefits, so an addition transition fits. "For example" fails because better mood is not an example of a stronger heart.

questions.s:
The bakery sold out of naan by noon every day for a week. ______ the owner hired a second baker and bought a larger tandoor.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: Similarly,
Therefore,
However,
For instance,
questions.e: Hiring another baker is a response to running out of naan, so a result transition fits. "However" fails because the owner's action follows from the problem rather than contrasting with it.

questions.s:
Hassan revised for two hours every evening for a month before the entrance test. ______ he scored in the top five percent of candidates.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: However,
Meanwhile,
For example,
Consequently,
questions.e: His high score is presented as the result of steady revision, so "Consequently" fits. "However" would wrongly suggest that he did well in spite of preparing.

questions.s:
Silver conducts electricity even better than copper does. ______ copper, not silver, is used in most household wiring, because silver is far too expensive.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: In other words,
Similarly,
For example,
Nevertheless,
questions.e: Choosing copper goes against what silver's better conductivity would suggest, so a concession fits. "In other words" fails because the second sentence does not restate the first.

questions.s:
Many early films were silent, and musicians played live in the cinema to accompany them. ______ the arrival of recorded sound in the late 1920s put thousands of cinema musicians out of work.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: Instead,
Likewise,
Later,
For example,
questions.e: The second sentence moves forward in time to a later change, so "Later" fits. "For example" fails because the arrival of sound is not an example of silent films.

questions.s:
The research team tried three designs for a water filter. The first clogged within days, and the second removed too few bacteria. ______ they settled on a design that combined sand, charcoal and a ceramic layer.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: Finally,
For instance,
Similarly,
In other words,
questions.e: The text lists attempts in order and ends with the last one, so "Finally" fits. "Similarly" fails because the third design succeeded, unlike the two that failed.

questions.s:
The poem never names the city it describes. ______ details such as the minarets, the river and the old walled bazaar have led many readers to identify it as Lahore.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: Still,
In other words,
Therefore,
Likewise,
questions.e: Readers identify the city even though it is not named, so a concession fits. "Therefore" fails because leaving the city unnamed is not what lets readers identify it.

questions.s:
A diet high in fibre has been linked to a lower risk of heart disease. ______ nutritionists often recommend whole grains, lentils and vegetables.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: Even so,
Previously,
In contrast,
For this reason,
questions.e: The recommendation follows from the health benefit, so a cause transition fits. "Even so" fails because the link to heart health supports the recommendation rather than working against it.

questions.s:
Ayesha's essay argues that libraries remain vital in the digital age. Her first point is that libraries offer free internet access to people who lack it at home. ______ she notes that librarians teach people how to judge which online sources are reliable.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: Second,
For example,
In contrast,
Instead,
questions.e: The essay's points are listed in order, so "Second" fits after "first point". "For example" fails because teaching source evaluation is a new point, not an example of free internet access.

questions.s:
The new appointment system has clearly cut waiting times at the hospital's outpatient clinic. ______ it is too early to say whether patients are receiving better care, since no data on treatment outcomes has been collected yet.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: For example,
In other words,
That said,
Accordingly,
questions.e: The second sentence limits the claim made in the first, so a qualifying transition fits. "Accordingly" fails because shorter waiting times are not a reason why it is too early to judge care.

questions.s:
Warmer winters allow more bark beetles to survive until spring. Larger beetle populations ______ kill more trees, and the dead trees provide fuel for bigger forest fires.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: nevertheless
in turn
for example
instead
questions.e: The text traces a chain in which each effect causes the next, so "in turn" fits. "Instead" fails because killing trees does not replace anything mentioned earlier.

questions.s:
The bridge's designer used a lightweight steel that had never been tested over such a long span. Engineers ran hundreds of computer simulations, all of which suggested the structure would be safe. ______ the city insisted on a full-scale load test before opening the bridge to traffic.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: Likewise,
Even so,
Thus,
In other words,
questions.e: Insisting on a test goes against the reassurance the simulations gave, so a concession fits. "Thus" is tempting because of the untested steel, but it would make the reassuring simulations the reason for the test.

questions.s:
Researchers expected that the bright colours of poison dart frogs mainly helped them attract mates. ______ studies showed that the colours chiefly warn predators that the frogs are toxic.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: Similarly,
Instead,
Therefore,
In addition,
questions.e: The studies replaced the expected explanation with a different one, so "Instead" fits. "In addition" fails because the finding did not add to the expectation; it overturned it.

questions.s:
Students who sleep well before an exam tend to perform better on it. ______ athletes who rest properly before a match tend to make fewer errors.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: For instance,
Nevertheless,
Likewise,
Instead,
questions.e: Athletes show the same pattern as students, so a similarity transition fits. "For instance" fails because athletes are not an example of students.

questions.s:
The artist began her career painting realistic portraits of village women in Punjab. ______ her work became increasingly abstract, until by the 1990s her canvases showed only blocks of colour.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: As a result,
For instance,
Over time,
Similarly,
questions.e: The text describes a gradual change in her style, so a time transition fits. "As a result" fails because painting realistic portraits did not cause her later abstraction.

questions.s:
The minister promised that the new tax would fall only on the wealthiest 1 percent of earners. ______ an analysis by independent economists found that it would also raise prices for ordinary households, since businesses would pass on part of the cost.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: However,
Similarly,
Accordingly,
In short,
questions.e: The economists' finding contradicts the minister's promise, so a contrast fits. "In short" fails because the second sentence does not summarise the promise; it challenges it.

questions.s:
Several cities in the region have expanded their bus networks in the past decade. ______ one city added electric buses on every route, becoming the first in the country to do so.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: For example,
Consequently,
Nevertheless,
In contrast,
questions.e: The city with electric buses illustrates the general trend, so "For example" fits. "In contrast" fails because that city followed the trend rather than departing from it.

questions.s:
Every chemical element emits light at its own unique set of wavelengths. ______ by splitting the light of a distant star into a spectrum, astronomers can tell which elements the star contains.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: In contrast,
However,
Thus,
Meanwhile,
questions.e: Identifying a star's elements is possible because each element has a unique pattern, so a result transition fits. "However" fails because the second sentence depends on the first rather than contradicting it.

questions.s:
The proposal to build the dam faces two serious objections. First, it would flood several villages whose residents have not been consulted. ______ the reservoir would trap the sediment that farmers downstream rely on to keep their fields fertile.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: Moreover,
Instead,
In other words,
For example,
questions.e: The second objection adds to the first, so an addition transition fits. "In other words" fails because trapping sediment is a different objection, not a restatement of the flooding.

questions.s:
The violinist's early recordings are technically flawless but emotionally distant. Her later recordings contain small slips of intonation; ______ they are far more moving.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: nonetheless,
for example,
similarly,
therefore,
questions.e: The later recordings move listeners despite their slips, so a concession fits. "Therefore" fails because slips of intonation are not what make the recordings moving.

questions.s:
Scientists long believed that the adult human brain could not produce new neurons. ______ evidence has since accumulated that at least one region, the hippocampus, may keep producing new neurons throughout life, though the question is still debated.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: Similarly,
However,
Accordingly,
In short,
questions.e: The new evidence challenges the earlier belief, so a contrast fits. "Accordingly" fails because the old belief did not lead to evidence against it.
