questions.s:
The village school had no electricity, no library and a single teacher for 140 students. ______ the girls who passed their matriculation exams that year did so against long odds.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: For instance,
In contrast,
Even so,
Thus,
questions.e: The hard conditions explain why passing was against long odds, so a result transition fits. "Even so" is tempting because passing seems surprising, but the sentence says the girls faced long odds, which follows from the conditions rather than going against them.

questions.s:
When interest rates rise, borrowing becomes more expensive and businesses tend to invest less. ______ when rates fall, cheaper loans encourage firms to expand.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: Conversely,
Therefore,
Similarly,
For example,
questions.e: The second sentence describes the opposite situation with the opposite effect, so "Conversely" fits. "Similarly" fails because falling rates have the reverse effect of rising ones.

questions.s:
The charity aims to raise literacy among adult women in rural Balochistan. ______ it trains local women as teachers and runs evening classes in village homes.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: Nevertheless,
Similarly,
In contrast,
To this end,
questions.e: Training teachers and running classes are the means of reaching the stated aim, so "To this end" fits. "Nevertheless" fails because the activities serve the aim rather than going against it.

questions.s:
Some linguists argue that the words a language offers can affect how its speakers perceive the world. ______ speakers of languages that have separate basic words for light blue and dark blue may tell those shades apart more quickly.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: Nevertheless,
Previously,
For instance,
In contrast,
questions.e: The second sentence gives a case that illustrates the linguists' claim, so "For instance" fits. "In contrast" fails because the example supports the claim rather than opposing it.

questions.s:
The first edition of the dictionary contained about 40,000 entries. ______ the latest edition contains more than 90,000, reflecting a century of new scientific and technical words.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: Similarly,
Therefore,
By comparison,
For example,
questions.e: The text compares the sizes of two editions, so "By comparison" fits. "Similarly" fails because the numbers differ greatly.

questions.s:
Glass is made by melting sand at very high temperatures. ______ glassmaking has always required large amounts of fuel, and early glassworks were often built near forests.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: In contrast,
For example,
Hence,
Nevertheless,
questions.e: The need for fuel follows from the high temperatures, so a result transition fits. "Nevertheless" fails because needing fuel is expected, not surprising, given the heat required.

questions.s:
The plan to ban cars from the old city's narrow lanes has drawn protests from shopkeepers. ______ some opposition was expected; any change to how customers reach the bazaar affects the shopkeepers' income.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: For example,
As a result,
Of course,
In contrast,
questions.e: The writer acknowledges that the protests were predictable and explains why, so "Of course" fits. "As a result" fails because the protests did not cause the opposition to be expected; the expectation came before them.

questions.s:
The study did not find that social media use causes anxiety in teenagers. ______ it found only that the two tend to occur together, which could mean that anxious teenagers simply spend more time online.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: Furthermore,
Similarly,
Consequently,
Rather,
questions.e: After stating what the study did not find, the text says what it did find, so "Rather" fits. "Furthermore" fails because it would add a point to a finding that was never made.

questions.s:
The town's ancient irrigation channels are not merely of historical interest. ______ several of them still carry water to orchards today.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: In fact,
Similarly,
For this reason,
However,
questions.e: The second sentence backs up and strengthens the first, so "In fact" fits. "However" is tempting after a "not merely" statement, but the sentence supports the first claim rather than contrasting with it.

questions.s:
The museum now allows visitors to photograph its collection, as long as they do not use a flash. ______ all photography inside the galleries was forbidden.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: Previously,
Consequently,
Likewise,
In addition,
questions.e: The second sentence describes the earlier rule, so a time transition pointing to the past fits. "Consequently" fails because the new policy could not have caused the old ban.

questions.s:
The team expected its solar panels to perform worst in winter, when the days are short. ______ the panels' output dropped most sharply in June, when dust storms coated them with fine sand.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: Similarly,
Unexpectedly,
For example,
Accordingly,
questions.e: The June drop contradicts the team's expectation, so "Unexpectedly" fits. "Accordingly" fails because it would present the result as matching the expectation.

questions.s:
The coach told the team to drink enough water, warm up properly and stretch after training. ______ she told them to rest when they felt pain rather than play through it.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: In contrast,
Instead,
As a result,
Above all,
questions.e: The last instruction is presented as the most important in a list of advice, so "Above all" fits. "In contrast" fails because resting when in pain is another piece of advice of the same kind, not an opposing one.

questions.s:
Many listeners assume that the driving rhythms of a qawwali performance are invented from scratch each time; ______ performers draw on a large stock of traditional patterns that they combine in new ways.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: for example,
in reality,
consequently,
likewise,
questions.e: The second clause corrects a common assumption, so "in reality" fits. "Consequently" fails because listeners' assumption does not cause the performers' practice.

questions.s:
Critics of the transport plan argue that it is too costly. They also point out that it ignores the needs of the city's poorest neighbourhoods. ______ they claim, the plan would mainly benefit wealthy districts that already have good services.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: Indeed,
Previously,
Instead,
Nevertheless,
questions.e: The last sentence strengthens the critics' second point, so an emphasising transition fits. "Instead" fails because the claim does not replace the critics' earlier objections; it reinforces them.

questions.s:
The engineer's first design for the drone frame was rejected because it was too heavy. ______ her second design used aluminium in place of steel and weighed 30 percent less.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: Similarly,
Nevertheless,
For example,
Accordingly,
questions.e: The lighter second design responds to the rejection, so "Accordingly" fits. "Similarly" fails because the second design differed from the first in exactly the way that mattered.

questions.s:
The government has announced that a new hospital will open in the district in 2027. ______ patients who need surgery must travel four hours to the provincial capital.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: For example,
Until then,
As a result,
Likewise,
questions.e: The long journey describes the situation before the hospital opens, so "Until then" fits. "As a result" fails because the announcement does not force patients to travel.

questions.s:
Pakistani truck art covers vehicles with painted flowers, birds, poetry and portraits, often down to the smallest panel. ______ decorating a single truck can keep a team of painters busy for several weeks.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: Previously,
In contrast,
Nevertheless,
Unsurprisingly,
questions.e: Weeks of work is what one would expect for such detailed decoration, so "Unsurprisingly" fits. "Nevertheless" fails because the long work follows from the detail rather than going against it.

questions.s:
The novelist rarely gives interviews and has never appeared on television. ______ she answers every letter that readers send her, often at length.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: Thus,
Indeed,
Yet
Likewise,
questions.e: Answering every letter contrasts with her avoidance of publicity, so "Yet" fits. "Indeed" fails because it would present her letter-writing as further proof that she avoids the public.

questions.s:
Some economists predicted that the rise in the minimum wage would lead to job losses. A study of 300 small firms in Lahore and Multan a year later found no such effect; ______ several of the firms had hired additional staff.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: nevertheless,
if anything,
in other words,
for this reason,
questions.e: Hiring more staff goes slightly beyond "no job losses" in the opposite direction from the prediction, so "if anything" fits. "In other words" fails because hiring extra staff is a stronger claim than finding no effect, not a restatement of it.

questions.s:
Desalination plants can supply drinking water to dry coastal cities. ______ they use large amounts of energy and release salty waste that can harm marine life.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: In other words,
On the other hand,
Consequently,
For instance,
questions.e: The second sentence lists drawbacks that contrast with the benefit, so "On the other hand" fits. "Consequently" fails because supplying water does not explain the energy use as a result.

questions.s:
In the Indus Valley, early farmers relied on the river's yearly floods to water and fertilise their fields. ______ farmers along the Nile organised their calendar around the river's annual rise.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: Likewise,
In short,
Instead,
Consequently,
questions.e: Nile farmers depended on their river in the same way, so a similarity transition fits. "Consequently" fails because Indus farming practices did not cause those in Egypt.

questions.s:
The college library extended its opening hours during exam season. ______ more students used it in the evenings than ever before.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: However,
For example,
As a result,
Instead,
questions.e: The rise in evening use followed from the longer hours, so a result transition fits. "However" fails because the second sentence does not contrast with the first.

questions.s:
Lahore is famous for its food streets. ______ the city is home to historic sites such as the Badshahi Mosque and the Lahore Fort.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: Therefore,
Moreover,
In contrast,
For instance,
questions.e: The second sentence adds another reason the city is known, so an addition transition fits. "Therefore" fails because the food streets do not cause the historic sites to exist.

questions.s:
Dolphins are mammals, not fish. ______ they breathe air through a blowhole and must come to the surface regularly.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: Similarly,
Instead,
However,
Therefore,
questions.e: Breathing air follows from being a mammal, so a result transition fits. "However" fails because breathing air is consistent with being a mammal.

questions.s:
Zara wanted to buy a new laptop for her university course. ______ she saved part of her allowance every month for a year.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: Even so,
For example,
To afford one,
In contrast,
questions.e: Saving money was her way of reaching the goal, so a transition of purpose fits. "Even so" fails because wanting a laptop does not work against saving for one.

questions.s:
A block of wood floats on water. ______ a block of iron of the same size sinks at once.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: For instance,
Therefore,
Similarly,
In contrast,
questions.e: The iron behaves in the opposite way to the wood, so a contrast fits. "Similarly" fails because sinking is the opposite of floating.

questions.s:
Before planting the seeds, the farmer ploughed the field. ______ she watered the soil and sowed the seeds in rows.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: For example,
Then,
Instead,
However,
questions.e: The steps are described in order, so a sequence word fits. "Instead" fails because she did not replace ploughing with watering; she did both, one after the other.

questions.s:
Many fruits are rich in vitamin C. ______ oranges, guavas and strawberries all contain large amounts of it.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: Therefore,
For example,
Meanwhile,
However,
questions.e: The named fruits illustrate the general statement, so "For example" fits. "Therefore" fails because the general statement does not cause these particular fruits to contain vitamin C.

questions.s:
The film received poor reviews from critics. ______ it became one of the most popular films of the year.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: Nevertheless,
For instance,
Similarly,
Consequently,
questions.e: Its popularity goes against what bad reviews would lead one to expect, so a concession fits. "Consequently" fails because poor reviews would not cause popularity.

questions.s:
Air quality in the city worsens sharply every November, when smoke from crop burning is trapped near the ground by cold, still air. ______ schools in the city have sometimes closed for several days during that month.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: Consequently,
In other words,
Similarly,
Nevertheless,
questions.e: The school closures are a result of the bad air, so a result transition fits. "Nevertheless" fails because closing schools is an expected response, not a surprising one.

questions.s:
The chemist expected the solution to turn blue. ______ it turned pale green, suggesting an impurity in one of the samples.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: Therefore,
For example,
Instead,
Likewise,
questions.e: The colour change differed from the expected one, so "Instead" fits. "Therefore" fails because the expectation could not cause a different result.

questions.s:
The new phone's camera is excellent in daylight. Its performance in low light, ______ is disappointing: night photos come out grainy and blurred.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: for example,
similarly,
however,
therefore,
questions.e: Poor low-light performance contrasts with the daylight praise, so "however" fits. "Similarly" fails because the second judgement is the opposite of the first.

questions.s:
Kites fill the sky over Lahore during the spring festival of Basant. ______ the festival marks the arrival of spring with music, yellow clothing and special food.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: Despite kite flying,
Beyond kite flying,
Instead of kite flying,
Unlike kite flying,
questions.e: The second sentence adds other parts of the festival, so a phrase of addition fits. "Instead of kite flying" fails because the text has just said that kites are flown during the festival.

questions.s:
The journal requires every study it publishes to share its raw data. ______ other researchers can check the analysis and try to reproduce the results.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: Even so,
In contrast,
This way,
For example,
questions.e: Checking and reproducing results is what sharing data makes possible, so "This way" fits. "Even so" fails because the rule supports checking rather than standing in its way.

questions.s:
The professor's lectures are known for being difficult. ______ students consistently rate her course as one of the most valuable in the programme.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: In other words,
Likewise,
Therefore,
Even so,
questions.e: High ratings go against what difficult lectures might suggest, so a concession fits. "Therefore" is tempting because hard courses can be rewarding, but the text gives no reason to treat difficulty as the cause of the high ratings.

questions.s:
Some species of bamboo can grow almost a metre in a single day. ______ bamboo is being studied as a quickly renewable alternative to timber in construction.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: Because of this rapid growth,
Despite this rapid growth,
Unlike this rapid growth,
Before this rapid growth,
questions.e: Fast growth is the reason bamboo can be renewed quickly, so a cause phrase fits. "Despite this rapid growth" fails because fast growth helps rather than hinders bamboo's use as a renewable material.

questions.s:
The two candidates disagree on almost every economic question. ______ both support expanding free primary education.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: For instance,
Thus,
In addition,
Still,
questions.e: Their shared view is an exception to their general disagreement, so a concession fits. "For instance" fails because agreement is not an example of disagreement.

questions.s:
The museum's ground floor displays ancient Gandhara sculptures of the Buddha. ______ the upper floor is devoted to Mughal-era manuscripts and miniature paintings.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: In other words,
For example,
As a result,
By contrast,
questions.e: The two floors hold different collections, so a contrast fits. "As a result" fails because the ground-floor display does not cause the upper floor's contents.

questions.s:
The mosquitoes that spread dengue fever breed in standing water. ______ health officials urge residents to empty buckets, flowerpots and old tyres after it rains.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: Therefore,
Similarly,
In contrast,
However,
questions.e: The advice follows from how the mosquitoes breed, so a result transition fits. "However" fails because the advice is consistent with the first sentence rather than opposed to it.

questions.s:
In the fourteenth century, Ibn Battuta travelled across North Africa, the Middle East, South Asia and China. ______ he dictated an account of his journeys, which remains an important historical source.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: Similarly,
Later,
Instead,
For example,
questions.e: Dictating the account came after the travels, so a time transition fits. "Instead" fails because he did not dictate the account in place of travelling.

questions.s:
The coach praised the team's defence after the tournament. ______ she said, the players had conceded only two goals in six matches.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: Indeed,
However,
Nevertheless,
Instead,
questions.e: The statistic strengthens the praise, so an emphasising transition fits. "However" fails because conceding only two goals supports the praise rather than contrasting with it.

questions.s:
The study's sample was small, and all of its participants came from a single city. ______ its findings should be treated as preliminary until larger studies are done.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: Accordingly,
Nonetheless,
Similarly,
For example,
questions.e: Treating the findings with caution follows from the study's limitations, so "Accordingly" fits. "Nonetheless" fails because the limitations support caution rather than going against it.

questions.s:
The essay does not argue that technology harms education. ______ it argues that technology helps only when teachers are trained to use it well.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: Moreover,
Therefore,
For example,
Rather,
questions.e: After saying what the essay does not argue, the text gives its actual claim, so "Rather" fits. "Moreover" fails because it would add to a claim the essay was just said not to make.

questions.s:
Readers often assume that a novel's narrator speaks for the author. ______ the narrator of this novel is a fictional character whose views the author frequently mocks.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: As an illustration,
In the same way,
In this case, however,
For this reason,
questions.e: The novel is an exception to the readers' usual assumption, so a contrast fits. "In the same way" fails because a mocked narrator does not speak for the author.

questions.s:
The bridge was designed to carry 5,000 vehicles a day. Within a decade of opening, it was carrying three times that number. ______ engineers began planning a second bridge long before the first had reached the end of its expected life.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: Unsurprisingly,
Nevertheless,
In contrast,
Similarly,
questions.e: Planning a second bridge is the expected response to such overuse, so "Unsurprisingly" fits. "Nevertheless" is tempting because the first bridge was still young, but the planning follows from the traffic rather than going against it.

questions.s:
The poet's early work is crowded with references to classical Persian poetry. ______ her later poems use plain, everyday Urdu that any reader can follow.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
o: For instance,
By contrast,
Accordingly,
Indeed,
questions.e: Plain later poems differ from the allusive early work, so a contrast fits. "Indeed" fails because it would present the plain later style as reinforcing the crowded early style.

questions.s:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• K2 is the second-highest mountain in the world, at 8,611 metres.
• It lies in the Karakoram range, on the border between Pakistan and China.
• It was first climbed in 1954 by an Italian expedition.
• Climbers call it the "Savage Mountain" because it is so difficult and dangerous.

The student wants to emphasize where K2 is located. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
o: K2 stands in the Karakoram range, on the Pakistan–China border.
An Italian expedition made the first ascent of K2 in 1954.
K2, known as the "Savage Mountain," is famously hard to climb.
At 8,611 metres, K2 is the second-highest mountain in the world.
questions.e: Only this choice gives K2's location: its range and the border it sits on. The other choices are accurate but describe its height, its reputation or its first ascent instead.

questions.s:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Shalimar Gardens in Lahore were built in the 1640s during the reign of Shah Jahan.
• The gardens are laid out in three terraces, each lower than the one before.
• They contain more than 400 fountains.
• In 1981 they were named a UNESCO World Heritage Site together with the Lahore Fort.

The student wants to describe the layout of the Shalimar Gardens. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
o: In 1981, UNESCO listed the Shalimar Gardens and the Lahore Fort as a World Heritage Site.
The Shalimar Gardens date from the reign of the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan.
The Shalimar Gardens are arranged in three terraces that step down one after another.
Built in the 1640s under Shah Jahan, the Shalimar Gardens are one of Lahore's best-known sights.
questions.e: The terraces describe how the gardens are laid out, which is the goal. The choices about the 1640s, Shah Jahan or UNESCO give history, not layout.

questions.s:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• In 2022, researcher Nida Qureshi studied the effect of lighting in classrooms.
• She compared 40 classrooms with large windows to 40 classrooms with small windows.
• Students in rooms with large windows scored 9 percent higher on reading tests, on average.
• Qureshi suggested that natural light may improve concentration.

The student wants to present the main finding of Qureshi's study. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
o: Qureshi found that students in classrooms with large windows scored about 9 percent higher on reading tests.
In 2022, the researcher Nida Qureshi studied how lighting affects students in classrooms.
Qureshi's 2022 study compared forty classrooms that had large windows with forty classrooms whose windows were small.
According to Qureshi, natural light may help students concentrate.
questions.e: The finding is the 9 percent difference in reading scores, and only this choice states it. The choice about forty classrooms of each kind describes the method, and the choice about concentration gives Qureshi's suggested explanation rather than what she found.

questions.s:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The cheetah and the pronghorn are both among the fastest land animals.
• The cheetah lives mainly in Africa; the pronghorn lives in North America.
• The cheetah can sprint at about 100 kilometres per hour, but only for short bursts.
• The pronghorn can keep up a speed of about 55 kilometres per hour over several kilometres.

The student wants to contrast the running abilities of the two animals. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
o: The cheetah can reach about 100 kilometres per hour, though only in short bursts.
The cheetah sprints at about 100 km per hour in short bursts, while the pronghorn holds about 55 km per hour for kilometres.
Both the cheetah and the pronghorn rank among the fastest land animals on Earth.
The cheetah lives mainly in Africa, whereas the pronghorn, another very fast animal, is found in North America.
questions.e: Only this choice sets the cheetah's short sprints against the pronghorn's long-distance speed. The choice about Africa and North America is a contrast, but of where the animals live, not how they run.

questions.s:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Truck art is a style of decoration found on trucks and buses in Pakistan.
• Artists cover vehicles with bright flowers, birds, landscapes and lines of poetry.
• A fully decorated truck can cost its owner several months' income.
• Truck art has been shown in galleries abroad.

The student wants to introduce truck art to an audience unfamiliar with it. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
o: The owner of a truck decorated in this style may spend several months' income on a single vehicle's paintwork.
Artists who paint trucks often add landscapes and lines of poetry.
Truck art has been shown in galleries outside Pakistan.
Truck art, a Pakistani style of vehicle decoration, covers trucks and buses with flowers, birds and poetry.
questions.e: An unfamiliar audience needs to know what truck art is and what it looks like, which this choice explains. The other choices assume the reader already knows what "truck art" or "this style" refers to.

questions.s:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Ecologist Farhan Malik studies the Indus river dolphin, which is found mainly in Pakistan.
• The dolphin is nearly blind and finds food by echolocation.
• Malik's project aims to learn how irrigation barrages affect where the dolphins can travel.
• He has placed underwater sound recorders along a 200-kilometre stretch of the river.

The student wants to emphasize the aim of Malik's research. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
o: Malik has placed underwater sound recorders along a 200-kilometre stretch of the Indus River.
The Indus river dolphin, which is nearly blind, finds its food by echolocation.
Farhan Malik is an ecologist who studies the Indus river dolphin, found mainly in Pakistan.
Malik wants to find out how irrigation barrages affect where Indus river dolphins can travel.
questions.e: The aim is what the project wants to learn: how barrages affect the dolphins' movement. The choice about sound recorders describes Malik's method, not his aim.

questions.s:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Many traditional buildings in hot, dry regions have thick walls of mud or stone.
• Thick walls absorb heat during the day and release it slowly at night.
• Traditional houses in Yazd, Iran, also use tall wind-catching towers to cool their rooms.
• Old havelis in Lahore are built around shaded inner courtyards.

The student wants to make a generalization about traditional buildings in hot, dry regions. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
o: Both Yazd's houses and Lahore's havelis are examples of traditional buildings.
In hot, dry regions, traditional buildings often have thick walls that absorb heat by day and release it at night.
In the Iranian city of Yazd, traditional houses have tall towers that catch passing winds and channel them into the rooms.
Old havelis in Lahore are arranged around inner courtyards that give shade.
questions.e: A generalization covers buildings across the region, as this choice does. The choices about Yazd and Lahore describe particular places, so they are specific examples rather than general statements.

questions.s:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Indus Science Fair is an annual competition for secondary school students.
• The first fair was held in Sukkur in 2016.
• Students present projects on water, energy and farming.
• Winners receive scholarships funded by local businesses.
• The 2024 fair attracted more than 1,200 entrants.

The student wants to state when and where the first Indus Science Fair took place. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
o: Winners at the annual Indus Science Fair receive scholarships from local businesses.
More than 1,200 students entered the Indus Science Fair in 2024.
At the Indus Science Fair, students present projects on water, energy and farming.
The first Indus Science Fair was held in Sukkur in 2016.
questions.e: Only this choice gives both the place, Sukkur, and the year, 2016, of the first fair. The choice about 2024 gives a date, but for a later fair and without a place.

questions.s:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Mehwish and her brother Omar both run small bakeries in Multan.
• Mehwish sells mostly through a phone app that delivers to people's homes.
• Omar sells only from the counter of his shop.
• Both bakeries are known for their nan khatai biscuits.

The student wants to emphasize a difference between how Mehwish and Omar sell their goods. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
o: The bakeries run by Mehwish and Omar are both known for their nan khatai biscuits.
Mehwish and Omar, who are brother and sister, both run small bakeries in Multan.
Mehwish sells most of her baked goods through a phone app that delivers them to people's homes.
Mehwish sells mostly through a home-delivery app, while Omar sells only from his shop counter.
questions.e: This choice sets the two selling methods side by side. The choice about the phone app describes only Mehwish, so it shows no difference, and the other two choices stress what the siblings share.

questions.s:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• An urban heat island is a city area that is noticeably warmer than the surrounding countryside.
• Concrete and asphalt absorb sunlight during the day and release the heat slowly.
• A 2021 study found that central Karachi was up to 4 °C warmer at night than nearby rural land.
• Planting trees and using light-coloured roofs can reduce the effect.

The student wants to explain to an audience unfamiliar with the term what an urban heat island is and one cause of it. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
o: According to a 2021 study, central Karachi was up to 4 °C warmer at night than the rural land around it.
Concrete and asphalt absorb sunlight during the day and then release the heat slowly.
An urban heat island, a city area warmer than the nearby countryside, forms partly because concrete and asphalt store heat.
Planting trees and using light-coloured roofs can reduce the urban heat island effect in cities such as Karachi.
questions.e: The goal has two parts, a definition and a cause, and only this choice gives both. The choice about concrete and asphalt names the cause but never says what an urban heat island is.

questions.s:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Many rural schools in Thar lack reliable electricity.
• Without power, their computer labs and fans cannot be used.
• A pilot project installed solar panels on the roofs of 25 of these schools.
• Attendance at those schools rose by 12 percent during the hot months.

The student wants to present the result of the pilot project. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
o: After solar panels were put on 25 schools in Thar, their attendance in the hot months rose by 12 percent.
Rural schools in Thar often lack the reliable electricity needed for computer labs.
Many rural schools in Thar cannot use their computer labs or fans, because they lack reliable electricity.
A pilot project installed solar panels on the roofs of 25 rural schools in Thar.
questions.e: The result is the 12 percent rise in attendance, which only this choice reports. The choice about installing panels describes what the project did, not what came of it.

questions.s:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Ibn al-Haytham was an 11th-century scholar who studied light and vision.
• He tested his ideas with careful experiments.
• Galileo Galilei was a 17th-century scientist who studied motion and astronomy.
• He also tested his ideas with experiments.

The student wants to emphasize a similarity between Ibn al-Haytham and Galileo. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
o: Galileo, a 17th-century scientist, studied motion as well as the planets and stars.
Ibn al-Haytham studied light and vision, while Galileo studied motion and astronomy.
Both Ibn al-Haytham and Galileo tested their ideas through experiments.
Ibn al-Haytham lived in the 11th century, about six centuries before Galileo.
questions.e: Testing ideas by experiment is what the two men shared. The choice about their subjects contrasts them, and the choice about centuries stresses the gap between them.

questions.s:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Tarbela Dam on the Indus River was completed in 1976.
• It is one of the largest earth-filled dams in the world.
• Its reservoir stores water for irrigation across Punjab and Sindh.
• Its power station generates electricity for the national grid.

The student wants to emphasize the size of the Tarbela Dam. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
o: The Tarbela Dam's power station supplies electricity to the national grid.
Tarbela, on the Indus River, is one of the largest earth-filled dams in the world.
Completed in 1976, the Tarbela Dam stands on the Indus River.
Water stored behind the Tarbela Dam irrigates farmland across both Punjab and Sindh.
questions.e: Calling Tarbela one of the largest earth-filled dams in the world stresses its size. The choice about irrigation across two provinces tells what the dam does, not how big it is.

questions.s:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Researchers long believed that a hawkmoth species in northern Pakistan fed only at night.
• In 2023, a team led by Sana Iqbal filmed the moths feeding at midday on alpine flowers.
• Those flowers open only in daylight.
• Iqbal argues that the moths may be important daytime pollinators.

The student wants to emphasize how Iqbal's findings challenge an earlier belief. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
o: The alpine flowers on which the hawkmoths were filmed open only during the day.
In 2023, Sana Iqbal's team filmed hawkmoths in northern Pakistan feeding on alpine flowers.
Although the moths were long thought to feed only at night, Iqbal's team filmed them feeding at midday.
Iqbal argues that the hawkmoths may be important pollinators of flowers that open only in daylight.
questions.e: Only this choice states the earlier belief and the finding that contradicts it. The others report Iqbal's work without mentioning the belief it challenges.

questions.s:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Sea of Green is a 2019 novel by the writer Rabia Hasan.
• It follows a young tea picker in the hills of Sri Lanka.
• It has been translated into eleven languages.
• Hasan grew up on a tea estate herself.

The student wants to introduce the novel Sea of Green and its author. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
o: Rabia Hasan, who grew up on a tea estate herself, has seen her work translated into eleven languages.
Translated into eleven languages, the novel follows a young tea picker in Sri Lanka.
Sea of Green, a 2019 novel by Rabia Hasan, follows a young tea picker in Sri Lanka's hills.
Rabia Hasan's novel has been translated into eleven languages.
questions.e: This choice names the novel, its author and what it is about. The others leave out the title or the author, so they do not introduce both.

questions.s:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Bioplastics are plastics made from plant materials such as corn starch or sugarcane.
• Ordinary plastics are made from oil.
• Some bioplastics break down within a few months in industrial composting facilities.
• Bioplastics currently cost more to produce than ordinary plastics.

The student wants to emphasize an advantage of some bioplastics over ordinary plastics. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
o: Corn starch and sugarcane are among the materials used to make bioplastics.
Unlike ordinary plastics, some bioplastics break down within months in industrial composting facilities.
Bioplastics are made from plant materials such as corn starch or sugarcane.
Bioplastics currently cost more to produce than ordinary plastics, which are made from oil.
questions.e: Breaking down quickly is an advantage, and this choice compares it directly with ordinary plastics. The choice about cost points to a disadvantage, and the choices about corn starch and sugarcane only describe what bioplastics are made of.

questions.s:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• In 2021, agronomist Imran Butt studied wheat farms in southern Punjab.
• He divided 60 farms into two groups.
• Farms in one group had their fields levelled by laser; the others did not.
• Farms with laser-levelled fields used 25 percent less irrigation water.
• Wheat yields were similar in both groups.

The student wants to describe the method Butt used in his study. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
o: Butt divided 60 farms into two groups, only one of which had its fields levelled by laser.
In 2021, agronomist Imran Butt carried out a study of wheat farms in southern Punjab.
Butt found that farms with laser-levelled fields used 25 percent less water but produced similar yields.
Laser land levelling cut water use by a quarter on the farms Butt studied, without lowering wheat yields.
questions.e: A method is how the study was set up, which this choice explains: two groups, one with laser-levelled fields. The choices about water use and yields give results, and the choice about 2021 gives only the time and place.

questions.s:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Engineer Kamran Aziz designed a low-cost incubator for newborn babies.
• It can run on a car battery when the mains power fails.
• It costs about one-tenth as much as a standard hospital incubator.
• Aziz's goal was to help small clinics that cannot afford standard incubators or lack a steady power supply.
• It has been tested in clinics in Sindh and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

The student wants to explain the purpose of Aziz's design. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
o: Clinics in Sindh and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa have tested the low-cost incubator that Aziz designed.
Aziz's incubator, which can keep running on a car battery when the mains power fails, costs about one-tenth as much as a standard model.
Engineer Kamran Aziz has designed an incubator for newborn babies.
Aziz designed his incubator to help small clinics that cannot afford standard incubators or lack steady power.
questions.e: The purpose is the problem Aziz meant to solve, which only this choice states. The choice about the car battery and the price lists features of the design, not the reason for it.

questions.s:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Lahore Museum was founded in 1865.
• Its present building on The Mall opened in 1894.
• It holds a large collection of Gandhara art.
• John Lockwood Kipling, father of the writer Rudyard Kipling, was one of its early curators.

The student wants to emphasize when the museum's present building opened. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
o: The Lahore Museum's present building on The Mall opened in 1894.
John Lockwood Kipling was one of the Lahore Museum's early curators.
The Lahore Museum, which holds a large Gandhara collection, stands on The Mall.
Founded in 1865, the Lahore Museum is known for its Gandhara art.
questions.e: Only this choice gives the opening date of the present building, 1894. The choice with 1865 is tempting, but that is when the museum was founded, not when its present building opened.

questions.s:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• A 2023 survey asked 2,000 university students in Pakistan where they mainly get their news.
• 64 percent said social media.
• 21 percent said television.
• 9 percent said newspapers or news websites.
• The rest gave other answers.

The student wants to emphasize how far ahead social media was of the next most common news source. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
o: Only 9 percent of the students surveyed relied mainly on newspapers or news websites.
Social media, chosen by 64 percent of students, was used about three times as often as television, the next choice at 21 percent.
The 2023 survey found that 64 percent of 2,000 university students in Pakistan relied mainly on social media for their news.
Television, the main source for 21 percent of students, came second.
questions.e: To show how far ahead social media was, it must be compared with the runner-up, television, as this choice does. The choice giving 64 percent of 2,000 students reports social media's share without any comparison.

questions.s:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Karakoram Highway links Pakistan with China.
• It is about 1,300 kilometres long.
• It passes through the Hunza valley.
• At the Khunjerab Pass it reaches a height of about 4,700 metres.

The student wants to emphasize how high the Karakoram Highway climbs. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
o: On its way to China, the Karakoram Highway passes through the Hunza valley.
The Karakoram Highway connects Pakistan and China across the mountains.
At the Khunjerab Pass, the Karakoram Highway climbs to about 4,700 metres.
The Karakoram Highway, about 1,300 kilometres long, links Pakistan with China.
questions.e: Height is the goal, and only this choice gives the road's highest point. The choice with 1,300 kilometres is tempting because it gives a large figure, but that figure is length, not height.

questions.s:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Chemist Amna Siddiqui developed a paper strip that tests drinking water for arsenic.
• The strip changes colour within ten minutes if arsenic levels are unsafe.
• Each strip costs less than Rs 20.
• Laboratory tests for arsenic can take several days and cost thousands of rupees.

The student wants to compare Siddiqui's strip with laboratory tests in terms of speed and cost. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
o: Laboratory tests for arsenic in drinking water can take several days and cost thousands of rupees.
Each of the arsenic-testing strips developed by the chemist Amna Siddiqui costs less than Rs 20.
Siddiqui's strip gives a result in ten minutes for under Rs 20, whereas laboratory tests can take days and cost thousands of rupees.
Amna Siddiqui's paper strip changes colour within ten minutes if a water sample contains unsafe levels of arsenic.
questions.e: A comparison needs both the strip and the laboratory test, on both speed and cost, and only this choice gives all four facts. Each other choice describes only one side.

questions.s:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Crop rotation is the practice of growing different crops on the same land in successive seasons.
• Legumes such as lentils and chickpeas add nitrogen to the soil.
• Many farmers in Punjab grow wheat in winter and cotton or rice in summer.
• Rotation can also break the life cycles of pests.

The student wants to explain how crop rotation can benefit the soil. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
o: Rotating crops from one season to the next can also help farmers by breaking the life cycles of the pests that attack their fields.
Crop rotation means growing different crops on the same land in successive seasons.
Many farmers in Punjab grow wheat in winter and cotton or rice in summer.
Including legumes such as lentils or chickpeas in a rotation enriches the soil, because these crops add nitrogen to it.
questions.e: Only this choice links rotation to a benefit for the soil: legumes add nitrogen. Breaking pest life cycles is a real benefit, but it is not a benefit to the soil.

questions.s:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• A 2018 study in Islamabad found that children who read for pleasure scored higher on vocabulary tests.
• The Islamabad study surveyed 600 children aged 8–11.
• A 2020 study in Dhaka found the same link among teenagers.
• The Dhaka study surveyed 900 teenagers aged 13–16.

The student wants to emphasize that the two studies reached a similar conclusion despite studying different age groups. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
o: Though one studied children aged 8–11 and the other teenagers aged 13–16, both studies linked reading for pleasure with stronger vocabulary.
The Islamabad study surveyed 600 children aged 8–11, while the Dhaka study surveyed 900 teenagers aged 13–16.
A 2018 study in Islamabad found that children who read for pleasure scored higher on vocabulary tests.
Both the Islamabad study and the Dhaka study surveyed hundreds of young people about their reading.
questions.e: The goal has two parts, the shared conclusion and the different age groups, and only this choice gives both. The choice comparing 600 children with 900 teenagers shows the difference but not the shared finding.

questions.s:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The markhor is a wild goat found in the mountains of northern Pakistan.
• It is Pakistan's national animal.
• Males have long, corkscrew-shaped horns.
• It feeds on grasses in summer and on leaves and twigs in winter.

The student wants to describe the markhor's diet. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
o: The markhor lives in the mountains of northern Pakistan.
Male markhor have long horns shaped like corkscrews.
The markhor eats grasses in summer and leaves and twigs in winter.
Pakistan's national animal, the markhor, is a wild goat of the northern mountains.
questions.e: A diet is what an animal eats, which only this choice describes. The other choices give the markhor's status, appearance and habitat.

questions.s:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• In 1990, a village in Swat had one primary school, which only boys attended.
• Today the village has four schools, two of them for girls.
• Literacy among women in the village has risen from about 10 percent to about 55 percent.
• Most of the new schools were built by a community trust.

The student wants to emphasize how much women's literacy in the village has changed. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
o: In 1990, this village in Swat had only a single primary school, which was attended only by boys.
The village now has four schools, two of which are for girls.
Literacy among the village's women has risen from about 10 percent to about 55 percent.
Most of the village's new schools were built by a community trust.
questions.e: Only this choice gives the before-and-after literacy figures for women. The choice about four schools shows a change in schooling, but it says nothing about literacy.

questions.s:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• A qanat is an underground channel that carries water from an aquifer to fields or villages.
• Qanats slope gently downhill, so water flows through them by gravity without pumps.
• Vertical shafts along the route let workers dig and clean the channel.
• In Balochistan, where they are called karez, qanats are still in use.

The student wants to explain how a qanat moves water without pumps. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
o: Vertical shafts along a qanat's route allow workers to dig and clean the underground channel.
Known in Balochistan as karez, qanats are still in use in parts of that province.
A qanat is an underground channel that brings water from an aquifer to fields.
Because a qanat slopes gently downhill, water flows through it by gravity alone.
questions.e: The gentle slope and gravity explain the movement of water, which is the goal. The choice about vertical shafts explains how a qanat is built and maintained, not how water moves through it.

questions.s:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Sleep researchers have long known that sleep helps people remember facts.
• In 2022, Hamza Rauf tested whether sleep also helps people learn physical skills.
• Participants practised a piano melody and then either slept or stayed awake for eight hours.
• Those who slept then played the melody with 20 percent fewer errors.

The student wants to present Rauf's findings to an audience already familiar with the link between sleep and memory for facts. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
o: In Rauf's 2022 study, participants practised a piano melody and then either slept or stayed awake for eight hours before playing it again.
Rauf found that sleep may help with physical skills too: people who slept after practising a melody made 20 percent fewer errors.
In 2022, Hamza Rauf studied whether sleep helps people learn physical skills.
Sleep researchers have long known that a night's sleep helps people remember facts.
questions.e: This audience already knows about sleep and facts, so the useful new point is Rauf's result about physical skills, which this choice gives. The choice about facts repeats what the audience knows, and the other two give Rauf's question and method but not his findings.

questions.s:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Badshahi Mosque in Lahore was built under the emperor Aurangzeb.
• It was completed in 1673.
• Its courtyard can hold about 100,000 worshippers.
• It is built of red sandstone decorated with marble.

The student wants to emphasize the capacity of the Badshahi Mosque. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
o: Completed in 1673, the Badshahi Mosque was built under the emperor Aurangzeb.
The courtyard of Lahore's Badshahi Mosque can hold about 100,000 worshippers.
The Badshahi Mosque is made of red sandstone decorated with marble.
The emperor Aurangzeb ordered the building of the Badshahi Mosque in Lahore.
questions.e: Capacity means how many people a place can hold, which only this choice states. The other choices give the mosque's history and materials.

questions.s:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• A city council is considering two ways to reduce traffic in its old quarter.
• Plan A would close the main street to cars at weekends.
• Plan B would charge drivers Rs 200 to enter the old quarter on weekdays.
• Plan A would cost little to put in place.
• Plan B would raise money that could be spent on buses.

The student wants to emphasize an advantage of Plan B. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
o: Plan A, which would close the main street to cars at weekends, would cost very little to put in place.
Plan B, a Rs 200 weekday entry charge, would raise money that could be spent on buses.
Under Plan B, drivers would pay Rs 200 to enter the old quarter on weekdays.
The council is weighing two plans for reducing traffic in the city's old quarter.
questions.e: Raising money for buses is an advantage of Plan B, and this choice states it. The choice about low cost gives an advantage, but of Plan A, and the choice about Rs 200 describes Plan B without saying what is good about it.

questions.s:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Novelist Usman Ghani writes long, slow-moving novels with many characters.
• Short-story writer Farah Naz writes brief, fast-paced stories with one or two characters.
• Both writers set their work in Karachi.
• Ghani writes in Urdu; Naz writes in English.

The student wants to emphasize a difference in the length and pace of the two writers' work. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
o: Ghani's novels are long and slow-moving, whereas Naz's stories are brief and fast-paced.
Although both set their work in Karachi, Ghani writes his fiction in Urdu, while Naz writes hers in English.
Both Usman Ghani and Farah Naz set their fiction in the city of Karachi.
Usman Ghani writes long, slow-moving novels that feature many characters.
questions.e: Only this choice contrasts the two writers on length and pace. The choice about Urdu and English is a difference too, but of language, and the choice about Ghani describes only one writer.

questions.s:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Some plants protect themselves by forming partnerships with ants.
• The bullhorn acacia of Central America gives ants shelter in its hollow thorns and food in the form of sugary nectar.
• In return, the ants attack insects and animals that try to eat the tree's leaves.
• The ants also cut away vines that grow on the tree.

The student wants to present the bullhorn acacia as an example that illustrates a general point. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
o: The bullhorn acacia gives ants shelter in its hollow thorns and food in the form of sugary nectar.
The ants that live on the bullhorn acacia cut away vines that grow on the tree.
Some plants protect themselves by forming partnerships with ants.
Some plants rely on ants for protection; for example, the bullhorn acacia feeds and shelters ants that attack its leaf-eaters.
questions.e: Only this choice states the general point and then presents the acacia as an example of it. The choice about the general point alone gives no example, and the other two describe the acacia without connecting it to any wider claim.

questions.s:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Hira Saleem is a software developer in Peshawar.
• In 2021 she created Rasta, an app that maps wheelchair-accessible shops, offices and mosques.
• Users can add places and rate how easy they are to enter.
• Saleem built the app after her father began using a wheelchair.
• The app now lists more than 3,000 places.

The student wants to explain why Saleem created Rasta. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
o: Hira Saleem's app Rasta maps shops, offices and mosques that wheelchair users can enter.
Saleem created Rasta after her father began using a wheelchair.
Rasta, an app made by Hira Saleem in 2021, now lists more than 3,000 places.
On Rasta, users can add places and rate how easy they are to enter.
questions.e: The reason for the app is her father's need, which only this choice gives. The other choices describe what the app does or how large it has grown.

questions.s:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Most spiders use their webs to catch prey.
• The diving bell spider lives almost entirely underwater.
• It uses silk to hold a bubble of air, in which it lives and eats.
• It is found in ponds and slow streams in Europe and Asia.

The student wants to emphasize what makes the diving bell spider unusual. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
o: The diving bell spider is found in ponds and slow-moving streams across Europe and Asia.
Unlike most spiders, the diving bell spider lives underwater, in an air bubble that it holds in place with silk.
The diving bell spider, like most other spiders, makes silk.
Most spiders, including many of the species found in Europe and Asia, use the webs they spin to catch their prey.
questions.e: Only this choice contrasts the spider's underwater bubble with what most spiders do. The choice about making silk stresses what it shares with other spiders, the opposite of the goal.

questions.s:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• A 2024 trial tested a new malaria vaccine on 1,500 children in two districts.
• The vaccine reduced malaria cases by 60 percent over one year.
• The trial did not measure whether protection lasts beyond one year.
• The researchers plan a longer follow-up study.

The student wants to present the trial's main result while acknowledging a limitation of the trial. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
o: The vaccine cut malaria cases by 60 percent over a year, though the trial did not show whether protection lasts longer.
Because the trial did not measure protection beyond one year, the researchers are planning a longer follow-up study.
The researchers who tested a new malaria vaccine on 1,500 children are planning a follow-up study.
In a 2024 trial involving 1,500 children in two districts, a new malaria vaccine reduced cases by 60 percent over one year.
questions.e: Only this choice gives both the result and the limitation. The choice with 1,500 children reports the result without any limitation, and the choice about the follow-up study gives the limitation without the result.

questions.s:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Ajrak is a traditional cloth from Sindh.
• It is usually dyed deep red and indigo blue.
• Printers use carved wooden blocks to stamp patterns onto the cloth.
• Ajrak is often given to guests as a sign of respect.

The student wants to describe how ajrak patterns are made. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
o: Ajrak is a traditional cloth that comes from the province of Sindh.
Ajrak, a traditional cloth from Sindh, is often given to guests as a sign of respect.
Ajrak is usually dyed in deep red and indigo blue.
Ajrak patterns are stamped onto the cloth with carved wooden blocks.
questions.e: Only this choice explains the making of the patterns: stamping with carved blocks. The choice about red and blue describes the colours, not how the patterns are made.

questions.s:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• In 2010, unusually heavy monsoon rains fell over northern Pakistan.
• The Indus and its tributaries overflowed.
• About one-fifth of the country's land area was flooded.
• Millions of people were forced from their homes.

The student wants to emphasize the cause of the 2010 floods. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
o: The 2010 floods began when unusually heavy monsoon rains made the Indus and its tributaries overflow.
The floods of 2010, which forced millions of people from their homes, covered about one-fifth of Pakistan's total land area.
In 2010, floods covered about one-fifth of Pakistan's land area.
Millions of people in Pakistan were forced from their homes by the floods of 2010.
questions.e: The heavy rains that made the rivers overflow are the cause, and only this choice names them. The other choices describe the floods' size and effects.

questions.s:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Urdu is usually written in the Nastaliq style of a script based on the Persian alphabet.
• Hindi is written in the Devanagari script.
• Speakers of everyday spoken Urdu and Hindi can largely understand each other.
• Formal Urdu borrows more words from Persian and Arabic; formal Hindi borrows more from Sanskrit.

The student wants to emphasize a similarity between Urdu and Hindi. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
o: Speakers of everyday Urdu and Hindi can largely understand each other.
Urdu is usually written in a Persian-based script, while Hindi is written in Devanagari.
Formal Hindi takes much of its vocabulary from Sanskrit.
Formal Urdu borrows more words from Persian and Arabic than formal Hindi does.
questions.e: Mutual understanding of the spoken languages is a similarity, and only this choice states it. The choices about scripts and vocabulary point to differences.

questions.s:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Researchers measured noise levels in 50 streets in Lahore.
• Busy main roads averaged 78 decibels.
• Residential lanes averaged 62 decibels.
• Some narrow market lanes averaged 81 decibels, louder than the main roads.
• Most of the noise in the market lanes came from loudspeakers and generators.

The student wants to emphasize the most surprising finding of the study. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
o: Most of the noise in the market lanes came from loudspeakers and generators.
Busy main roads in Lahore averaged 78 decibels, compared with 62 decibels for residential lanes.
Some narrow market lanes, at an average of 81 decibels, were even louder than Lahore's busy main roads.
The researchers measured noise in 50 streets in Lahore, from main roads to residential lanes.
questions.e: One would expect main roads to be the loudest, so narrow lanes being louder is the surprise, and this choice presents it. The choice comparing main roads with residential lanes gives an expected result.

questions.s:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Rosetta Stone was found in Egypt in 1799.
• It carries the same text in three scripts: hieroglyphic, Demotic and ancient Greek.
• Scholars could already read ancient Greek.
• The stone helped Jean-François Champollion decipher hieroglyphs in 1822.

The student wants to explain why the Rosetta Stone was important for understanding hieroglyphs. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
o: Jean-François Champollion deciphered Egyptian hieroglyphs in 1822.
The Rosetta Stone carries the same text in three different scripts, one of them ancient Greek.
Found in Egypt in 1799, the Rosetta Stone carries one text written in three scripts: hieroglyphic, Demotic and ancient Greek.
Because the stone repeats one text in Greek, which scholars could read, it helped Champollion decipher hieroglyphs.
questions.e: The stone mattered because a readable Greek version unlocked the same text in hieroglyphs, and only this choice explains that link. The choice about three scripts describes the stone but does not say why scholars being able to read Greek made it useful.

questions.s:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Faisal Mosque is in Islamabad.
• It was designed by the Turkish architect Vedat Dalokay.
• Its shape was inspired by a Bedouin tent.
• It was completed in 1986.

The student wants to emphasize what inspired the design of the Faisal Mosque. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
o: Vedat Dalokay, an architect from Turkey, designed a mosque that was completed in 1986.
The shape of Islamabad's Faisal Mosque was inspired by a Bedouin tent.
The Faisal Mosque in Islamabad was designed by the Turkish architect Vedat Dalokay.
Completed in 1986, the Faisal Mosque stands in Islamabad.
questions.e: The Bedouin tent is the inspiration, and only this choice mentions it. The choices about Dalokay name the designer but not what inspired the design.

questions.s:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Honey can last for a very long time without spoiling.
• It contains very little water.
• It is slightly acidic.
• These conditions make it hard for bacteria to grow.

The student wants to explain why honey resists spoiling. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
o: Bacteria find it hard to grow in some foods, and honey can last a long time.
Honey resists spoiling because its low water content and slight acidity make it hard for bacteria to grow.
Honey can last for a very long time without spoiling.
Honey is a food that contains very little water and is slightly acidic.
questions.e: An explanation must connect honey's properties to the result, as this choice does with "because". The choice about water and acidity lists the properties but never says what they do.

questions.s:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Saima Khan is a marathon runner from Quetta.
• She began running at the age of 30.
• In 2023 she finished the Lahore Marathon in 3 hours 5 minutes.
• She now coaches a running club for women.

The student wants to emphasize what Khan achieved in 2023. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
o: Saima Khan, a marathon runner from Quetta, did not begin running until she was 30.
Saima Khan now coaches a running club for women in addition to running marathons.
In 2023, Saima Khan finished the Lahore Marathon in 3 hours 5 minutes.
Saima Khan is a runner from Quetta who coaches a women's running club.
questions.e: Only this choice reports the 2023 marathon time. The other choices describe Khan's background and coaching, not her 2023 result.

questions.s:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Penguins are birds that cannot fly.
• Their wings have evolved into stiff flippers.
• They use their flippers to "fly" through water.
• Emperor penguins can dive deeper than 500 metres.

The student wants to explain how penguins use their wings. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
o: Penguins are birds, but they cannot fly.
Unlike most birds, penguins are unable to fly through the air at all.
Penguins use their stiff, flipper-like wings to push themselves through water.
Emperor penguins can dive to depths of more than 500 metres.
questions.e: This choice says what penguins do with their wings: swim. The choice about not flying says what the wings cannot do, not how they are used.

questions.s:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Thar Desert lies along the border between Pakistan and India.
• It covers about 200,000 square kilometres.
• Although it is very dry, it is one of the most densely populated deserts in the world.
• Many of its people herd camels, goats and sheep.

The student wants to emphasize something unusual about the Thar Desert's population. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
o: Many of the people who live in the Thar Desert herd camels, goats and sheep.
Although it is dry, the Thar is one of the world's most densely populated deserts.
The Thar Desert lies along the border between Pakistan and India.
The Thar Desert, which covers about 200,000 square kilometres, lies on the Pakistan–India border.
questions.e: A dense population is unusual for a desert, and only this choice points this out. Herding is a fact about the people, but nothing in the notes says it is unusual.

questions.s:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• In 2019, a school in Gujranwala replaced its paper textbooks with tablets.
• Teachers reported that students were more engaged in lessons.
• Test scores did not change significantly.
• The tablets cost the school Rs 3 million.

The student wants to present a balanced view of the results of the switch to tablets. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
o: Teachers said students were more engaged after the switch, but test scores did not change significantly.
The school spent Rs 3 million on tablets, and its students' test scores did not change significantly.
After a Gujranwala school replaced paper textbooks with tablets in 2019, teachers reported that students were more engaged in lessons.
In 2019, a school in Gujranwala replaced its paper textbooks with tablets that cost Rs 3 million.
questions.e: A balanced view gives a positive and a less positive result, as this choice does. The choice about engagement gives only the good news, and the choice about Rs 3 million gives only the disappointing one.

questions.s:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Photosynthesis takes place in a plant's chloroplasts.
• Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll, a pigment.
• Chlorophyll absorbs mainly red and blue light.
• It reflects green light, which is why leaves look green.

The student wants to explain why leaves look green. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
o: Chlorophyll is a pigment that absorbs mainly red and blue light.
Photosynthesis takes place inside a plant's chloroplasts, which contain chlorophyll, a pigment that absorbs light.
Leaves look green because their chlorophyll reflects green light while absorbing mainly red and blue light.
Plants carry out photosynthesis in parts of their cells called chloroplasts.
questions.e: The green colour comes from the light chlorophyll reflects, and only this choice says so. The choice about red and blue light tells what chlorophyll absorbs, which alone does not explain why leaves look green.

questions.s:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The cousins Ali and Danish both started small businesses in 2022.
• Ali opened a juice stall in Hyderabad.
• Danish started an online tutoring service.
• Ali needed Rs 150,000 to start his stall; Danish needed only a laptop he already owned.

The student wants to emphasize a difference in what the two businesses cost to start. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
o: Ali needed Rs 150,000 to start his juice stall; Danish needed only a laptop he already owned.
Ali's business was a juice stall in the city of Hyderabad, while his cousin Danish's business was an online tutoring service.
Danish's online tutoring service needed only a laptop that he already owned.
In 2022, the cousins Ali and Danish each started a small business.
questions.e: Only this choice sets the two start-up costs side by side. The choice about the juice stall and the tutoring service shows a difference, but in the type of business, not its cost.

questions.s:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Bulleh Shah was a Sufi poet who lived in Punjab in the 18th century.
• He wrote in Punjabi.
• His poems criticise religious hypocrisy.
• His verses are still sung today by qawwals and folk singers.

The student wants to emphasize Bulleh Shah's lasting popularity. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
o: Bulleh Shah's verses, written in the 18th century, are still sung today by qawwals and folk singers.
Bulleh Shah was a Sufi poet who wrote in the Punjabi language.
In his poems, Bulleh Shah criticised religious hypocrisy.
Bulleh Shah, who lived in Punjab in the 18th century, was a Sufi poet whose poems criticise religious hypocrisy.
questions.e: Verses still sung centuries later show lasting popularity, and only this choice mentions this. The other choices describe who he was and what he wrote about.

questions.s:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Coral reefs cover less than 1 percent of the ocean floor.
• They support about a quarter of all known marine species.
• Rising sea temperatures cause corals to expel the algae that live in them, a process called bleaching.
• Bleached corals can die if high temperatures continue.

The student wants to emphasize the importance of coral reefs to marine life. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
o: Coral reefs cover less than 1 percent of the ocean floor.
Bleached corals can die if high sea temperatures continue for too long.
Though they cover less than 1 percent of the ocean floor, coral reefs support about a quarter of all known marine species.
When sea temperatures rise, corals expel the algae that live in them, a process known as bleaching.
questions.e: Supporting a quarter of marine species shows the reefs' importance, made more striking by their small area. The choice with less than 1 percent alone stresses how small reefs are, not how important.

questions.s:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• In 2022, a bakery chain in Karachi switched from plastic to paper bags.
• In the first month, customer complaints about the bags rose, mostly because the bags tore.
• The chain then switched to a thicker paper.
• By the third month, complaints had fallen back to their usual level.

The student wants to describe the sequence of events that followed the switch to paper bags. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
o: In 2022, a bakery chain in Karachi decided to stop using plastic bags and switched to paper bags instead.
The bakery chain's switch to thicker paper brought complaints back to their usual level.
Customers complained that the bakery chain's new paper bags tore easily.
After the switch, complaints about tearing rose; the chain then used thicker paper, and complaints fell back by the third month.
questions.e: Only this choice follows the events in order: complaints, thicker paper, recovery. Each other choice gives just one stage of the story.

questions.s:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Nastaliq is a style of Perso-Arabic calligraphy.
• It developed in Iran in the 14th and 15th centuries.
• Its letters slope downward from right to left.
• Most Urdu books and newspapers are printed in Nastaliq.

The student wants to introduce Nastaliq to an audience unfamiliar with it and explain its importance for Urdu. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
o: Nastaliq is a style of calligraphy whose letters slope downward from right to left.
The letters of Nastaliq slope downward from right to left.
Nastaliq developed in Iran during the 14th and 15th centuries.
Nastaliq, a style of Perso-Arabic calligraphy, is used for most printed Urdu books and newspapers.
questions.e: This choice tells an unfamiliar reader what Nastaliq is and why it matters for Urdu. The choice about sloping letters defines the style but says nothing about Urdu.

questions.s:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Psychologist Maryam Akhtar studied how people estimate time.
• Participants waited in a room for exactly five minutes.
• Those who had nothing to do estimated that they had waited about eight minutes.
• Those who were given a puzzle estimated about four minutes.
• Akhtar concluded that boredom makes time feel longer.

The student wants to present Akhtar's conclusion along with the evidence for it. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
o: Boredom makes time feel longer, Akhtar concluded: idle participants judged a five-minute wait as eight minutes, puzzle-solvers as four.
In Akhtar's study of time estimation, participants waited in a room for exactly five minutes and then estimated how long they believed they had waited.
From her study of how people estimate time, Akhtar concluded that boredom makes time feel longer.
Participants in Akhtar's study who were given a puzzle estimated that their five-minute wait had lasted only about four minutes.
questions.e: The goal needs both the conclusion and the evidence, and only this choice gives both. The choice about the puzzle gives part of the evidence without the conclusion, and the choice about boredom gives the conclusion without the evidence.

questions.s:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Silk Road was a network of trade routes linking China with the Mediterranean.
• Merchants traded silk, spices, paper and glass.
• Ideas and religions, including Buddhism, also spread along the routes.
